body:
LIVE with Sen. Chris Van Hollen: The Fight for New Senate Leadership!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/8763?t=1011&akid=11636%2E5885482%2Etm5teR ]Graphic with a picture of Van Hollen reading: LEADERSHIP FOR CHANGE
TOWN HALL WITH SEN. CHRIS VAN HOLLEN. NOV. 23 @ 8:30p ET / 5:30 PT

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/8763?t=1012&akid=11636%2E5885482%2Etm5teR ]Join Zoom@ 8:30pm ET

Dear Peter Willis,

LIVE Leadership for Change Town Hall with Sen. Chris Van Hollen!

Our Revolution is proud to endorse Sen. Chris Van Hollen for Senate
Majority Leader. And we’re mobilizing our grassroots movement to make sure
senators hear the call for change.

Why Van Hollen? Because he’s shown he’s willing to take on powerful
interests — including those within his own party.

He’s fighting to crack down on corruption and the influence of federal
contractors who bankroll political campaigns. He’s challenging the
expansion of U.S.-Israel military integration and pushing to strip Section
219 from the National Defense Authorization Act.

And he’s a longtime champion of Medicare for All.

That’s the kind of leadership this moment demands. Someone willing to
stand up to corporate power, challenge the political establishment, and
fight for the issues that matter most to working people: affordable
healthcare, getting big money out of politics, ending endless wars, and
stopping more bombs for Israel.

In our new survey, nearly 75% of you told us you want to see a new Senate
Majority Leader. Well, this is our chance.

At Monday’s LIVE town hall, we’ll hear directly from Sen. Van Hollen about
what’s at stake in the Senate leadership fight, his vision for the new
Democratic majority, and how our grassroots movement can help shape what
comes next.

We’ll also be joined by leaders from MoveOn, the International Association
of Machinists union, Sunrise Movement, Friends of the Earth Action, and
Progressive Maryland as we build momentum for a new era of politics in
America.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/8763?t=1013&akid=11636%2E5885482%2Etm5teR ]Click Here to Join the Zoom - 8:30pm ET start time

Our movement fought hard to win this majority. Now we have to make it
deliver.

The voters sent a clear message on Election Day: We’re ready for
change.And that means new leadership willing to take on Trump, the
billionaires, and the corporate interests standing in the way of progress.

Let’s turn our Progressive Earthquake into a new era of leadership in
Washington.

When we organize, we win.

Our Revolution

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: You get a 10-minute head start. Now what?
body:
Plus: Trump is frustrated with JD Vance, and it is getting worse | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/pNkltASL9u4?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | | It has been a week! Microsoft went down. Every flight in the country got grounded. Four big banks had problems, United’s computers quit, the NSA’s internal network went dark, and then Apple. It has felt like three months, and we haven’t even mentioned the stock market yet.
Nobody has shown that any of it is connected. [But Costco is selling out of generators, and we spent a good part of this show figuring out how much getting ready is enough. ](https://us.list-manage.com/18Czr5GBGwC?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)Then there’s Trump and JD Vance, which is getting ugly faster than we thought it would.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/15svuGxZxAM?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | 🔦 **GENERATORS ARE SELLING OUT AT COSTCO, AND WE HAD TO FIGURE OUT WHERE OUR LINE IS**
As of last Sunday, 21 of the 26 big generators on Costco’s website were gone, including one that costs $7,000. Do we all need one of those?
Our number one worry is how to reach our daughter at college if the phones don’t work. So we stocked up on water, got a couple weeks of food together, and did not buy out the toilet paper aisle. We’re not bunker people, and nobody in this house is canning.
But what would you do with a 10-minute head start before everything shuts off? Stay in the city or get out?

🤖 **ONE STORY SAYS THE OUTAGES COULD ACTUALLY BE GOOD NEWS**
Josh Hawley says if this is all a coincidence, it’s the greatest coincidence in the history of the world. That’s what everybody is thinking.
But the New York Post has a different take. Companies are using AI to hunt for holes in their own software, AI is finding a whole lot more than anybody expected, and the rush to fix them is what’s knocking things offline. We’re not telling you that’s the answer. It’s the first explanation that sounded plausible to both of us.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/IyVuqRMU138?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| | 🇺🇸 **TRUMP IS FRUSTRATED WITH JD VANCE, AND IT’S GOING TO GET WORSE**
After the midterms, JD Vance said the Iran war is why Republicans lost. Trump agreed with him at first. Now he’s telling people Vance should have added that going in was the right call.
Here’s the problem. JD doesn’t believe that, and he never has. So he’s got nowhere to go. And when somebody had to stand up this week and tell the country not to be scared about the outages, it wasn’t the vice president. It was Marco Rubio. Again.
There’s a real chance JD Vance doesn’t run for president at all.

🎬 **ROB LOWE SAYS HOLLYWOOD BLACKLISTED HIS MOVIE BECAUSE BEN SHAPIRO WROTE IT**
Rob Lowe made a movie with Nick Nolte and James Franco about a prisoner in Stalin’s Moscow. He says every film festival turned it down, and the only reason is who wrote the script.
He sounds a little shocked. Dude, welcome to the party.

Nobody has shown that any of it is connected. there’s Trump and JD Vance, which is getting ugly faster than we thought it would. | | 🔦 GENERATORS ARE SELLING OUT AT COSTCO, AND WE HAD TO FIGURE OUT WHERE OUR LINE IS As of last Sunday, 21 of the 26 big generators on Costco’s website were gone, including one that costs $7,000. Do we all need one of those? Our number one worry is how to reach our daughter at college if the phones don’t work. So we stocked up on water, got a couple weeks of food together, and did not buy out the toilet paper aisle. We’re not bunker people, and nobody in this house is canning. But what would you do with a 10-minute head start before everything shuts off? Stay in the city or get out? 🤖 ONE STORY SAYS THE OUTAGES COULD ACTUALLY BE GOOD NEWS Josh Hawley says if this is all a coincidence, it’s the greatest coincidence in the history of the world. That’s what everybody is thinking. But the New York Post has a different take. Companies are using AI to hunt for holes in their own software, AI is finding a whole lot more than anybody expected, and the rush to fix them is what’s knocking things offline. We’re not telling you that’s the answer. It’s the first explanation that sounded plausible to both of us. | | | 🇺🇸 TRUMP IS FRUSTRATED WITH JD VANCE, AND IT’S GOING TO GET WORSE After the midterms, JD Vance said the Iran war is why Republicans lost. Trump agreed with him at first. Now he’s telling people Vance should have added that going in was the right call. Here’s the problem. JD doesn’t believe that, and he never has. So he’s got nowhere to go. And when somebody had to stand up this week and tell the country not to be scared about the outages, it wasn’t the vice president. It was Marco Rubio. Again. There’s a real chance JD Vance doesn’t run for president at all. 🎬 ROB LOWE SAYS HOLLYWOOD BLACKLISTED HIS MOVIE BECAUSE BEN SHAPIRO WROTE IT Rob Lowe made a movie with Nick Nolte and James Franco about a prisoner in Stalin’s Moscow. He says every film festival turned it down, and the only reason is who wrote the script. He sounds a little shocked. Dude, welcome to the party. | | | PLUS: The new 2028 poll and the Democrat sitting on top of it, the guy who now runs CBS and CNN on why nobody trusts the news, and the Thanksgiving movies we already have tickets for. | | | ✅ LIKE on ✅ hit the bell ✅ FORWARD to anyone who needs to catch up on the news ✅ at NoDoubtAboutItPodcast.com | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | © 2026 Choose Adventure Media. After a nationwide FAA ground stop disrupted flights, I am demanding answers.
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143946014/661947174/-201694504?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0N2I2MGMzMC1iM2U3LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wy1lEV6xMH6ePn1sistZ-uZZPp5IRoKL914MtrfusRg=&emci=6ae67a6e-7fe7-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=47b60c30-b3e7-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=9494239)

| | On November 13, a failure in the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) communications network prompted a nationwide ground stop, disrupting air travel and leaving thousands of travelers stranded. More than 12,000 flights were canceled nationwide. At Paine Field in Everett, 17 flights were canceled Friday, followed by eight more on Saturday. And when President Trump was asked about the disruption, his response was simple: **"I don't take any responsibility."** That is unacceptable. **The flying public deserves a safe, reliable aviation system. When that system fails, the American people deserve answers.** As the top Democrat on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, I am demanding accountability from the Trump administration. Congress approved $12.5 billion last year to make necessary upgrades to our air traffic control system. Fifteen months later, the administration has obligated just $4.3 billion and spent only $1 billion, leaving $11 billion unspent. On November 12, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy requested another $30.1 billion from Congress. clean_body: After a nationwide FAA ground stop disrupted flights, I am demanding answers. | | | | On November 13, a failure in the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) communications network prompted a nationwide ground stop, disrupting air travel and leaving thousands of travelers stranded. More than 12,000 flights were canceled nationwide. At Paine Field in Everett, 17 flights were canceled Friday, followed by eight more on Saturday. And when President Trump was asked about the disruption, his response was simple: "I don't take any responsibility." That is unacceptable. The flying public deserves a safe, reliable aviation system. When that system fails, the American people deserve answers. As the top Democrat on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, I am demanding accountability from the Trump administration. Congress approved $12.5 billion last year to make necessary upgrades to our air traffic control system. Fifteen months later, the administration has obligated just $4.3 billion and spent only $1 billion, leaving $11 billion unspent. On November 12, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy requested another $30.1 billion from Congress. Just one day later, following the nationwide ground stop, that request jumped to $50 billion. Before asking taxpayers for billions more, the Trump administration needs to explain why its funding request increased by $20 billion overnight, how it is spending the funding Congress has already approved, and what it is doing to prevent another nationwide disruption. Alongside Representative André Carson, the top Democrat on the Aviation Subcommittee, I am demanding answers from the FAA and Department of Transportation about the failures that led to the ground stop, the status of aviation safety upgrades, and the administration's plans for the funding Congress has already provided. We are preparing to make oversight of the administration's air traffic control modernization efforts a top priority in the next Congress to make sure this chaos does not happen again. With the busy holiday travel season approaching, Americans need confidence that our aviation system is safe and reliable. I will continue pushing for the investments needed to modernize our air traffic control system, demand transparency about how taxpayer dollars are spent, and hold this administration accountable. Thanksgiving.

occasions. I’m talking about my great-grandmother's perfect scalloped
oysters.

still have it:

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261124-1-ak.AiKyQn&refcode=em20261124-3921&t=1004&akid=3921%2E251025%2EQ2yAqs ]Perfect Scalloped Oysters

One bite and you’ll understand why it’s lasted four generations. It’s too
good to keep to ourselves.

So, here’s the deal: [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261124-1-ak.AiKyQn&amount=10&refcode=em20261124-3921-3921&t=1005&akid=3921%2E251025%2EQ2yAqs ]Donate any amount to fuel our movement, and we’ll

earlier this month was only step one.

The lobbyists and megadonors who spent against us aren’t going anywhere.
You can bet that come January, their top priority will be stopping us from
finally getting money out of politics, putting money in your pockets, and
passing Medicare for All.

Grassroots support is how we keep the pressure on. Your support gives us

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261124-1-ak.AiKyQn&amount=10&refcode=em20261124-3921&t=1025&akid=3921%2E251025%2EQ2yAqs ]If you’re able to, chip in any amount to help me continue fighting. In

Abdul

My grandparents, Jan and Judy, still have it: [ ]Perfect Scalloped Oysters One bite and you’ll understand why it’s lasted four generations. It’s too good to keep to ourselves. So, here’s the deal: [ ]Donate any amount to fuel our movement, and we’ll send you the recipe as thanks. [ ]Donate $10 ›› I know, the election’s over and I’m still in your inbox. But winning earlier this month was only step one. The lobbyists and megadonors who spent against us aren’t going anywhere. You can bet that come January, their top priority will be stopping us from finally getting money out of politics, putting money in your pockets, and passing Medicare for All. Grassroots support is how we keep the pressure on. Your support gives us the resources to build the strongest possible office as we prepare for the new year. [ ]If you’re able to, chip in any amount to help me continue fighting. In return, we’ll send you our family recipe just in time for Thanksgiving. Yours in the work, Abdul

name: Ragen Davey
subject: Protect Polar Bears: Speak up to defend vulnerable wildlife in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge!
body:
The Department of the Interior could harm polar bears and cubs with seismic exploration. Send a message today!

The Department of the Interior could harm polar bears and cubs with seismic exploration. Send a message today!
                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/6352307/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/6352308/38SyG9Xl)

Act Today: Protect Polar Bear Mothers and Cubs! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6352309/38SyG9Xl)

Defender,

Polar bear cubs could be harmed and killed in their dens – and the agency responsible plans to move ahead anyway.

The Department of the Interior has proposed allowing seismic exploration for oil and gas on the Coastal Plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. That Coastal Plain is the heart of the refuge and is home to critical denning habitat for vulnerable polar bears.

Speak Up Today: Urge the Interior to protect polar bears from the harms of seismic exploration in the Arctic Refuge! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6352310/38SyG9Xl)

The proposed project could bring nearly 360 workers and a fleet of massive seismic vehicles, including “thumper trucks” that generate up to 64,000 pounds of force as they send powerful vibrations into the fragile Arctic tundra.

That seismic activity ripples through the earth, panicking polar bear mothers — driving them out of their dens and away from their young.

The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service’s own estimates show a high possibility of this outcome. But under the current proposal, seismic activity could be unleashed on the Refuge despite the risks.

The Department of the Interior is taking public comments on this plan now. We must raise our voices before the deadline and demand protections that keep polar bears and their cubs safe!

Submit your public comment urging the Department of the Interior to safeguard polar bears from the worst effects of seismic exploration! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6352311/38SyG9Xl)

Thank you for speaking up in defense of polar bears and all Arctic wildlife.

Sincerely,

Ragen Davey

Representative, Alaska

Defenders of Wildlife

(http://www.facebook.com/DefendersofWildlife) (http://twitter.com/defenders) (https://www.instagram.com/defendersofwildlife/?hl=en) (http://www.youtube.com/defendersofwildlife) (https://www.tiktok.com/@defendersofwildlife)

Defenders of Wildlife 1130 17th Street NW • Washington, DC 20036 defenders.org (https://defenders.org)

Get Dark and Corporate Money Out of the 2028 Democratic Primaries!

Peter Willis,

Our next Democratic presidential nominee must be chosen by WE THE PEOPLE —
not billionaire donors and corporate Super PACs.

After nearly TWO YEARS of organizing by Our Revolution and our progressive
allies inside the Democratic Party, we've achieved a major step forward in
the fight to get dark and corporate money out of the 2028 Democratic
presidential primaries.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40189?source=email-20261124&t=1011&akid=11645%2E5885482%2Ex1HyVj ]Headline: Democrats unveil 2028 debate rules with new dark money
restrictions for presidential hopefuls. Subheadline: The DNC framework
covers super PACs and 501(c)(4) spending but relies largely on candidates'
own self-reporting.

On Monday, the Democratic National Committee announced a plan aimed at
curbing outside influence by requiring presidential candidates to sign a
pledge denouncing Super PAC and dark money spending that boosts their
campaigns or attacks their opponents.

This is a big deal. But a pledge is only as powerful as the pressure
behind it.

Now comes the next phase of our fight: Holding EVERY presidential
candidate accountable for rejecting this money — and making sure the DNC
follows through.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40189?source=email-20261124&t=1012&akid=11645%2E5885482%2Ex1HyVj ]SIGN THE PETITION: MONEY OUT. VOTERS IN!

Here's why this matters.

In 2028, Democrats need to put forward the strongest possible candidate to
defeat whoever the Republicans nominate — someone who can build a winning
coalition, fight for working people, and take on the powerful interests
driving the affordability crisis.

But we can't have a fair contest if billionaire-funded Super PACs are
allowed to tip the scales before voters even have their say.

## Record St. Johns Flooding Continues
Gov. ## Six Charged for Orlando Animal Abuse
State agents [arrested six workers](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkDFu7CAURVeDO1vAYGAKit-4m9-mtLB5jF-CeRYwtrL7aLKF1Fe6R-d8POaHx4T5-d_v4CLFOcNVE7QGZS6wUgkxEQXMz5Vyw_yCmmiWXOpeiF6q2a8NT5iV74Izynq-dOCEuY-jMMbYbnNRm5Gvi_ZKRQVGaL0sKkpupTVKqNihe_8JIZXgoxbjsERug1LjqC1Yf78xxSFgozJ8EuaYvumEEhMVDH5Yae-S21o7Krv9Y3Jicrqua6g5t_O9Mjm9pZicXm3bAaH09QD_VXvMPZXkc6D-wrb1FfejUmZy6ooLx4UpYdWGKf7cPaZfVPtjpdPJnwAAAP__MgZ9fg) Friday at Ali Meat International, a halal slaughterhouse in Orlando, on charges that they tortured livestock during a June 2025 event where customers paid to buy and slaughter animals. The case began when a member of the public sent investigators 19 videos from the event. Officials say [the footage shows](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJyk0LHO3CAQBOCnsTtOgMHmCoo07v60Ka21WeyNMHsCfE7eProob5B-9GlmfnwtX0CJ8v4dTvSR45Lxrglbw7IU3LiEmJgD5X3j3ChfWBMvWupRKCW0WWBr9MbFQB_8ZBzItUevpqe1apom1x8-OAQn5TRKq-y6QUTjVhUGt5rJPs3Qk_94SmmjpB2VfaxRumCMtaNDB8-hMxIDNS6Pn0w5pt_8xhITFwrw2Pjskz9ae9Vu-NbpudPzfd-PyL8GyyVBDvwJdXr-bOv0PAooBWvDIP4hoia49qNhOfiqKOpxNRH4zgJOCgJSwh0aca7i4FIo0iYg0wlJwHpV7IsPr5tSojpOnZH7CZT-Nmv_eerb6z8BAAD__4EIj8o) workers stepping on dying animals, cattle shocked and beaten, and staff guiding a 12-year-old's hand to kill a sheep. Attorney General James Uthmeier called it "[horrific animal abuse](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkL2y2yAQhZ8GdXhgBUIuKNLQ3bQpNSt-LJIVeBC2Jm-fUcZvcLstdr_9zvn1tXxhplweP3GPNtW0lHgeFHuPbWnR1xYS1Rpyefhaei6veFBdQMDEpeSgFvQ9v-OicAjWqBnFOkQrzV1raYyZh816ECYCaOPBKI2TGVcxKwP3JMeU4D5ke_GkBCWFnqS-rUnMQSmtpznOeB-ZEjHkXtvtd80l0d_6ji1RbTngzdd9ILv1_jzY-IOBY-DO87x5yv5PbYQl1GuJgbuyMXBUPRIDd31l4KS85pGB-yB5x_aI_eCfa74hIfH11f0WGz-2-uSXAceSdySO6-uIDNzQbHiemSgfk2FKPHbM9N-vf7Pat4V_AQAA__8CzI2u)" and said the business has been shut down. Manager Nadeem Shakeel, 44, admitted organizing the event, officials said, and agents found a stolen rifle in his office. Shakeel faces [up to 105 years](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykULGuqzAU-xrYQEkaEhgyvIWtb30jOk1OIE-HnCqkRf37K_oLd7EtWbJl_7svd0iU8voXdnSR45LxPAhrxbIU9FxCJOaQ8uo515RfeBAvSijTSdkpvYCv6Y2LhjY4q0cQjxadtNMwSGvt2G5OxQDgo_GTFNY8bByj9kooaQRII0Kb3JUnpdJSDEYO_SOKMWg9DGbEEaZbowWGVLn0_znlSB9-Y4nEJQXoPe8tua3W59Hc_jRqbtR8nmf_gY35chs1X6MaNb8ugFKTJ7yk6fwGZcXQARF-OacdqKtc6qtgJ6226mamsd_qTm1x4XkmonQY22ix7pDo219_ed3bqZ8AAAD__0fXg2I) in prison if convicted, and the other five face 10 to 25 years. ICE has placed detainers on four defendants from Mexico, Pakistan, and Haiti who officials say are in the country illegally.
## Deltona Cancels Christmas Parade
Deltona has canceled its Dec. 12 [Christmas parade](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkLGO5CAQRL_GzrAMBhsCgkuczaUXWm1oz_QJ0yPgxrd_v5rV_sHmpap6789tuwElyvffcKI_-NgyXjVha1i2goFLPBJzpHwPnBvlf1gTb2pUs5BSKL1BaPTCTUMf_aItjHuPXi7OGLksi-0f3s077k5GO9mglVTgXJxn66JRUtrJ9eTffVIqLUczSzPsx2ij1sbMFi24qdMjRmpchr9M-Ugf_MJyJC4UYQh89sk_WnvWbvrVqbVT63Vdw8H_J8MlQY78DnVqfbN1ao2YGmcQAXLAVEV4FKrthCqeUCCiCNSwiu-BKuDEHE_MTUx98fF5UUpU56XT4_0ESl8X2g_tvbz6DAAA__8wRoY3) and nearly every other city event, saying Amendment 3's property tax cut will force more than $23 million in budget cuts by 2030. City Manager Doc Dougherty's [letter to residents](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkb2yozAMhZ8GOmWwMeAUFNvQ3W23ZIQtJ9oRdsZ2uJO33yE3b7CdZr6jn6Pz52v9QhaOt9-40xxSWCN9F6FaKa-ZXMo-SEqe482lWDk-qUhadadHUAq0WdFVPmg12Pp5Mha7raVZTddhUNM02fY-a6utxc1sI23dRmR80P31au0YutBvoeX5nKeUNqobRjVcttBZb8wwjJYsXvvGdOS5pnz5mzgGeaWDcpCU2ePFpb2V-V7rozT9r0YvjV7cVpQ-SaOX01CjF0kOpdGLJ6kpInzawWF0JAXcPXOpOxZ4YEZP4LhSAd3DziKcInAE3Cn6nWKFHtyzllPEVMClZ3wXPmOp7H7gkeRZGH_oC1Dk1L-ADoq1AIVA7-fJ63MF-TbP_vF9Lizj1JjutiPL22L9z3SOWf8LAAD__6mnqv0) put next year's cut at about $12 million, with $5 million more to come. Only two self-funded 5K runs remain on the schedule, and the city is withdrawing vehicle orders and ending construction contracts. Dougherty said Deltona's reliance on low property values and little commercial development leaves it more exposed than most. Dougherty wrote that even though the city has lowered its tax rate for four years in a row, the cuts are "[only the beginning](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkDEO3CAURE-DOyzDgvEWFGncbdqUFoaP_SP8WQGxtbePHO0NUr-Z0cz8ei0vhwlp--kOsDHHheCqCVqDshTwuYSYcg5Im8_UkP5ATXmRgxy5EFyqxfmGJyzKdcEaNblh7cAK89RaGGOmbrdxVOMah3WdNKxRmhAiGC2kcKBHaZ4d2jtPCKnEoEeh-zUOU1BK63GCyT0fTA0QsOXS_85IMX3yCSWmXDC43uejS3Zv7V3Z4weTM5PzdV19JWrnTZmc71FMzl8Lk3Om9OFtB77ChkRIG_9C7rF9uHfkIVXu94K1Ha7ytysuwE1vsTuAwgHU-IPJuSs2vC9MCetomBq2w2H6V6z956enlX8DAAD__z9Tjvg)" of service reductions. Voters passed Amendment 3 with 62% on Nov. 3, raising the homestead exemption on non-school property taxes to $250,000 by 2028. Supporters say [about 92% of Floridians](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAURb_G7rAAgzEFxTbpsu2W1gs8kreDIQImVv5-5NH8wfRH5-qef9ftCpQo3__Cji6WuGU8WsLesW4VfakhplIC5bsvuVP-xJbKJrlcmBBMqg18pxduCsbgjFqB30Z0wlithTFmHR9ORh6ltaitNcGAsfNtWSAqGQM3ahEjudMnhFSC60Xo6Rb5GpTSellxBTsPimOgXur0v1CO6V1eWGMqlQJMvuxjco_en22Y_wzyMsjLcRzTeeRA_DiBQV5-cOapv5mH7DE15h-VWt-hsSdUCMhOMYMdc9gxdzYzIY3Ws-BjdeF5UErUFjMoft-B0vd2_2W2l5NfAQAA__-RF4LL) will save money, while state economists project local governments will lose about $5 billion in the first year.

## TN to Reach 8.1 Million People by 2040

The state is expected to add nearly 1.2 million residents from 2020 to 2040, after [adding more than 98,000 people in 2024](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSozAMQL_GdGYsYYgpXFxDl2uvZBxbBN8Zm8FKMvn7G3Z2dj9gO80rnvT05zpfXUwx33-7jSzzMmd61UTMdMyc97I_kuNY8n6Uv-TPKdNrRoWDBJCoZ-c5PmnWrgn2hjA67RuycBn7HkwP0Kx2MQsN3bAYTxQurvNhQGP6TjkkY_TSRHsKAVADKINjS15phdqMyvnBDCS0ohC5HC2vxJQz1Uq0pHd50tH6sjXJrsx7Fd0vgZPAiXMNvn3wv5bCQ-B0LhA4gRI4dSBwupV3kJ4y0yE_46r8UsvvcslFHuT8Ko0EucWUTnh7S1T6tDWHDfvrxHW4CK3um4vp4yb-4UOfFv8HAAD__9ZyiqE), its largest one-year gain on record. Residents 65 and older will see the biggest growth, rising from 1.32 million in 2024 to 1.68 million in 2040, or nearly 21% of the population. ## Storm Could Snarl Thanksgiving Travel
A potent coastal storm is set to push [_heavy rain and strong winds_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkLHOpSAQhZ8GO4yDqFhQbGN3t93SIIxXEgQDk0t8-433f4S_m8lJzpfv_HutL-ODj--_5kS9R7tGrCUgEebVxEQHZptMIRMKpXxGW0ykVXRi5ABcyPXKqVxoaYXG6Wnqx9k1qGGahwHUANAcelM42n6z3bZZpWCwVmGnZiHcqJzaofH6KQQQEqBTPbSzw0FOo5w3OWE_b0x26Dyl3O7hTh_MMWU6rMkp-Gham84m6IPoKqz_w8TCxFJrbStaekImlgfAxALw3D0Ty-5zIW4CZuJ7ymjN8_4Y8wPN5-ZfY17uQnjyam4mliZrd1Ufgi_jxGT3Po0PXz79dr2PFv8DAAD__4UkhWw) across North Carolina from Wednesday into Thanksgiving, threatening messy conditions on the year's busiest travel days. Forecasters expect widespread downpours and gusts Wednesday, and warn that a few inches of rain could flood roads. The Cape Fear coast could pick up another 1 to 3 inches. Monday offered a gray, foggy preview, with dense fog northwest of Charlotte and highs in the low 70s before a cold front was expected to drop [temperatures into the 50s](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkE9r3DAQxT-NfdPikf_IPujQNGtoSkJZKCEnMyvPWqKytEhTm_32xTn1ntvMe_B4v_f-Or2i8y4sb7iSvgUzBdqzJ2ZKE4bIlpKJmBl95pjWYDIGnmQlOwEgZDPdU8x3MjxBOWul6m6YS9KghraFvgUora7aHoy8KpxR9pVSg7w1HUEPpkbAQZVOH4EAsgGo-hpOw0xto7pmuDaK6uFaNBXNjmM63fwjbpRCTGwNpuhdwJOJa-m1Zb7nov5WyLGQ477vpz1Hw9thHwLhQVPI8RYTGcyc_7vFJ57Ij8y0Csa0EGeRaHExiN2xFZZwe4iE7vjDLNim-Hexgi2GP3lxmwtLIcfzx-X98vvp54-38eXXy-X8_P35SX50XXcu5FgmPd93573LnSqaalnR-c_6_NXxNy3_BQAA__8kvZy2) today. A coastal flood advisory was already posted along the southeast coast. The system should clear for a mostly dry holiday weekend, though rain chances still run [near 60% Thanksgiving morning](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJyk0DGP3CAQBeBfgztWDMbmKCjSuLu0Ka1ZGK9HwbACtGT_fXQn5RekftL7nt6vz_0TOXF-_MSL_JHDnmm0RL1T3TGXflINBVvH1HqpVw4Nc9-10qsEkNrsz1rak0LfYYre2nl1cSIP1i0LfCwA0-lnOhbUloylAw6lgOzsokOE-wrRuYn9VyGANgDqY4abi7QYuxp3N5ZmdxdGUeRe6u1I7_KimkvtZ8BaEme8hXJNyZ-9P5uYfwi9Cb2NMW7jDzPor1joDWvnkEjo7eIU5VVyxLcMpSSqclCXg3N8y35i_t0e_OL8kBU5y29L_sOE3qxZ1KKMnaqPz8EpcVutMOpxIafvMf1_r3x5_TcAAP__TYSLGA) at the coast, with gusty winds lingering into Thursday.
## Anthropic IPO Boosts State Pension Fund
North Carolina's pension fund stands to gain [_more than $700 million_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJyk0LGupCAUgOGn0Q4jiCIFxTZ2s-2WBuE4ssFzDJwZs2-_mZvcJ7j9n6_4_zzWh0854fO3P8HtGFaEu2ZghrJ6JD6gBPKVfa5M5cRQPfKqejUJKYXS61WoXhB4lW10xgyTjS04aew4ynmUsj0c6EnaGeZhtiHM-2Yms4XNjGM_WWtMbJP7gFIqLWU_D7KzEUZtJm03bWCwW6N7iImpdHv-R28oSIWP4AvlhL4LdLbZHcxXbYZfjVoatdz33X0Hf-lV0OdP16jFIx-FrhREukgEeuUofIzi4wrT96dgEhjEBVgTodhfGBu1tMXF6045pzqZRvfP06cvsuWfjns79T8AAP__qICE8A) from an early stake in Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, after its record-setting Nasdaq debut. State Treasurer Brad Briner said the state's $250 million investment, made eight months ago, was worth about $950 million after Anthropic's first day of trading Thursday, a gain of roughly $700 million. Shares were priced at $83, a price that valued the company at about $1.5 trillion, then [_opened at $111.50_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE9jMiPbYBgCB5uQzaYbImM3gyXTRu2eQXP7Ff8KPy6pqt7791yePuWEr7_-ALdhWBCumoEZaPFYeAcKxVf2uXKhA0P1yItRZpBaS9MvJ5V6QuBFN9GNYzdMsQGnx8la_bBaN7tTK4CNqgMd9DQE-4hqmJTd1AbbaruuSe4u1Nr0WqtHp9spgu3HoZ_WfoRuWkWvICYu1G75Wz5AWIj34KnkhL4N5Wiy25nPKro_wszCzNd1tRf5fIfCzDeWMHMuwWdhZo-8UzlTkOksMsL6ZnmAxyqvhBKDJOBEcACy3N4YJRP4-iYgWf23SiwfOFYgeR8XZm7IxfNKOac6jKJXr8Onn-mGf2v148z_AAAA__-nKY-4) and closed the day at $97.17. Briner said the gain shrinks a long-running pension shortfall and could open the door to a cost-of-living raise for retirees. He was also candid about weak spots, noting five-year returns of about 5.5%, below the 6.7% median for large public plans.
## Cooper Names Leadership Team for Senate
Sen.-elect Roy Cooper announced his [_U.S. Senate leadership team_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJyk0L2OtCAUxvGr0Q4jX6IFxdtMN2-7pTnCcSRBMHBWMne_mb2FrZ_klyf_r-f6hBBDev2HE-2e3Jqw1YhEWFZImQ4sLkMliJVyOZOrkGgVo5gY50yo9Sq5Xuho5b23xshp8T1abhat-aw57w9rRuWd0zB5VHLe9K6Nlgq12lDC7Oc-2A_IuVCcj7Pkw-JRKzOpZVMG5bJ1akQfKJdhj-98Y0m50OGg5BgSDC6ffbQH0VU7-a8Tj048WmtDa_CmW372TjwqJiBkGNERK_nNXM4XFtZCPEN6UU4sAYUbGVTmjoA7yzurBPvOIKX8nRxWFhE8lnqEixHCx-2L9VcLMYY6mU6NrxNC_P1Efy16W_ETAAD__zGdj6Q) Thursday, naming former North Carolina Health and Human Services Secretary Kody Kinsley as chief of staff. Kevin Monroe will serve as state director, and Julia White will lead the transition team. _" Washington, DC is broken and North Carolinians are ready for leadership that will lower costs, end the chaos, and focus on their needs,"_ Cooper said. He [_praised the trio 's experience_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJyk0DGP4yAQBeBfY3dEBmNjCopr0uXaK60JjGMkzFjDXKL8-1V2f8LWn9570vt3W2-QS66Pv3Bg2GpcK75aQRHkFSrJjhwJmkBpQnzU2KDKagYzK62VsevJ1E6Msuo-BefG2aceg3Z-mvQyad3vwcQIw2KNx1HjZg34zQ0zpDEt1rnJ9jl8CrU2VuthGfXFJ5ysm62_W4ejv3d2wJSF-LKVNz2RK7HsEZhKrnCJdPQl7CJn68Y_nbl25sr0jkQn8kc7c21YQYgVFoyimN7qhxXUSv9rxKYKQkJuez7VRqwE4RPsOaTzlUvJbXadHR4H5PI9Kb897BnMVwAAAP__9_-DAA) and commitment to delivering results for the state. Kinsley, a Wilmington native, previously oversaw Medicaid expansion that [_covered more than 730,000 residents_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJyk0L2OtCAUxvGr0Q4jX6IFxdtMN2-7pTnCcSRBMHBWMne_mb2FrZ_klyf_r-f6hBBDev2HE-2e3Jqw1YhEWFZImQ4sLkMliJVyOZOrkGgVo5gY50yo9Sq5Xuho5b23xshp8T1abhat-aw57w9rRuWd0zB5VHLe9K6Nlgq12lDC7Oc-2A_IuVCcj7Pkw-JRKzOpZVMG5bJ1akQfKJdhj-98Y0m50OGg5BgSDC6ffbQH0VU7-a8Tj048WmtDa_CmW372TjwqJiBkGNERK_nNXM4XFtZCPEN6UU4sAYUbGVTmjoA7yzurBPvOIKX8nRxWFhE8lnqEixHCx-2L9VcLMYY6mU6NrxNC_P1Efy16W_ETAAD__zGdj6Q) and launched a medical debt relief program erasing billions in bills. Monroe brings more than three decades of public service, while White has advised Cooper for over 25 years.

## Virginia Spruce Named National Christmas Tree
A red spruce cut from the mountains of Highland County will stand as this year’s National Christmas Tree on the Ellipse near the White House. Crews with the George Washington and Jefferson National Forests [_selected the roughly 35-foot tree_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2u5CAQBODT4AzL9OCfCQg2cTabbmg1pm16F-MRsEZz-ye_K7ykkpI-lerPa3khB477bzzIlGtbItUcqBRKS_EY_-WdL457Lmc67FnDO5FboINBKiVBL7gWvmjR2DizoSZ8NmTU-Ox7NY16aLzRA2C3ThZ7bbXtYCOnoe_IDthbR7Zhc3tKgVZKAfQtuHFCoK13duiG9SF0R47Lmdri6eK0c2Tcwue8KLXreTTB-FLeWTx-CZgFzLXWtjr7d7xbAfPtC5iVumMSMK8-cS4HZlkSkfS8-4DRyfX8H8tHekJHTlbMnuNezijdKmBuknHvyiFwHkahu_1ADt8Dyg-_uwx8BQAA__--MITK) on Nov. 15, hauling it from the high country of Western Virginia to Washington. It’s the third straight year a spruce from this national forest has been chosen for the honor. _“We are honored to share this magnificent red spruce with the nation as the National Christmas Tree and to showcase the natural beauty and heritage of Virginia on a national stage,”_ said Acting Forest Supervisor Troy Morris. The [_National Christmas Tree Lighting_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOpDAQAF8DGcg2GGYCB5eQzaUXosZucOuMjexeo_n9avYLG1ZSJdW_1_oCChSPv3Ci4bqvEe8SkBnzyh7i_3JQpXgUTvnc0h2ujG5VQk2dlJ0aV7BMFdcRWmd2GBGeLRo5P7WWj3mcWm8Ad-vkvFmrYBNi0PIp5D5rAKHBDbol8_FJqUYppVK6V25-gMJdu20Skx2aUaAjTrlnj5XyQZFgD-9UMfc2nW0wnvkqzfCnUUujlvu--3iV_kj1Q96nRi1XgPhOX7lSIW7UEoEpRQid9ZkKn1A6zoi957PNxl03hUBlmptRHCdQ-CnxLydVo74DAAD__61Sf3c) is set for Thursday, Dec. 3, in President’s Park. ## Two COTA Drivers Killed in Crash
Two Central Ohio Transit Authority bus drivers [died Monday after their buses collided head-on](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkM2K2zAURp9G3inoL7K98KIdxqShM6Sl0HZlZOkmukWRjCTb9O2L5xW6vRcO53w_36Y3gwHj4908YajJ36cIewlQK-RpXovNpniPy5Js2iBDWiAWMwkmNOWcCjUZW3GDSZnGDQokv_cNDLztz2fe9Z1q_HBmQgrGOy1nrrlrW7Basb6XTEnt7nODw8HjXCjOuRb8xIwEy7rOqdYpCZooBg5ryqfqIXlM9_D30DnZ9GzC4GtdCpGfiBiJGPd9P-0e0_EkYjx6iBhDsiYQMQrqwDhaYINsAsX4Z83gqD-OKdKPXopxS2HD-KDLOge0tGYTC1Y6rwUKtSmsz3k9sNeXz19vV6m_fb-cb6-XX68v79fbj4v68puIscmDW3YMAYtuiWKPp8Hw4Vz_d-ttEP8CAAD__6xalBE) near Columbus' Weinland Park. The crash happened just after 8 a.m. on East 11th Avenue, [a few blocks from the Ohio State Fairgrounds](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOhCAQxvGnwY6NILpaUFxjt9deaUYYdS4sYwDd7Ntf3Fe4fjL5_b-fx_QAChTXb3iiLbwtU8RXDlgKpmk-skuQt432nR2fmJB3jBkmXetOKiW1mcAVOnEyUHlrsFHLUKFV96FtVT_0ptpsAwC67b13bjZmaRcPZtBtB9B6VLWryF7_lNJGKdVpdauhQVf3vTd3bxrshKnRU-F0KxvyRryE98W5OX5WwW6l7Fk0X0KPQo8wu47jm4-UyeN1IvR4VQk9BnYQhB45ovQIXiotKf4eCb2EpWCSn2BJ8eRwUlxlebF0XEDOR8YsI0KSl0DmAgXlApTWxEf0uUrW7y8KgXJ3F6Zen0DhIyz_Xfa0-i8AAP__0ySSZw). A third vehicle then struck one of the buses from behind, though the people inside had only minor injuries. Fire officials described both buses as "mangled," and crews had to cut them open to reach passengers. One driver died at the scene and the other at a hospital. At least nine others were hospitalized in stable condition, [including three taken to Nationwide Children's Hospital](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0bGunTAMgOGnCZuP4hACDAxd2G7XjsgkzknaHIJCAPXtK-4rdLb025_862v5opji9v5JH55qDn7Z-D4S18plWc_DFjpCiPuebb64cN55O2hRUhlABKUXsjVevGhq3KS5RT82PGE_dh0O46CbMHnksTeuHdbWeM-dNMZox14ptmroVROnp4eoNCIahS9JLVs5DE73TrdshJbsYs3lVQPnELNPf59zXjZ_mjSFWvdDtD-EmoWa7_t-oazXMxRqplKjTSzU_MiEmlO2lISaERyTexRx-30WdkC-coFvMsTtyumK2xvqncHmSrCeBx-AkGvgAheHpwsbU4GbY6LNwU7lD9iczs96Pru6VgIzuk53A5BZHWhpPYw9G7A8EPfWYrdyUya33zGleJheaPn-UEzfuvq_X7km9S8AAP__mLaiTg). Police haven't released the drivers' names, and the cause of the crash is under investigation.
## Ohio AG Fights Federal Sports Bet Rule
Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson is [helping lead attorneys general from 43 states and Washington, D.C.](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upyAUxJ9GOwwc8Kuw2MbubrulOcBBuEExwF-zb7_xvsK2k5nJb-bP1_aFIYZz_40HLTV5t530lEi1Ut70p5iMxftwXcmkmzKli86CG3AYmBAM1Iamhps2ha1dFEnh5pYWMc59L6Z5Uq1f5tlpnAikHXrNR0PSTMJJ0pMEK4Vsw_L2CQFKCDGA6DhKMnyarBqtkjQ0ipMNNeWueko-JBf_vjidSUcbF1_rVRr5q4G1gfV5nu47ffKJkb1jXlMDa0wGYwPrG2e4s-8UzsIUsFQ95cLCyVzYfQ3nzhxZyhhZuVKuhWmqP_KBJ31uyg2smGswkTbsx0FKLhn0TrHeasO0GTnT86QHp0Yw3HW-HrHNi72eEGMow9govh8Y4g9__d_f7wX-BQAA__87QJkD), in fighting a federal rule that would treat sports bets on prediction markets as financial "swaps." The Commodity Futures Trading Commission's proposal would put those wagers, offered by platforms like Kalshi, under federal oversight. The bipartisan coalition formally objected in a Nov. 18 letter. The attorneys general argue the rule would let operators sidestep state licensing, age limits, and problem-gambling protections. _"A sports bet isn't a derivative just because the CFTC says so,"_ Wilson said. The CFTC [says event contracts tied to sports, politics, and weather are commonly treated as swaps](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFurDAQheGnMd0iz9gYKFzchm6vojQp0WCGtSWzRrYDyttHmyIvkO5Un47-j_t8pxDD8_GfdrY1-W1-8lUi18p5Xj6Ly1S8D8eRXDo5czr4WWhGieYGcEM9k6vh5FlTs1rNCraxYQv92HUwjINuvO07GDvH5KQBWgbFG-JGixnNggo0N8G-PADUAGAQWkmKnRyGVferVmyElryGmnJbPScf0ha_Xndal_YmWl_rUYT6J3ASOF3X1bqtuvaRToHTW-ZS3lPafzdHpsJF4DQqkDc0TbbrcYUYQzG90PKxU4g_dv1rk9PidwAAAP__6lF2Hw) and that the rule would clear up legal ambiguity. Chairman Michael Selig has argued the agency holds exclusive jurisdiction over those markets.
## Hippo Cove Reopens without Fiona

UN Climate Summit Ends in Failure U.N. climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, collapsed Sunday after the European Union, the U.K., and others rejected a final draft that . The COP31 talks ran two days past their deadline, the longest overrun in the conference's history, before COP31 President Murat Kurum he understood there was no agreement on the text. It's the first time the summit has ended without an overarching agreement since Copenhagen in 2009. Rather than fossil fuels, the draft leaned on carbon-capture targets, and more than 90 countries separately backed a voluntary pledge to raise electricity's share of global final energy use from 23% to , with few specifics on how it would be generated. Trump Halts Iowa Blast Pending Court OK President Trump said Monday he has ordered the Army not to detonate nearly five tons of unstable explosives at an Iowa ammunition plant until a federal appeals court and Gov.-elect Rob Sand agrees. The Army had planned to blow up 68 barrels of degraded lead azide, a detonator compound, in Middletown, arguing the material could explode on its own as temperatures fall and that a controlled blast is the safest option. Trump said he agrees but will defer to the Eighth Circuit, which paused an EPA emergency permit Thursday. Residents, farmers, and lawmakers in Iowa and Illinois have fought the plan over fears that could drift for miles. The Army says it will spray the ground and mist the air to keep most of it on base. Last Friday, a 34-year-old Indian national living in a Chicago suburb stood up in federal court and admitted to one of the largest Medicare rip-offs ever charged: $227 million in fraudulent claims, of which Medicare actually paid out about $136 million -- billed for COVID-19 test kits that seniors never ordered and never received. Some of the people on those claims, federal prosecutors say, were already dead.
His name is Syed Murtuza Kablazada. He pleaded guilty to two counts of health care fraud, agreed to forfeit more than $46 million seized from ten bank accounts, and faces up to 20 years.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1c01e64c-ea87-47f1-958a-b5dcad60633f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Syed Mehdi Hussain and Syed Murtuza Kablazada
But the guilty plea isn't the real story. The real story is where the scheme started -- and what it says about how badly Washington is guarding your medical identity.
**An $11 Million Shopping Trip**
Beginning in January 2023, Kablazada and his partners quietly acquired three Chicago-area labs -- **Chicago Care** , **V Care** , and **Al-Ameer**. Then, according to DOJ, he paid approximately $11 million to a purported telemarketing company _based in Pakistan_.
What did $11 million buy? The personally identifiable information of hundreds of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries -- names, dates of birth, and the beneficiary ID numbers that are the keys to America's largest health insurer.
Run the arithmetic and it gets insulting. Hundreds of thousands of records for $11 million works out to roughly $20 to $40 per senior. Your entire Medicare billing identity -- the thing that follows you into every exam room for the rest of your life -- wholesaled for less than I found Buckingham Nicks (1973) on vinyl for on Discogs.com.
With that data in hand, the labs ran fake claims for over-the-counter COVID test kits for six straight months while Medicare paid on autopilot. The proceeds moved overseas through transfers and unlicensed money transmitters, and some of it bought luxury cars.
**How Does Your Medicare Number End Up in Pakistan?**
This is the question that should keep every Medicare beneficiary -- and every member of Congress -- up at night. And the federal government has already answered it, in black and white, in other cases.
HHS's Office of Inspector General has documented a Pakistan-based call center operating under the name **Hello International Marketing Solutions** (HIMS) that obtained Medicare beneficiary information, including ID numbers, through theft and deception. DOJ's 2025 fraud-case summaries spell out exactly how: hacking, scraping publicly accessible websites, and building fake websites that tricked seniors into handing over their own information by advertising free health care products. That's not a telemarketing company. That's a data-theft operation wearing a telemarketing costume.
Once the data is stolen, the call center does two jobs. First, it robocalls beneficiaries to farm recorded consent for COVID kits, durable medical equipment, and genetic tests that were never requested -- a consent recording that gets stapled to the claim to defeat Medicare's utilization edits. Second, it wholesales the stolen ID numbers to U.S. fraudsters like Kablazada, and recruits American accomplices to move the data around unlawfully.
To be precise: DOJ hasn't publicly named Kablazada's specific vendor. But OIG has documented this exact playbook feeding exactly this kind of fraud -- and the scale is staggering. OIG currently lists four fugitives wanted in $703 million in Medicare false claims tied to that Pakistan call-center network. One of them, Fizza Farid, allegedly served as a nominee owner of a U.S. medical supplier -- the same figurehead trick Kablazada used by installing foreign nationals as lab owners, who then fled the country when investigations began. Farid herself fled in April 2025 and is believed to be in Islamabad. A related case alone cost Medicare and Medicare Advantage $418 million in paid claims.
Fugitives
And the Kablazada complaint says the same marketing-company data fed schemes in at least 17 states, totaling more than $500 million in false claims.
**Pay First, Ask Never**
Here's the structural scandal underneath the sensational one. A name plus a Medicare Beneficiary Identifier is a complete billing key. Medicare adjudicates claims on the encounter data in front of it -- there is no step where the system confirms a beneficiary ever requested, consented to, or received the item. A stranger in another hemisphere with a stolen number and a recorded robocall can bill your account, and the machine pays.
Then we chase. Justice did catch this -- but only _after_ roughly six months of billing and $136 million out the door, and only by prosecuting the downstream lab operator. The upstream node, the call center harvesting the data, sits offshore where CMS has no direct reach, and its alleged operators are fugitives. That's pay and chase working exactly as designed: recover a rounding error, years later, while the data broker keeps dialing.
Washington's defenders will say the system caught it. Sure -- the way a smoke detector that goes off after the house has burned down caught the fire eventually.
**What You Can Do Tonight**
\- Read your Medicare Summary Notice -- every quarter, every line. Look for COVID test kits, braces, genetic tests, or medical equipment you never requested. Don't forget deceased family members' files; they are the juiciest targets of all.
\- Call 1-800-MEDICARE to dispute anything unfamiliar, and report suspected fraud to the HHS-OIG hotline at 1-800-HHS-TIPS.
Kablazada will likely serve prison time and face removal from the country. That's accountability for one man. But until Medicare builds a verification step between the claim and the payout -- and until the call centers in Islamabad stop being safe harbors for stealing American seniors' medical identities -- the next $227 million is already being dialed.

name: Pat Moore
subject: My opponent wants huge data center pollution w/ no guardrails
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pat Moore for Congress
body:
Voters here are still fired up and ready to flip this district after coming out in record numbers this midterm, but we have to be ready to fight back against MAGA’s attacks.
| | | [](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001T6z2EJNdFK03QtXXOASqrVv1tLK7CjvNveLFtWG6cvoRs2NsBzLR-kmtI8Rs7MWzT-QJlRFt3AHjTQB1Bi7ju9AHhv523X-bbi5o_6AeMPqCFSnVYdV-fFeamLCEv88rCETZUjhuyp5lgk_geMEwvTiUsJ_0jwX8p1BrxDSnEAzNSR8C64LXgNld45-y-bMgAUxQFj6C2eDKH1Q-Pconyhq9lDpRmjq2al-_iwRDbMo=&c=L4tEmPh1yRVur_C5ccttHYx1PJ71vZ77j9FCofOYu0uFZgNmPTi2KA==&ch=A2fZS9shY-IBZqJg_V2lYfDMHPgU1mw5AQX1cjaOnDq-hcfefNlChA==)
---
Friend,
A new study showed that large scale data centers are _already_ responsible for emitting an estimated 25.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide every year, almost as much as the entire country of Denmark.
This is crazy, and unacceptable.
I’m Pat Moore, Democrat for Louisiana’s 5th district. My race is headed to a Dec 12 runoff after I finished in first with 0.73% lead against my MAGA opponent Gabe Firment.
**I believe we need strict rules to prevent data center projects from polluting our communities, wasting our water, and driving up utility prices just to benefit tech billionaires.**
But my opponent doesn’t care about any of that. He’s more concerned that we the people “ _keep an open mind_ ” about what the billionaires want from _us_. He cares more about the needs of Elon Musk, Peter Thiel, Mark Zuckerberg and the rest of the billionaire class than about us.
[](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001T6z2EJNdFK03QtXXOASqrVv1tLK7CjvNveLFtWG6cvoRs2NsBzLR-kmtI8Rs7MWzyLn8fDDzdZ_g7J8RVqI-tl9Ey5DeIRiY-ViC1cb-LJMh9KGLOwweRWS7QjTDbzDq-QCcH-ojf9JnN8hPOUG4sHNWUPJxD3Ref0mIQW78HRiDxO8getLJGY_Ma73F33KmBZ1UZJ7ga_X5vbXM_R3E-GM3c5IAxg5DczFOnKhfqNwqmWs2uR2vESr80SWc7Ojq&c=L4tEmPh1yRVur_C5ccttHYx1PJ71vZ77j9FCofOYu0uFZgNmPTi2KA==&ch=A2fZS9shY-IBZqJg_V2lYfDMHPgU1mw5AQX1cjaOnDq-hcfefNlChA==)
---
Voters just sent politicians a clear message about data centers in their backyards and neighborhoods: not without our consent, not without paying their own way, and not without seriously reducing environmental impact.
**But if my MAGA opponent wins on December 12 all bets are off.** We’ll have a data center on every corner and in every neighborhood—except for the super wealthy’s.
But Democrats just proved that if we organize and fight to win, with the right candidate and the right message we can flip even deep red seats.

| Friend, [There is no gentle way to say it, so I won’t try: _**Republicans got crushed on Election Day.**_](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyMkj-P3CAUxD8N7ljB44_twkUky92liFZJiVh49qKzsQV4L_n2Ebt3qdMOo5nfG_HrzbzZsIa4fLcbDqnMJmVT7pjQve8xxMUAA005pyCNdSU80Ejb-ME7b7lrcOBtrxQIKWVzHxBmKUHPmunZMtcz8Dep-Gz7Wevb3DZhqHmcg-QgmFAXx5S2ne77TrSqs4pIZldM5ZLwOG9rcDYWm9_nPTm8uH1r1uFeypGJ-EZgIjBldGfCy0eICX11EJhiyo7A9EQ_9lworuhK2CPNZ3rgHxqXEJcU3J0iPWwNEtNZNrOhD-dGxIibDSsBXcW8n8khEeMOm6nup1ocEeOP60S_DvrUnd0OG5ZIxFhfav1X-6vcpTPf0dO4mH8Y5kX8CthjwViIGOcz-mRDDnEhoO1Wjj2HGkTEKF-KJGLkjBHQqe6QqlWMJZ1IQONvU4L_BOGca3O90p_XC-et7HpTgHVKdpKqVjVp8MdHWNeQdUskW-r9z73L__-KxwB_AwAA__-ug8FP) To put it in historical terms, last week’s GOP defeat is the seventh-largest midterm defeat since 1938, when Franklin Delano Roosevelt’s Democrats took the worst midterm beating of the modern era. But he had room to fall. __We, however, walked into November 3rd holding the narrowest of margins, with almost no cushion at all, and a defeat that a bigger majority might have absorbed, hit us with nothing underneath to break the fall.__ A defeat this size doesn’t heal on its own, and unless we understand exactly why voters turned away from us, the next one will come faster and cut deeper, and the history books won’t be ranking it seventh. [_**The work of understanding this defeat has to start somewhere, and I’d like it to start with you. Will you please take this two-minute Post-Election Assessment?**_](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyMkj-P3CAUxD8N7ljB44_twkUky92liFZJiVh49qKzsQV4L_n2Ebt3qdMOo5nfG_HrzbzZsIa4fLcbDqnMJmVT7pjQve8xxMUAA005pyCNdSU80Ejb-ME7b7lrcOBtrxQIKWVzHxBmKUHPmunZMtcz8Dep-Gz7Wevb3DZhqHmcg-QgmFAXx5S2ne77TrSqs4pIZldM5ZLwOG9rcDYWm9_nPTm8uH1r1uFeypGJ-EZgIjBldGfCy0eICX11EJhiyo7A9EQ_9lworuhK2CPNZ3rgHxqXEJcU3J0iPWwNEtNZNrOhD-dGxIibDSsBXcW8n8khEeMOm6nup1ocEeOP60S_DvrUnd0OG5ZIxFhfav1X-6vcpTPf0dO4mH8Y5kX8CthjwViIGOcz-mRDDnEhoO1Wjj2HGkTEKF-KJGLkjBHQqe6QqlWMJZ1IQONvU4L_BOGca3O90p_XC-et7HpTgHVKdpKqVjVp8MdHWNeQdUskW-r9z73L__-KxwB_AwAA__-ug8FP) | [RESPOND HERE >>](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyMkj-P3CAUxD8N7ljB44_twkUky92liFZJiVh49qKzsQV4L_n2Ebt3qdMOo5nfG_HrzbzZsIa4fLcbDqnMJmVT7pjQve8xxMUAA005pyCNdSU80Ejb-ME7b7lrcOBtrxQIKWVzHxBmKUHPmunZMtcz8Dep-Gz7Wevb3DZhqHmcg-QgmFAXx5S2ne77TrSqs4pIZldM5ZLwOG9rcDYWm9_nPTm8uH1r1uFeypGJ-EZgIjBldGfCy0eICX11EJhiyo7A9EQ_9lworuhK2CPNZ3rgHxqXEJcU3J0iPWwNEtNZNrOhD-dGxIibDSsBXcW8n8khEeMOm6nup1ocEeOP60S_DvrUnd0OG5ZIxFhfav1X-6vcpTPf0dO4mH8Y5kX8CthjwViIGOcz-mRDDnEhoO1Wjj2HGkTEKF-KJGLkjBHQqe6QqlWMJZ1IQONvU4L_BOGca3O90p_XC-et7HpTgHVKdpKqVjVp8MdHWNeQdUskW-r9z73L__-KxwB_AwAA__-ug8FP)

I’ve watched parties take a beating like this and recover, and I’ve watched parties take a beating like this and spend a decade in the wilderness.

And if the margins are any indication, people want big, swing-for-the-fences change.
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=172%2E42639%2EjA5eDY)
It would be difficult to imagine a greater rebuke to Donald Trump and the Republican Party than the election that just happened.
Coast-to-coast, in so-called "blue states", "red states", and even the "purple states”, the American people sent a message that they want change.
And if the margins are any indication, they want big, swing-for-the-fences change.
Bring down prices.
End the corruption.
Usher in some accountability.
But what does that mean legislatively?
It means taking on corporate power - the oligarchs and robber barons - who have been ripping away the American Dream for decades. It means rising paychecks and cheaper daily goods and things like health care, childcare, and housing. It means raising the minimum wage and making sure that people can retire in this country with dignity and security.
On corruption, it means banning congressional stock trading, getting super PAC money out of elections, and ending the ability for billionaires to try and buy our elections. It means stopping the insider trading on prediction markets from those entrusted with serving people. It means investigating and putting a stop to the rampant corruption coming out of the White House and the Trump family.
And on accountability, it means that if someone has been ripping off the American people, they should be held accountable. It means investigations into the abuse of power by ICE in this country. And it means that Pete Hegseth has got to go. People want this war in Iran to end. The chaos and corruption in the Defense Department is indefensible. And Donald Trump should fire the guy and spare the American people the spectacle of having him impeached.
I was re-elected thanks to the support from the residents of my district and people across Pennsylvania and the country who helped out.
That's why I thought it important to share a short email about how I'll be looking at things in the new Congress.
Don't give up the ship,
Chris Deluzio

* * *

☀️ Wait ... Before you click away! 🇺🇸
Here is the truth: Chris Deluzio is quite seriously considering running for John Fetterman's seat, but one of the things he'll have to know in advance is whether the support is there to take him on. Because if we do, we'll be taking on not only John Fetterman, but AIPAC, Trump, and an overwhelming amount of corporate money spent against us.
He is not asking you to donate millions of dollars. And there are many ways for you to say you'd like him to run for Fetterman's seat. But one thing he will see right now - as he thinks about this over the holiday - is what kind of financial support there is for his potential campaign.
We're not asking for a crazy amount, just a few bucks to help us fill the coffers after the last election and to prepare for whatever comes next.

Drought and abnormal dryness now cover about 57% of Colorado, [leaving 43%](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkDHPpCAQQH-NdhgZELSguMZur73SDDCsZFE2yK7Zf3_xcpf7-q-b5CVv5s2v23LDmOJ-_4kbmerCstN5JKqVyuJLft3XuuGT80d9lQd9Dtz9FhfoQTHOGcgFXY1vWiS23oQADlVLhutpGGAAMbar8RNapwWNNA4jqVGHcfIKlScZglVDG83l4xwkF30PU-ctqWC1C6SlRaUa2ZOPNZeuruRyygV9DumT31Q6l7c2mbXW59GIHw3MDczneXbTVXLRBmYsNbpEFyGsK5X_E_vna2D-G8y2vF_bviItmIagBAlgwIVlcphGhtIKZqUW0mvSog9tMf55xpTioXQj-_uGMf05sX7zu28DvwMAAP__ymqOeA) of the state clear, a figure not seen since December. A state hearing officer [dismissed what is believed](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ8GOkd444BTUFxD9197JVrsdVhhsGVviPL2J-4VrptiNPPp-_Mz_yBHPl6_cadRXJgP-tRIIlRmX9L7tcqOWetN3mWjb8XD7zxDB73SWoGZ0QmfNBts_RgCOOxbGvXwfDzgAXfbrqNdvDXWWgJaAvgejLXd4p5dpx_aoml5vPa0BqPvXQfPm1-oD8vgAg1mwb5vTEeeJZWbrORSTAV9CvGbTio3l_Y2jqtIrs39VwNTA1NJbvvu6X0I8nEmdnTVGpiuowYmra98b2DyRDngRsqlPUfkQ5TnunOt5BUfCgaV8UWqvC9LSlYUFfjwVW2cszrZU1JcVS5JyAl5VVG4UANTW0afPxwj135oTPfakeM_XPlP0-cIfwMAAP__aOaU2g) to be the first complaint under Colorado's 2024 deepfake law. ## Jensen Huang is back. I want to know who bought before the announcement.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3f1f8efc-eec1-4b63-806c-66034e6b6fbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I was watching the market before it opened Monday, and Nvidia was already up around 7% when I looked. I thought, what the hell is happening? A company that just fell off a cliff doesn't suddenly move like that for no reason. I figured we might get a new contract, some other announcement, maybe a new CEO. I didn't think Jensen Huang was coming back. I definitely didn't think it would happen like this.
Nvidia's board reinstated Huang on Monday after concluding that his return didn't pose a national security risk. Trump pushed for him to come back and publicly welcomed the decision. Nvidia shares jumped about a third in early trading, and the rally moved well beyond Nvidia. John Thune raised concerns about advanced American chips reaching China, and Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries called for scrutiny of Nvidia and the administration's role.
Now let me put my tinfoil hat on for a minute. Who was buying before the news broke? I brought up Ro Khanna on Facebook. Disclosures showed sales by his wife's trust right before Huang's departure. I'd like to see the same kind of attention paid to who bought before the reinstatement. When the filings come out, I want dates and amounts. The timing is a reason to look at the records. The records are where you find out what actually happened.
A friend and I were talking about this yesterday. His point was that the market was doing its job. Nvidia supplies the chips and helps finance parts of the AI buildout. If there's uncertainty about who runs the company or whether Nvidia can stay ahead on chips, that uncertainty runs downstream to companies like OpenAI and Anthropic. Of course investors are going to price that in.
I think he's right. I also think it shows how fragile this is. A handful of companies carry an enormous share of the stock market. Then one guy leaves, comes back, and you see how much of the AI trade was riding on him. We've seen swings like this when a new industry is taking shape. Think about the dot-com era. Companies can open and close fast, and none of us knows yet how this industry looks when it matures.
A million dollars invested before a 40% move becomes $1.4 million. Scale that up and you see why I want to know who knew about the decision, when they knew, and what they bought. Big money was made here.
[Reuters | Nvidia reinstates Huang and tech shares surge](https://substack.com/redirect/9f86a098-f52f-4b2d-9253-3584e1010d47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) * [The Wall Street Journal | Trump asked Vance to help persuade Nvidia](https://substack.com/redirect/675d61d0-c1a3-4fb9-baa3-6016cc4db7a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) * [Reporting on the Khanna trust disclosures](https://substack.com/redirect/a6fee95c-2dcf-43bb-8583-371081b289e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## MetroHealth projects a $79 million loss next year
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/38dd5e15-dcf8-41b9-bcfe-daaf2b21af17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
MetroHealth, Cuyahoga County's public safety-net hospital system, is budgeting for a **$79 million loss in 2027**. It expects to provide roughly **$541 million in uncompensated care** , a record for the system. CEO Dr. Christine Alexander-Rager expects MetroHealth to finish 2026 with a positive margin of about **$83 million**.
She pointed to declining Medicaid coverage, the expiration of enhanced ACA subsidies, lower government reimbursements, and rising costs. I'm watching what this means for county funding and staffing. When people lose coverage, they still get sick. A safety-net hospital has to budget for what happens next.
[Ideastream | MetroHealth's CEO on the projected 2027 loss...](https://substack.com/redirect/4f957577-c08d-4952-8cf8-dd08f0790048?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Ahead of Thanksgiving, I wanted to reach out and express my gratitude for your ongoing support.

Thanks to everyone who turned out to vote their values this month, America is preparing to move in a new direction. With incoming Democratic control of the House, we have an opportunity to hold Trump accountable and undo the damage he, alongside Republicans in the House, have inflicted on our communities.

There’s a lot of work to be done. But it’s an absolute honor to have your continued trust as I fight to address skyrocketing healthcare costs, ensure people don’t have to choose between putting food on their table or paying their rent or mortgage, and bolster our democracy to preserve it for future generations.

The road ahead won’t be easy, but with you by my side, I vow to work every day to deliver for Ohioans and people across the nation.

**Today, I wanted to say thank you for your support. I hope you are able to spend the next few days surrounded by your family and friends, enjoy good food, and relax. Thank you for staying in this fight with me.**

Together,

Shontel | Shontel Brown is proud to be elected as the Congresswoman for Ohio’s 11th District. She has spent the last decade serving the people of Ohio and building coalitions. As she enters her second full term in Congress, she will use that experience to continue the fight for affordable quality health care, jobs that pay fair wages, a strong public education system, and to preserve and protect our democracy for generations to come. Will you join her and be the change we need?

#### One Name, One Market
## **Nvidia brings its founder back, and the S &P 500 jumps 4.7 percent in a day**
_Last week your index fund paid for one company 's turmoil. On Monday it got a good part of the bill back._
The partner above is betting on one executive's track record. On Monday, Wall Street made the same kind of bet, with trillions of dollars behind it.
Nvidia's board voted unanimously to _[bring Jensen Huang back](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/229c3e62-5058-4b15-b469-6c8eb2d61c42?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ as chief executive, eleven days after he resigned. The S&P 500 rose 4.7 percent to 7,237, its strongest session since April 2025. Nvidia climbed about 31 percent, the Nasdaq added 6.5 percent, and the Dow gained nearly 1,450 points.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ce2536d3-092f-4eb4-81b4-4764a1e73b1b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

**[He Turned a $300M Biotech Into a $6.7B Pfizer Deal. Now He's Betting on Concussions.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1211250f-401d-4c78-8100-83ccc44bc7c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
When Amit Munshi took over Arena Pharmaceuticals in 2016, it was a roughly $300M company. Six years later, Pfizer bought it for $6.7B.
Before that, he spotted the lead drug at Kythera, a company he co-founded that later sold to Allergan for $2.1B.
He's also a co-founder of Oxeia Biopharmaceuticals. "The window between 'this could work' and 'the world figures it out' is narrow," Munshi says. "When I see it open, I pay attention."
What caught his eye was OXE-103, an investigational drug based on ghrelin for persistent concussion symptoms. In a small, open-label Phase 2a pilot, 85% of treated patients responded, vs. 33% on standard care alone.
Oxeia also holds the rights to a $200M+ clinical data package from Japanese pharma giant Daiichi Sankyo, with 300+ patients already dosed. And NFL veterans Alex Smith and Richard Sherman, who both know concussions firsthand, have joined the mission. Next up is a 160-patient, placebo-controlled Phase 2b trial.
Join Munshi as an Oxeia shareholder before the 12/9 bonus deadline.

#### **[Revenue Grew From $1 Million to $26 Million](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/81310545-f406-447b-84ce-eb95f538fd4a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The company behind 45 Colombian farms, around 10 million coffee trees, $26 million in 2025 revenue, and products reaching 3,000+ North American stores is giving individual investors a way to get in at the current price.
**Green Coffee Company isn 't a coffee shop concept hoping to become the next Starbucks.**
Think about how many businesses can touch coffee before you buy it.
* A farmer grows the beans.
* An exporter buys them.
* A trader moves them.
* A processor handles them.
* A roaster prepares them.

Eventually, a brand and retailer get the finished product in front of consumers.
**Each business needs to make money along the way.**
**Green Coffee Company was built to handle more of that process itself.** By owning farms, operating proprietary processing facilities, and participating in roasting and distribution, the company can cut out more middlemen and capture more value across the supply chain. _**[See the offering->](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/81310545-f406-447b-84ce-eb95f538fd4a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
Green Coffee Company generated approximately $1 million in revenue in 2021. By 2025, that figure had grown to $26 million.
Then there's Juan Valdez®. Through an exclusive commercial partnership, Green Coffee Company holds rights involving Juan Valdez packaged coffee across U.S. and Canadian retail and institutional channels. Products tied to that relationship are already reaching major retailers including Target and Walgreens.
Green Coffee Company is still private, but its Regulation A offering allows individual investors to participate without being accredited.

#### The Morning Cup
**Coffee is getting cheaper at the source, and the store shelf is starting to notice**
While stocks whipsawed, coffee kept easing. Brazil's growers are bringing in a record crop, and some of that relief has already reached the checkout line.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/be178353-f3ec-4b87-9a8f-6967f674f44b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Brazil's October coffee exports rose 23 percent from a year earlier, and the USDA expects [a record Brazilian crop](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/be4ce1b0-50fc-4051-95f5-846da312db5a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of 71.9 million bags for 2026-27.
Robusta, the cheaper bean behind many instant and canned blends, fell last week to its lowest price since about mid-2024.
At the store, [the coffee line in October's inflation report](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/7f0ef273-a8de-42ac-ad39-38db5fff83eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) fell 3.6 percent in a single month, and roasted coffee dropped 4.6 percent.
One wrinkle: exchange warehouses hold the smallest stock of certified arabica in 27 years, so a bad weather headline from Brazil can still send prices jumping.
Cheaper beans take months to work through roasters and grocers, so the savings arrive a few cents at a time. For a household that brews two pots a day, those cents add up by spring.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ad306af2-28b7-446e-97ba-cc90f8323796?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
#### One Number
**$58.63** is what a classic Thanksgiving dinner for ten costs this year, according to _[the Farm Bureau's annual survey](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/c68535fd-8a36-4be7-bd53-d551b5e2c625?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_, up more than 6 percent and the first increase since the 2022 record of $64.05. The turkey drove most of it: a 16-pound bird averages $23.68, about 10 percent more than last year. High diesel prices pushed up the cost of hauling food from farm to store, so the holiday table carries a small piece of the fuel bill.
#### Why I Led Here
In Army logistics we had a name for a supply line that depends on one bridge: a single point of failure. Planners spent careers building second routes, because the day the bridge goes out is never the day you get to pick.
Last week showed how much of the stock market now runs over one bridge. Over the holiday I plan to look up how much of my own index fund sits in its ten biggest names, then decide calmly whether I am comfortable with that number before the next board meeting decides for me.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/3ca2f541-8871-4518-a389-ec060bd492b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/c3e7de99-8fd1-46b0-b76a-a98972281d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_When the world moves, hold your ground._

* **Iran 's currency plunged on the black market after new U.S. Treasury sanctions** targeted over two dozen exchange houses and alleged front companies tied to the country's "shadow banking" network, with the rial losing roughly 5% of its value against the dollar in a single day.

Ilhan Omar's D.C. home revealed federal prosecutors believe she committed immigration-related crimes though most of the warrant's details, including a 67-page affidavit, remain sealed. Investigators are reportedly examining whether Omar misrepresented her birth year to gain citizenship through her father in 2000 and whether her 2009 marriage to Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, suspected to be her brother, was fraudulent; Omar has said she doesn't believe this "to the knowledge" she has. Judge James Boasberg noted that administration officials' own public comments about the probe, including remarks from VP JD Vance and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin alleging fraud, weakened prosecutors' case for keeping information sealed going forward. Trump orders faster, broader death penalty prosecutions President Donald Trump signed a memo directing AG Todd Blanche to seek including murder of minors, murder during rape or sex trafficking, and kidnapping-related killings, expanding his earlier order covering law enforcement murders and capital crimes by illegal immigrants. | | ---|---|--- The memo also instructs prosecutors to expedite executions, oppose delay tactics, and eliminate unnecessary administrative holdups, signed following a DOJ event condemning California Gov. Gavin Newsom's recent commutation of over 548 death row sentences. The White House criticized Newsom 's move as prioritizing politics over victims, noting Californians have twice rejected ballot measures to abolish the death penalty. Newsom defended his decision as reflecting California's values, calling state-sanctioned executions incompatible with justice in an imperfect legal system. **He has no idea who he's dealing with.**
I didn't come to Congress with a wall of trust funds or a fortune in the bank. I’m an immigrant who grew up in a working-class household. That’s exactly why he’s trying this trick. He thinks working-class leaders can be pushed around and out-spent.
**We cannot let him succeed.**
I am NOT backing down from our constitutional duty to hold the powerful accountable. But as his lawyers and DOJ allies escalate their legal threats against me, I need to ensure we have every resource in place to defend our oversight work, assemble top-tier legal talent, and fight back against these retaliatory attacks.

| On Nov 3, Black state Representative Patricia "Pat" Moore beat her MAGA opponent by .73% in Louisiana's 5th (R+17) forcing a Dec 12 runoff.
Quickly, Dems from across the US rallied around Pat propelling us to raise $1 million in the 1st week of the runoff.
But with our historic midterm win making many complacent, zero national attention, and Thanksgiving around the corner, fundraising has nosedived.
---
| [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001w438-EeqEwZriTc7_bBbz6ApqDv_eLSWJojiPWpVEjoExsmL5X5mhdKGg2bGYMGoAwvWvyomQTfLgYdpjgi4hFyOb4fUOhe6AvjjV99aUiLiYLuJ4prV7_B5158lPSbiNqXnsEmx-KyyJ-WlBvg4hQCR3dFGTyGT7eFtTG686yEUZv9zkhu-I9t6LHsJhNS3uzCAGP1KYInX_aInwVzcUkUP_Fl9jdoEHSODRywcpHEOu8OqdKbgbQ==&c=rSaXUqdV8u21lkGJ85WWq_P6-ZIfhbTVyZ0A7qlOGidnebM0lcr8aA==&ch=yfFJxHLyvGhgwzvO-RxoawGt8fhKQ2448ucttevIka8LNmzc3twR3A==)

What the hell is going on with Mike Rogers?
I mean, he had one thing that seemed to bring him joy, being the Republican Big Dawg in the House Armed Services Committee (HASC), and this week he just walked away from it. Everyone is asking "Why?" and I think I've figured it out... we just need some background.

In the US House of Representatives, members can serve only three terms, or six years, as their party's senior member on committees. Mike Rogers (R-Boeing) shad met the limit. He served as the senior Republican on the Homeland Security Committee from 2019 to 2021. He was the ranking Republican on the HASC from 2021 to 2023, and he's chaired it since 2023.
The HASC was Mike's jam. It brought him nearly a million dollars in campaign contributions from defense contractors; he got to brag about doubling the defense budget to $1.5 trillion a year; he got to toot his horn about how great all this would be for defense contractors in Huntsville and along the Gulf Coast (I guess he knows neither of those places are in his district).
No one was surprised in July when Mike said he would ask GOP leadership in the House for a waiver to stay on as the senior Republican on the HASC. But on November 17, Rogers flipped, telling _Punchbowl News_ , "I'm not going to pursue a waiver... I don't want the position." What happened, Mike? He seemed so sure for the last five months, and then suddenly he walked away.
Here's my guess, and it started three years ago...
Everyone remembers 2023, when the House GOP Caucus couldn't get enough votes to confirm Kevin McCarthy (R-CA) as speaker. After fourteen ballots, Mike Rogers stormed onto the House floor and acted like he wanted to take a swing at the leader of the opposition, Matt Gaetz (R-FL). It seems to have worked. Gaetz coalition began to fall apart, and McCarthy was confirmed. Most people forget that Gaetz was pushing his good friend, Jim Jordan (R-OH), for Speaker.
Ten short months later, in October 2023, McCarthy was out. Jim Jordan's name immediately came up as a strong candidate to replace him as Speaker. Mike Rogers was pretty clear about how he felt. Rogers made several public statements saying he would rather work with the Democrats to elect an acceptable Democrat as Speaker than let Jim Jordan win. Mike Johnson (R-LA) became the next Speaker.
So what does all that have to do with Rogers pulling back his waiver request? On November 10, the House GOP Caucus elected Jim Jordan as the new Minority Leader. Seven days later, Mike Rogers withdrew his waiver request. Twice, Mike Rogers actively campaigned to keep Jim Jordan from being Speaker of the US House of Representatives. Now, Jim Jordan has won, and Mike Rogers is clearly on the wrong side of the most powerful Republican in the House.
Rogers has never really cared about his district. He's never been seen here. He gets a little money for the Anniston Army Depot every now and then, but he has no idea what this district really needs--or he just doesn't care. For years, our Member of Congress has shown no interest in his constituents' welfare. Now, not only is he disinterested, but he has apparently pissed off the House's new GOP leadership. We were never going to get a lot of help from Mike Rogers. Now we're going to get none.
This district has serious needs. Now we can't expect any help from D.C. We'll have to work together to get by until we can get real representation in Congress.

I mean, he had one thing that seemed to bring him joy, being the Republican Big Dawg in the House Armed Services Committee (HASC), and this week he just walked away from it. Everyone is asking "Why?" and I think I've figured it out... we just need some background. Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work. In the US House of Representatives, members can serve only three terms, or six years, as their party's senior member on committees. Mike Rogers (R-Boeing) shad met the limit. He served as the senior Republican on the Homeland Security Committee from 2019 to 2021. He was the ranking Republican on the HASC from 2021 to 2023, and he's chaired it since 2023. The HASC was Mike's jam. It brought him nearly a million dollars in campaign contributions from defense contractors; he got to brag about doubling the defense budget to $1.5 trillion a year; he got to toot his horn about how great all this would be for defense contractors in Huntsville and along the Gulf Coast (I guess he knows neither of those places are in his district). No one was surprised in July when Mike said he would ask GOP leadership in the House for a waiver to stay on as the senior Republican on the HASC. But on November 17, Rogers flipped, telling Punchbowl News , "I'm not going to pursue a waiver... I don't want the position." What happened, Mike? He seemed so sure for the last five months, and then suddenly he walked away. Here's my guess, and it started three years ago... Everyone remembers 2023, when the House GOP Caucus couldn't get enough votes to confirm Kevin McCarthy (R-CA) as speaker. After fourteen ballots, Mike Rogers stormed onto the House floor and acted like he wanted to take a swing at the leader of the opposition, Matt Gaetz (R-FL). It seems to have worked. Gaetz coalition began to fall apart, and McCarthy was confirmed. Most people forget that Gaetz was pushing his good friend, Jim Jordan (R-OH), for Speaker. Ten short months later, in October 2023, McCarthy was out. Jim Jordan's name immediately came up as a strong candidate to replace him as Speaker. Mike Rogers was pretty clear about how he felt. Rogers made several public statements saying he would rather work with the Democrats to elect an acceptable Democrat as Speaker than let Jim Jordan win. Mike Johnson (R-LA) became the next Speaker. So what does all that have to do with Rogers pulling back his waiver request? On November 10, the House GOP Caucus elected Jim Jordan as the new Minority Leader. Seven days later, Mike Rogers withdrew his waiver request. Twice, Mike Rogers actively campaigned to keep Jim Jordan from being Speaker of the US House of Representatives. Now, Jim Jordan has won, and Mike Rogers is clearly on the wrong side of the most powerful Republican in the House. Rogers has never really cared about his district. He's never been seen here. He gets a little money for the Anniston Army Depot every now and then, but he has no idea what this district really needs--or he just doesn't care. For years, our Member of Congress has shown no interest in his constituents' welfare. Now, not only is he disinterested, but he has apparently pissed off the House's new GOP leadership. We were never going to get a lot of help from Mike Rogers. Now we're going to get none. This district has serious needs. Now we can't expect any help from D.C. We'll have to work together to get by until we can get real representation in Congress. THE NEWS YOU NEED TO SEE Alabama Political Reporter:Alabama Power files for $160 million rate cut in 2027 Senator Katie Britt is claiming credit for Alabama Power filing for a $160 million rate cut for next year. That means the average Alabama family will save no more than $50 a year. Of course, Alabama Power will suffer. It could cut into the $1.5 billion in profits they made last year. Alabama Daily News:Sewell, Figures strongly back Jeffries for House speaker In a closed-door vote, the House Democratic Caucus voted 251-11to nominate Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY), virtually guaranteeing he will be elected the next Speaker of the House. If elected, Jeffries will be the first Black Speaker. The Democratic Members of Alabama's House delegation, Reps. Terri Sewell and Shomari Figures, actively supported Jeffries' nomination. Alabama Reflector:State audit finds 'sense of secrecy' at Alabama Department of Corrections An independent audit of the Alabama Department of Corrections (ADOC) found that the agency had "an underlying sense of secrecy." The Alabama Department of Examiners of Public Accounts (ADEPA), an arm of the State Legislature, reported having "great difficulty obtaining requested records from ADOC." ADEPA also stated, "Records that should be readily available at any state agency were not at ADOC. Ultimately, ADEPA had to issue a subpoena to ADOC to obtain certain records." ADOC will go on trial at the end of the month over conditions of the state's men's prisons, a lawsuit brought by the U.S. Department of Justice in 2020. | | ---|---|--- Thanks for reading! _You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. _**Lawyer Up.** _

That’s what I posted on social media late on election night while the results rolled in.

My message echoes what the American people made clear on Election Day. They’re saying they want change. They are tired of the destruction and the corruption of Donald Trump and his administration. [**If holding this administration is worth even $1 to you, I hope you’ll join me by pitching in $1 or more today >>**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/20290?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.11.24_RobertGarcia-LawyerUp_B2_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=4&akid=4058%2E259176%2E5Kuc6H) As Oversight Chair, I’ll be focused on four areas:

1️⃣ **We’re going to take on the Trump crime family.** The grift and corruption from this family are unprecedented in American politics.

2️⃣ **We’ll investigate DHS and the abuses of ICE.** When people are being kidnapped and detained, thrown to the ground, arms broken, that's inhumane, wrong, and the American public is sick of it.

3️⃣ **We will crack down on corporate corruption and consumer pricing.** We’ll investigate corporate donors to the White House ballroom, no-bid contracts like the Reflecting Pool, and other companies that are ripping off the American public.

4️⃣ **We’ll get to the bottom of the Epstein Case.** We’ll pursue accountability and justice for survivors and focus on transparency, regardless of wealth, power, or political affiliation.

So if you took part in any of these crimes against the American people, my message is simple: Lawyer Up.

The American people made their choice, and they rejected Trump’s corruption. But taking on this apparatus takes resources, grit, and grassroots power.
