Breaking: After setting more than $750 million on fire in the 2026 midterms, Trump and Elon may be about to flood the final race of 2026, Louisiana’s 5th District, with MAGA cash.
This is Rep. Patricia “Pat” Moore (D-LA). Against all odds, I lead by 0.73% in one of the reddest districts in America, and now I’m headed to a Dec. 12 runoff.
That has MAGA rattled.
This seat is their last line of defense in ‘26, and losing it would be one more humiliation they can’t afford.
That’s why we’re hearing that Trump and Elon’s money machine is eyeing this race, and that Musk’s super PAC could jump into this runoff to bail out another struggling Republican.
If they come in, we’ll be outgunned like never before. We spent every dollar we had just to get here.
But here’s what Trump and Elon can’t buy:
They can’t buy a daughter of Monroe who has spent 19 years serving this community, first on the Ouachita Parish Police Jury and now in the state House.
And they can’t stop us from making history. On Dec. 12, I’m ready to become the first Black woman Louisiana has EVER sent to Congress.

clean_body: The other side is playing the long game. | = Peter, Did you see the latest from The Atlantic? = = | = Let's talk about what happens after a blue wave. A lot of people assume that once the votes are counted, the hard part is over. We get to exhale. We get to catch up on sleep. We get to tune out for a while. The most extreme Republicans are counting on exactly that. Because here's what they see when they look at our blue wave: The first step in a six-year plan to take over this country and roll back our rights beyond anything we could imagine. They aren't rolling over. They aren't giving up. They're getting more extreme. They're regrouping, recruiting, and organizing for the long haul, and they're betting that Democratic supporters like you will get comfortable, get distracted, and stop showing up. We refuse to play along. Winning big during this year's midterms doesn’t mean we can let our guard down. Not when the other side is playing the long game. We’re building capacity for what will be one of the most important years in the history of this organization.
#

Friend,
As much as we wish we could take some time off this holiday season, we can’t.
But we’re not complaining.
We’ll go into 2027 with a historic majority in Congress and a staggering number of allied governors and state legislatures. Frankly, we’ve never had an opportunity like this. And that means we have a lot of work to do.
We’re building capacity for what will be one of the most important years in the history of this organization. And with the Supreme Court set to hear arguments about the constitutionality of assault weapons bans in early December, we need to be ready.
So, we’re asking you for $5.
Yes, just $5.
$5 because gun violence is still the leading cause of death for American kids.
$5 because some Supreme Court justices have already voiced their support for striking down the assault weapons ban.
And yes, $5 because GIFFORDS is one of the only organizations in the country that can do something to end this crisis.
The ball is in your court now. And we’re humbly asking you:
[**Please, make a donation of $5 (or more, if you can afford it) to GIFFORDS PAC.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261124-1-b&t=1&akid=12105%2E3935704%2EcWMbqD)

## MaineCare Fraud Storm Brewing
The welfare fraud that emerged throughout 2026 is only the tip of the iceberg. As the 133rd State Legislature convenes in December, and elected officials contemplate how to deal with a $1.35 billion shortfall, the fraud problem will only become more apparent. Prudent lawmakers would try to get a handle on the magnitude of the fraud epidemic that is going to crash down on the state like a tidal wave, because it will have severe implications for Maine's Medicaid funding, as well as the thousands of lives impacted directly by fraudulent and abusive care.
November's elections may have short-circuited the House Oversight Committee's probe into DHHS, but it will not deter the CMS Office of Inspector General, the Department of Justice, or the FBI from examining fraud conspiracies and whether public corruption contributed to those fraud conspiracies. At the center of the fraud crisis will be Maine's home- and community-based services -- that is, services provided in residential settings. In particular, MaineCare Section 21 and Section 29. Both of these programs provide long-term 24/7 care for disabled adults. Of the most massive MaineCare frauds brought down to date, all of them were residential care: Paradise Residential Services, We Care LLC, Beyond Residential Care, and Quality Care Access. Mark my words: This is just the tip of the iceberg, and the fraud conspiracy will reach well beyond a few scummy scammers.
As if waking up from a campaign-induced bender, Mainers are coming to terms with the loss of more than $500 million in congressionally directed spending that will befall Maine because voters opted to send Troy Jackson to Washington, D.C., instead of Sen. Susan Collins. But a less obvious consequence of Collins' retirement: The Trump White House no longer has any reason to hold back from hammering Maine's compliance with federally funded welfare programs. That hammer is coming.
### Fewer Enrollees, Bigger Bills: MaineCare's Cost Keeps Climbing
The Mills administration spent nearly $5.5 billion on MaineCare and related programs last fiscal year while the Medicaid/CHIP caseload fell. Four months into the new fiscal year, the main General Fund account used to pay providers was running 33 percent above its allotted weekly pace -- meaning the realized structural gap is yawning, not closing.
Augusta has already been through two rounds of MaineCare funding trouble in as many years. The latest expenditure reports prepared by DHHS give taxpayers good reason to ask what, exactly, those additional appropriations fixed. Over the last two fiscal years, MaineCare welfare spending increased $773.6 million, or 16.4 percent. Average monthly Medicaid/CHIP enrollment declined by about 28,105, or 6.7 percent.
For state taxpayers, the spending increase has been steeper than the overall program's growth. The expenditure report's "Total MaineCare State-Funded Activity" line, covering the General Fund and Fund for a Healthy Maine within the regular payment-cycle accounts, rose from $1.188 billion in fiscal 2024 to $1.565 billion in fiscal 2026. That is an additional $377.8 million, or 31.8 percent, in two years.
As Democratic lawmakers scramble to find more money to steal from the productive class and shovel into the welfare furnace, no one is asking: Are Mainers getting healthier from all this welfare spending? Or are we just helping a generation of fraudsters get their new Mercedes-Benz G-Wagons?
I think you know the answer...

### [ICE Releases Ecuadorian Teen Following Federal Judge's Ruling Over Warrantless Maine Arrest](https://substack.com/redirect/66ad784a-db30-4701-89ef-71a110405035?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
An 18-year-old from Ecuador is out of ICE custody after U.S. District Judge Stacey Neumann ruled that agents never made the individualized assessment the Constitution requires before taking him in. It started Monday, Nov. 16, when a Border Patrol agent pulled over a van in Livermore Falls. Six of the eight occupants were arrested. Court papers use the pseudonym "Juan Perez" for the teen, who entered the country in November 2024 -- allegedly at age 16 -- as an unaccompanied minor and got Special Immigrant Juvenile classification a year later. (For the uninitiated, there's a whole lot of "16-year-olds" who are actually in their 20s because posing as a minor gets an illegal alien preferential treatment -- or, I should say, more preferential treatment than is already bestowed upon the illegal alien protected class.)
Publicly available information still doesn't say what happened to the five other people arrested in that van, and nobody knows yet whether the Justice Department will appeal.
### [Lawmakers Question Maine Community Foundation on $1.9 million Sent to Lewiston Nonprofits](https://substack.com/redirect/8598a2ba-e119-4e60-8033-84d57b20aec2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
If you gave to the Lewiston shooting fund, you're owed an answer on where the money went. The Legislature's Government Oversight Committee questioned the Maine Community Foundation's leaders Wednesday, Nov. 18. After more than an hour of questions, the foundation's president gave a half-hearted apology. In the end, the GOC voted not to investigate further.
By the foundation's count, it raised about $6.6 million after the Oct. 25, 2023, shooting. It reports $4,696,067 to 162 victims, survivors and relatives, and $1,900,132 to 29 nonprofits through a separate fund, $65,522 each. It did not require those 29 to file full spending reports and says most reported voluntarily. Deborah Ellwood, the foundation's president and CEO, told the committee donors could choose which fund got their money and that the foundation waived administrative and processing fees. Lawmakers wanted to know why that split wasn't spelled out for the families.
At one point Ellwood channeled her inner Hillary Clinton: "What difference do you think that would make?"
Well, for one: No one would have donated to the scam Somali nonprofits. No one would have donated to any fund that had NGO scammers on the steering committee. No one would have donated to a fund that was going to be distributed to alleged gun criminals, killers, and welfare scammers. That's a pretty big difference, Deb!

### [Cuban Nationals Caught Cannabis Trafficking in Rural Maine](https://substack.com/redirect/a8e3a1e0-77ed-4443-bcac-0ade17888f57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

All three men were at the property when agents arrived.

### [Chinese Nationals Living in NH Plead Guilty to $2.8 Million Fraud Scheme](https://substack.com/redirect/d4050cbc-5025-4d2e-89c9-eeb84228abca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Two Chinese nationals who are married and live in Bedford, N.H., Zhong Chen, 43, and Sijia Guo, 32, admitted Wednesday to conspiracy to commit wire fraud. The scheme took in $2.8 million, according to our story, much of it from elderly victims across the country. Victims were told to mail packages holding between $5,000 and $30,000 in cash to addresses the couple controlled, and one Louisiana man sent $10,000 to buy a puppy.
The couple also used the Chinese messaging app WeChat to collect stolen card numbers from other Chinese nationals, then bought money orders and gift cards at post offices across New England. On one day, June 13, 2025, they used stolen cards for 16 money orders totaling $14,600 at six post offices in Massachusetts. Each faces up to 20 years in prison, and sentencing is set for March 2027.
### [Electric Bills Set to Rise Next Year Following Maine PUC Approval of Standard Offer Increase](https://substack.com/redirect/57f9b675-f795-4889-953d-449021453a01?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Next year's electricity supply charge is going up. The Public Utilities Commission set the 2027 standard offer on Tuesday: $4.99 a month more for the average Central Maine Power customer who uses 550 kWh, and $2.30 more for the average Versant Maine Public District customer at 500 kWh. Households got hit for about $11 a month last year. This charge pays the companies that generate the power, so none of it goes to CMP or Versant.
### [Lewiston Eyes April 13 Election to Replace Harriman as Councilor; Apologizes for Silence on Allegations](https://substack.com/redirect/d88d3cd9-63e1-42ef-b7c6-87b9d93f7930?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Lewiston's Ward 3 may have no voice on the City Council until spring. Councilors agreed on Nov. 17 that they want an April 13 special election to fill the seat of Scott Harriman, who also sits in the Maine House. Harriman submitted his resignation Nov. 6, effective Dec. 4, after allegations from a former tenant that he denies. The council is expected to make the date official at a special meeting Nov. 24.
Councilor Bret Martel said the council "fell short as a leadership body." The council announced no investigation. The April ballot would also elect six members of a new nine-member Charter Commission. Applications for the three seats the council appoints are due at 5:30 p.m. Nov. 24.
### [Our Waldoboro Exclusive: A Teenager Killed, a Niece Who Says She Begged Authorities to Act](https://substack.com/redirect/2d4a1445-b13f-4980-83b2-bca9fbb7d4f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The driver charged in the Waldoboro hit-and-run that killed a teenager has had his first day in court. Gifford Campbell, 53, appeared by Zoom Friday in West Bath District Court. Bail was set at $150,000, and he is due back Jan. 25, 2027, unless a grand jury indicts him sooner. The charges are manslaughter, OUI of drugs resulting in death, and leaving the scene of a fatal accident. He hasn't been convicted of anything. In an exclusive interview with Joe Sokol, the niece says she had been begging police and local authorities to do something about what she calls a known drug house in the neighborhood. Campbell was high on drugs when he hit the teen.

Police arrested Katie Spencer White, president and CEO of the Mid-Maine Homeless Shelter, in Brunswick on Nov. 20, the Morning Sentinel reports. She is charged with tampering with a witness, a Class C felony, and obstructing government administration. According to a police affidavit, the case began in August when a guest reported his methadone stolen, and White told staff not to speak with police. White cited federal confidentiality rules for substance-use records. She had no comment on the charges and is barred from the shelter as a condition of bail.

MaineCare Fraud Storm Brewing The welfare fraud that emerged throughout 2026 is only the tip of the iceberg. As the 133rd State Legislature convenes in December, and elected officials contemplate how to deal with a $1.35 billion shortfall, the fraud problem will only become more apparent. Prudent lawmakers would try to get a handle on the magnitude of the fraud epidemic that is going to crash down on the state like a tidal wave, because it will have severe implications for Maine's Medicaid funding, as well as the thousands of lives impacted directly by fraudulent and abusive care. November's elections may have short-circuited the House Oversight Committee's probe into DHHS, but it will not deter the CMS Office of Inspector General, the Department of Justice, or the FBI from examining fraud conspiracies and whether public corruption contributed to those fraud conspiracies. At the center of the fraud crisis will be Maine's home- and community-based services -- that is, services provided in residential settings. In particular, MaineCare Section 21 and Section 29. Both of these programs provide long-term 24/7 care for disabled adults. Of the most massive MaineCare frauds brought down to date, all of them were residential care: Paradise Residential Services, We Care LLC, Beyond Residential Care, and Quality Care Access. Mark my words: This is just the tip of the iceberg, and the fraud conspiracy will reach well beyond a few scummy scammers. As if waking up from a campaign-induced bender, Mainers are coming to terms with the loss of more than $500 million in congressionally directed spending that will befall Maine because voters opted to send Troy Jackson to Washington, D.C., instead of Sen. Susan Collins. But a less obvious consequence of Collins' retirement: The Trump White House no longer has any reason to hold back from hammering Maine's compliance with federally funded welfare programs. That hammer is coming. Fewer Enrollees, Bigger Bills: MaineCare's Cost Keeps Climbing The Mills administration spent nearly $5.5 billion on MaineCare and related programs last fiscal year while the Medicaid/CHIP caseload fell. Four months into the new fiscal year, the main General Fund account used to pay providers was running 33 percent above its allotted weekly pace -- meaning the realized structural gap is yawning, not closing. Augusta has already been through two rounds of MaineCare funding trouble in as many years. The latest expenditure reports prepared by DHHS give taxpayers good reason to ask what, exactly, those additional appropriations fixed. Over the last two fiscal years, MaineCare welfare spending increased $773.6 million, or 16.4 percent. Average monthly Medicaid/CHIP enrollment declined by about 28,105, or 6.7 percent. For state taxpayers, the spending increase has been steeper than the overall program's growth. The expenditure report's "Total MaineCare State-Funded Activity" line, covering the General Fund and Fund for a Healthy Maine within the regular payment-cycle accounts, rose from $1.188 billion in fiscal 2024 to $1.565 billion in fiscal 2026. That is an additional $377.8 million, or 31.8 percent, in two years. As Democratic lawmakers scramble to find more money to steal from the productive class and shovel into the welfare furnace, no one is asking: Are Mainers getting healthier from all this welfare spending? Or are we just helping a generation of fraudsters get their new Mercedes-Benz G-Wagons? I think you know the answer... The fraud will continue until the investigations get better. Support our work by subscribing today: RobinsonReport.Substack.com Lewiston residents filed three police reports over what happened during early voting at City Hall. The city released two weeks of surveillance video in response to a records request, then refused the final week, citing Maine election law and "advice" from the Secretary of State's Office. Regardless, the video already in the public domain shows leftist groups brazenly violating Maine's electioneering statutes while Somali "translators" fill out ballots on behalf of illiterate migrants -- who we're supposed to believe are naturalized U.S. citizens. U.S. Attorney Andrew Benson confirmed in late October that his office was reviewing early-voting footage. An 18-year-old from Ecuador is out of ICE custody after U.S. District Judge Stacey Neumann ruled that agents never made the individualized assessment the Constitution requires before taking him in. It started Monday, Nov. 16, when a Border Patrol agent pulled over a van in Livermore Falls. Six of the eight occupants were arrested. Court papers use the pseudonym "Juan Perez" for the teen, who entered the country in November 2024 -- allegedly at age 16 -- as an unaccompanied minor and got Special Immigrant Juvenile classification a year later. (For the uninitiated, there's a whole lot of "16-year-olds" who are actually in their 20s because posing as a minor gets an illegal alien preferential treatment -- or, I should say, more preferential treatment than is already bestowed upon the illegal alien protected class.) Publicly available information still doesn't say what happened to the five other people arrested in that van, and nobody knows yet whether the Justice Department will appeal. If you gave to the Lewiston shooting fund, you're owed an answer on where the money went. The Legislature's Government Oversight Committee questioned the Maine Community Foundation's leaders Wednesday, Nov. 18. After more than an hour of questions, the foundation's president gave a half-hearted apology. In the end, the GOC voted not to investigate further. By the foundation's count, it raised about $6.6 million after the Oct. 25, 2023, shooting. It reports $4,696,067 to 162 victims, survivors and relatives, and $1,900,132 to 29 nonprofits through a separate fund, $65,522 each. It did not require those 29 to file full spending reports and says most reported voluntarily. Deborah Ellwood, the foundation's president and CEO, told the committee donors could choose which fund got their money and that the foundation waived administrative and processing fees. Lawmakers wanted to know why that split wasn't spelled out for the families. At one point Ellwood channeled her inner Hillary Clinton: "What difference do you think that would make?" Well, for one: No one would have donated to the scam Somali nonprofits. No one would have donated to any fund that had NGO scammers on the steering committee. No one would have donated to a fund that was going to be distributed to alleged gun criminals, killers, and welfare scammers. That's a pretty big difference, Deb! A judge has ruled for us in our suit against Bangor police. The records at issue involve two brothers who work in home health care and were arrested for drunk driving in 2025. In May, we filed a Freedom of Access Act request for every incident report involving the pair. Bangor police sent back reports in which every name was redacted, the brothers' included, so we couldn't tell whether they were the reports we'd asked for. We sued to get the names restored. We'll have more details as soon as the Bangor Police Department gets around to complying. Lewiston's mayor makes $7,000 a year under city rules. Campaign records show Carl Sheline reported another $20,650 in loans in the 2026 campaign, which is almost three years of that salary. His campaign's December 2023 filing listed a $40,080.13 outstanding loan balance after he advanced another $15,467.85, with no repayments or forgiveness reported in that period. There are a lot of mysteries in Lewiston. Sheline's midnight wanderings around Lisbon Street and Bartlett Street, why he'd spend so much money for a per diem mayoral gig -- so many mysteries. Federal agents seized more than 200 marijuana plants and about 120 pounds of processed marijuana from a property in Embden after a search Thursday, according to a criminal complaint filed Friday in U.S. District Court in Bangor. Lester M. Fuentes Gonzalez, Hector A. Roque De Escobar and Osvaldo Guillermo Gamez Fernandez are each charged with conspiring to manufacture more than 100 marijuana plants and with manufacturing more than 100 plants. Court documents describe all three as Cuban citizens. An affidavit by Homeland Security Investigations Special Agent Pierre Mathieu says authorities believe the operation had been running since at least January. All three men were at the property when agents arrived. | | | | ---|---|--- | Nov 20 | Moises Alejandro Martinez Gutierrez, 29, of Venezuela, pleaded guilty in federal court in Boston to two counts: conspiracy to commit bank theft and damaging a protected computer. Prosecutors say he is a member of Tren de Aragua and was arrested in Augusta after a failed ATM jackpotting attempt on Feb. 5. They also tie him to five other attempted or completed jackpottings in Connecticut, Rhode Island, Massachusetts and New Hampshire. Jackpotting means loading malware into a machine so it empties itself. Two Chinese nationals who are married and live in Bedford, N.H., Zhong Chen, 43, and Sijia Guo, 32, admitted Wednesday to conspiracy to commit wire fraud. The scheme took in $2.8 million, according to our story, much of it from elderly victims across the country. Victims were told to mail packages holding between $5,000 and $30,000 in cash to addresses the couple controlled, and one Louisiana man sent $10,000 to buy a puppy. The couple also used the Chinese messaging app WeChat to collect stolen card numbers from other Chinese nationals, then bought money orders and gift cards at post offices across New England. On one day, June 13, 2025, they used stolen cards for 16 money orders totaling $14,600 at six post offices in Massachusetts. Each faces up to 20 years in prison, and sentencing is set for March 2027. Next year's electricity supply charge is going up. The Public Utilities Commission set the 2027 standard offer on Tuesday: $4.99 a month more for the average Central Maine Power customer who uses 550 kWh, and $2.30 more for the average Versant Maine Public District customer at 500 kWh. Households got hit for about $11 a month last year. This charge pays the companies that generate the power, so none of it goes to CMP or Versant. Lewiston's Ward 3 may have no voice on the City Council until spring. Councilors agreed on Nov. 17 that they want an April 13 special election to fill the seat of Scott Harriman, who also sits in the Maine House. Harriman submitted his resignation Nov. 6, effective Dec. 4, after allegations from a former tenant that he denies. The council is expected to make the date official at a special meeting Nov. 24. Councilor Bret Martel said the council "fell short as a leadership body." The council announced no investigation. The April ballot would also elect six members of a new nine-member Charter Commission. Applications for the three seats the council appoints are due at 5:30 p.m. Nov. 24. The driver charged in the Waldoboro hit-and-run that killed a teenager has had his first day in court. Gifford Campbell, 53, appeared by Zoom Friday in West Bath District Court. Bail was set at $150,000, and he is due back Jan. 25, 2027, unless a grand jury indicts him sooner. The charges are manslaughter, OUI of drugs resulting in death, and leaving the scene of a fatal accident. He hasn't been convicted of anything. In an exclusive interview with Joe Sokol, the niece says she had been begging police and local authorities to do something about what she calls a known drug house in the neighborhood. Campbell was high on drugs when he hit the teen. Videos from @TheMaineWire on X The Maine Community Foundation at the hearing. Lawmakers question the foundation over the Lewiston shooting donations. Rep. Adam Lee (D-Auburn) talked tough but ended up siding with his tribe. Maine Wire TV If you're reading this, you probably get Maine Wire TV delivered via Substack. But you can also watch us on Facebook, X, and. You can subscribe on Apple or Spotify, too! Here's the Nov. 23 episode... Around the Web Police arrested Katie Spencer White, president and CEO of the Mid-Maine Homeless Shelter, in Brunswick on Nov. 20, the Morning Sentinel reports. She is charged with tampering with a witness, a Class C felony, and obstructing government administration. According to a police affidavit, the case began in August when a guest reported his methadone stolen, and White told staff not to speak with police. White cited federal confidentiality rules for substance-use records. She had no comment on the charges and is barred from the shelter as a condition of bail. The Robinson Report is reader-supported. # How to Scan on iPhone Using Notes App
This nifty trick is an excellent way to make a digitized copy of any physical document that you can save to your phone, or quickly send via messages, email, or AirDrop, depending on your needs. In this tip, we’ll cover how to scan on iPhone using the Notes app.
## Why You’ll Love This Tip
* **Scan and store documents in your iPhone’s Notes app.**
* **Easily convert paper documents to PDF files for sharing over email, text, etc.**
* **This can be better than taking a picture of a document, because the scan function automatically adjusts your photo settings to be optimized for a printed document.**

## How to Scan a Document on iPhone
**System Requirements** _This tip was performed on an iPhone 17 Pro Max running iOS 26.6, but it also works with iOS 27. Find out how to update to the[latest version of iOS](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-262257-8632302-1a502c0977-9vdd0908b2)._The scanning feature isn’t just a photograph of a piece of paper. It actually uses special software to flatten and standardize the pages and uses Live Text to allow you to physically copy and paste words or numbers from the document into any text field. To discover more iPhone hidden gems, don't forget to check out our free [Tip of the Day](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-262257-8632303-1390fbabb5-9vdd0908b2) newsletter. Now, here’s how to scan documents on iPhone:
1. On your iPhone, open **Notes**.

|
---
2. Open a new note by tapping the **New Note button** in the bottom right or open an existing note.

---
3. Tap the **Attachment icon**.

---
### Enjoying Your Tip of the Day?
If you'd like to learn more about iPhone Life's premium paid subscription, [click here](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-262257-3310152-520a1152a1-9vdd0908b2)
4. Tap **Scan Documents**.

---
5. Position the document so that it is entirely in view and the camera will automatically take the photo.

---
6. You can also take the photo manually by pushing the shutter button.

---
7. If you do it manually, you'll see the option to **Keep** the scan or **Retake** if it is blurry or cut off.

---
8. You can continue scanning by repeating the steps above. Sometimes you need to move the camera completely away from your document, or it will keep automatically taking photos. Tap the **checkmark icon** to save.

---
9. To review your scans, tap the **Gallery icon**.

---
10. Because the pictures take automatically, you may accidentally get a picture you didn't want to save. To delete a scan, tap the thumbnail for the image you want to delete.

---
11. Tap the **more icon** in the middle of the thumbnail.

---
12. From the dropdown menu, tap **Delete Page**.

---
13. If you want to send your scanned pages, tap the **Share button** in the top right corner.

---
14. From here, you can choose where and how you'd like to share your scanned image.

---

And that's how to scan with iPhone's Notes app! Being able to scan documents with iPhone and store them in my Notes app, with the addition of the built-in password protection already offered by Notes, is the perfect way to eliminate traditional filing systems and keep all my important documents safe and in one place. If you'd rather [scan documents with iPhone's Files app](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-262257-8632304-01d0ac49cb-9vdd0908b2), you can do that too.

name: Justin Riemer - RITE President
subject: RITE Urges Supreme Court to Resolve Circuit Split Threatening States' Power to Secure Voter Registration
body:
|
---
| |
---
| | **RITE Urges Supreme Court to Resolve Circuit Split Threatening States’ Power to Secure Voter Registration ** **WASHINGTON, D.C.** — Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections (RITE), an organization dedicated to protecting the rule of law in elections, has joined the Republican National Committee in filing an [amicus brief](https://us.list-manage.com/OTbVnMH3rWt?e=ea91f782ea&c2id=bf38de461872f35bd013169f413b699e) in _Jester v. Get Loud Arkansas_ urging the U.S. Supreme Court to review and reverse a decision of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit blocking Arkansas’s requirement that voter registration applicants sign their forms by hand. In March, the Eighth Circuit upheld a preliminary injunction blocking the rule, acknowledging that it was parting ways with a Fifth Circuit decision that upheld Texas’s nearly identical requirement. “Having to sign your own voter registration form is not a civil rights violation,” said RITE President and CEO Justin Riemer. “The Fifth Circuit got this right in 2023. After the Eighth Circuit’s decision, the same commonsense rule is valid in Texas and blocked in Arkansas, and only the Supreme Court can fix that.” The brief makes three arguments. First, the federal courts of appeals are divided over the meaning of the Civil Rights Act’s materiality provision, leaving some States free to enforce voter-registration rules that others are barred from enforcing. Second, a handwritten signature is a traditional and important way to validate a registration application. It confirms that the applicant is a real person who is who she says she is, deters and detects fraud, and promotes public confidence in elections. Signing by hand, with perjury warnings in front of the applicant, also discourages false statements in a way an electronic signature does not. Third, a handwritten signature is “material” under the statute’s ordinary meaning because it matters in determining whether an applicant is qualified to vote. “Left-wing activist groups have spent years trying to turn a 1964 civil rights statute into a tool for second-guessing routine election administration policies,” said Riemer. “States are entitled to decide that a voter registration, like a tax return or a ballot petition, deserves a real signature. We urge the Court to take this case and say so.” RITE and RITE PAC have been leaders in defending commonsense laws attacked by progressive organizations using the materiality provision. RITE previously filed a brief with the Eighth Circuit in this Arkansas case in 2024. RITE PAC has supported the Pasco County Republican Party’s intervention in another materiality case that is currently pending in the Eleventh Circuit. In 2024, the Third Circuit agreed with RITE that Pennsylvania can enforce its requirement that voters sign and date their mail-ballot envelopes, following an earlier RITE win in the Pennsylvania Supreme Court. RITE has also defended Wisconsin’s absentee-ballot witness requirement against a materiality challenge. ###

This campaign began with a simple idea: Bobby was tired of South Texas politicians putting themselves before the communities they represent. It shouldn't feel impossible to grow up here, find a good job, buy a home, and raise a family.
Bobby believed in that idea so much that he retired from his 30-year music career. Here's how he put it:
_" I do music for me because I enjoy it, but when you're serving, it's not for you. It's for other people, and I think my life would be complete that way."_

name: Rep Kevin Mullin
subject: Heartfelt Gratitude.
body:
A Historic Election Night.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/fd0937eef19c/join-me-rep-diana-degette-for-lunch-in-ca-17667815?e=feea60f246)
---
|
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/18MLavZk4iM?e=feea60f246&c2id=eff6f64158732e8851993770f57c9616)
| |
### Dear Peter,

In the days since election night, I've reflected on all that we've accomplished together since you first elected me to Congress in 2022. It’s been four years since you entrusted me to fill the historic shoes of my mentor, Jackie Speier. One sentiment that continues to stand above all others, is gratitude.

It’s one of the greatest honors of my life to serve you in Congress. Your encouragement and commitment to our shared values is what drives me everyday to continue delivering results for the constituents of CA-15.

The results of this election represent an extraordinary moment for our nation and a powerful reminder of what is possible when we are united around a shared belief that we can build something better. The voters of San Mateo County and parts of San Francisco County supported my candidacy in a decisive 80% victory. I am humbled by these results and am honored to have earned every single vote.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/NI1RtfQOLCF?e=feea60f246&c2id=eff6f64158732e8851993770f57c9616)
| |

Across the country, voters sent a strong message to Donald Trump and his extreme Republicans in Congress: No more division. No more chaos. No more corruption. As a result, Democrats secured majorities in the U.S. House and U.S. Senate, ushering in a generational turnover in Congress.

Here in California, Prop 50 provided voters the opportunity to elect a slate of new Democrats to Congress, adding five net gain seats toward House Democrat’s majority, and expanding California’s representation to 25% of the House Democratic Caucus. I was proud to support these California candidates, and look forward to working closely with them to deliver results for the Golden State.

But a seat in Congress belongs to the people - not any one Member. These results are a shared achievement for every person who knocked on a door, made a phone call, volunteered, or contributed what they could. This moment belongs to the families, workers, students, and community leaders who refused to sit on the sidelines because they believed that our future was worth fighting for.

However, winning an election is not the finish line. These victories provide my House Democratic colleagues and me with an urgent responsibility to deliver material change for all Americans, regardless of party.

The challenges before us are enormous. Our work ahead must strengthen the guardrails of democracy, defend American freedoms, and restore faith in a federal government that rejects corruption. We must build an economy that works for everyone so that every family has a fair shot at achieving the American Dream. Above all, we have a responsibility to ensure the next generation inherits a country that is more prosperous, compassionate, and hopeful than the one we know today.
---
| [JOIN THE FIGHT](https://us.list-manage.com/5SbyIpJvpTB?e=feea60f246&c2id=eff6f64158732e8851993770f57c9616)
---
| |

The true measure of our success will not be the elections we win, but the future we leave behind. I know the road ahead won't be easy. Progress rarely is. But if this election has reminded me of anything, it's that there is no challenge too great when we are united by the belief that America's best days can still be ahead of us.

But that work starts now. As we approach the 120th Congress, I carry an earnest determination, steadfast humility, and unwavering sense of purpose into the work ahead. Thank you again for your ongoing support, and I look forward to continuing to fight for our future together.
---
| [JOIN THE FIGHT](https://us.list-manage.com/13TN8fk1dQF?e=feea60f246&c2id=eff6f64158732e8851993770f57c9616)
---
| |

With heartfelt gratitude,

### Rep. Kevin Mullin
###

### Congressman, CA-15

Tareq Abu Adhra fortifies a side of his makeshift shelter with sandbags to protect from Israeli gunfire, in the Bir 19 encampment in Khan Younis. November 18, 2026. Screenshot of video by Mohamed Ahmed.
_Story by Mohamed Ahmed and Sharif Abdel Kouddous_
KHAN YOUNIS, Gaza Strip--Nofal Al-Akhras filled another empty flour sack with sand, tied off the top, and heaved it onto the other bags lining the outside of his tent in the Bir 19 area of the southern Gaza Strip. A displacement camp in a desolate sandy expanse west of Khan Younis, Bir 19 lies close to the yellow line where occupying Israeli troops are stationed. Al-Akhras stacked the sandbags three high, at about waist level, among drying laundry hung on a sagging clothesline, forming a makeshift barrier--a desperate attempt to protect himself and his family from Israeli gunfire.
"Every day, around the clock, we are caught off guard by stray, deadly bullets fired indiscriminately," he told Drop Site News. "We have lost many loved ones who were martyred by stray bullets striking displacement tents for no reason whatsoever. We had no choice but to collect empty flour sacks, as you can see, and fill them with sand to build protective barriers to shield our children, our families, and our loved ones from the stray bullets."
Al-Akhras is not alone. Many families in Bir 19 have taken to placing sandbags on the sides of their tents that face east toward the Israeli soldiers. Palestinians in Gaza, already struggling to survive genocidal conditions imposed by Israel--with multiple displacements, inadequate shelter, a lack of protection from the winter cold, storms and flooding, shortages of food and medicine, a lack of sanitation, and near daily aerial attacks--find themselves having to crouch behind sandbags to avoid flying Israeli bullets.
Outside a nearby tent, a group of three children, no more than five or six years old, stood holding open a large flour sack as an older boy slowly filled it with shovelfuls of sand before struggling to stack it on some two dozen others lining two sides of their tent. Inside another tent, several sandbags were stacked at the head of each mattress. Two children lay on their backs watching a video with their heads propped up on a pillow against the bulging sacks.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/56ca2efd-4173-451b-bd32-50d291e8a14b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### Families use sacks filled with sand to protect their tents and shelters from Israeli gunfire in Bir 19, Khan Younis on November 18, 2026. Video by Mohamed Ahmed.
Many of the families in Bir 19 were displaced from Rafah, the southernmost city in the Gaza Strip, which was invaded by the Israeli military in May 2024 and subsequently completely depopulated and razed to the ground.
"When the Israeli army entered Rafah, they ordered us to evacuate the city and move to safe areas. We came to these 'safe areas' and settled here, but after the Israeli army took control of Rafah, they began subjecting us to indiscriminate gunfire every single day," Tareq Abu Adhra told Drop Site. He worked with his daughter to fortify a line of sandbags outside his makeshift shelter, made of tape and corrugated metal sheets.
"Every day, we hear bullets hitting the metal sheets and our tents. Our neighbors have been wounded. A child was martyred, a young man was killed two days ago, and a woman who was related to me was killed. Children are being killed in schools," he added. "This is what life is like for us in Bir 19 every day. So we decided to build protective barriers to shield ourselves. When we go to sleep at night, we sleep behind these barriers out of fear of the gunfire."
Bir 19 camp residents pointed out multiple bullet holes in the sides of tents. A sheet of corrugated metal at one makeshift shelter was riddled with bullet holes. Another tent had a thick barrier built along one side using a patchwork of rebar covered with tarp that was filled with sand about one meter thick.
"When we arrived here, we found that this was the worst place in the entire Gaza Strip when it comes to stray gunfire," Abdul Rahman Abu Adhra told Drop Site. "Just a week ago, a woman from our family was martyred when a bullet struck her as she was walking. That's why we built these barriers, to protect ourselves and our children."
"People just want to live. These are peaceful people but the Israelis aren't--they won't leave anyone alone, not civilians, not women, not children, not the elderly," he continued. "There's barely a kilometer between us and the Israelis, and we're trapped between them and the sea. If they advance any further, God help us. There will be nowhere left for us to go."
Israel has continued its near daily attacks despite a so-called ceasefire it signed over a year ago, in October 2025. Since then, nearly 1,700 Palestinians have been killed in airstrikes, shelling, and shootings by the Israeli military. Israel has also steadily encroached further west in violation of the agreement, moving from controlling 53% of the enclave to close to 70%, taking over more Palestinian land and corralling the entirety of Gaza's population onto less than a third of the territory. Many of the shootings occur close to Israel's line of control, where Israeli troops are stationed alongside newly built military bases.
On November 17, six-year-old Eyas Al-Namnam was shot and killed inside a tent east of Deir al-Balah in central Gaza. According to his family, Eyas had just woken up, started eating, and was doing his homework when his mother asked him to go to his aunt's nearby tent to finish his work. He was accompanied by his older brother and younger sister when Israeli forces opened fire.
"They hadn't even reached the entrance of the tent. His older brother went inside and then his little sister. His cousin told his older brother to sit down. His older brother sat down and Eyas was still standing. Then three shots were fired at him. Two bullets struck the ground and one hit him in the chest," another of Eyas's older brothers, Abdul Karim Al-Namnam, told Drop Site just hours after the incident. He spoke standing in the morgue as Eyas's small body wrapped in a white shroud and plastic body bag lay on a metal shelf beside him. "We were displaced from Gaza City. We fled from the north to the south, looking for safety. But there is no safety. There is no safety anywhere. Ceasefire? What ceasefire? There is shooting twenty-four hours a day. There is no peace at all. I wish there were some calm. At night, gunfire. During the day, gunfire. In the afternoon, gunfire."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/265d587f-815b-41a0-8d7d-e4ae0c71213c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### Family members mourn over the killing of six-year-old Eyas Al-Namnam, who was shot and killed inside a tent east of Deir al-Balah on November 17, 2026. Footage by Mohamed Ahmed.
Abdul Karim had carried Eyas in his arms to Al-Aqsa Hospital. Doctors tried to stop the bleeding for an hour and a half but were unable to resuscitate him. "Eyas was a six-year-old boy, a beautiful boy with lovely curly black hair, and he came in via the emergency department, the operating theater. He was already very unstable," Dr. Mary O'Shea, an Irish anesthesiologist who was volunteering at Al-Aqsa Hospital in Deir al-Balah for two weeks and was on the scene, told Drop Site. "He had an obvious gunshot in the middle of his abdomen and an exit wound at the back."
O'Shea said the hospital lacked the necessary equipment and medicines to provide the best possible emergency medical care to Eyas. "Usually, in a big trauma hospital, you get more information straight away--you would have scans, you would have ultrasounds, you would be able to identify where the bleeding was initially. You wouldn't be kind of searching in the dark," she said. "The monitors in Gaza, they don't really work...and the drugs that we use are all out of date, they're unreliable."
For the past three years, Gaza's health care system has come under sustained attack by the Israeli military. Hospitals, clinics, and medical centers have been bombed and raided, while a suffocating siege has caused severe [shortages](https://substack.com/redirect/871a0fb9-5df3-4761-97c5-ca5aa81d53f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of medicine as well as parts to repair and restore critical equipment, bringing the healthcare system to the point of "systemic collapse," according to the UN.
"That's one of the things that I've found hard to think about," O'Shea said. "If he was somewhere else, would the outcome have been different? Maybe it would have been. I can't say 100% if it would have been, but maybe--maybe we would have been able to save Eyas's life, and that's heartbreaking. This is the reality in Gaza. There's so many stories like this, so many stories."
In Bir 19, Manar Abu Adhra had one child killed by Israeli gunfire in a tent earlier this year. Her daughter Rafif, just a year and five months old, was ill, and Manar was preparing to take her to a clinic for treatment.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/49a5822c-db11-417d-a12e-e350b0451589?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

"It was around 7 a.m. I left her behind me in the tent and went outside to get some clothes to change her into. Then I came back when I heard [her father] screaming. A bullet had pierced her head while she was playing inside the tent," Abu Adhra recalled. "She had done nothing wrong. She hadn't gone out to fight. She wasn't part of the resistance or anything like that. She was just a little girl inside her tent."
"We go to sleep afraid that we might lose another child, or that something might happen to us adults," she added. "At night, we move the children into this area so they can sleep behind the sand barriers we've built."
One of Abu Adhra's surviving children, eight-year-old Rahaf, hobbled beside her on crutches as she spoke. Her right leg had been amputated just below the waist after she was wounded in a separate Israeli attack.
"I lost my sister. Her name was Rafif. I lost her to stray gunfire, and we're still suffering from the shooting to this day," Rahaf said. "I used to play with her, and now I'm afraid to go to sleep because I might lose one of my siblings or get shot myself. I just wish the war would end so we could finally live without the constant gunfire."

Story by Mohamed Ahmed and Sharif Abdel Kouddous KHAN YOUNIS, Gaza Strip--Nofal Al-Akhras filled another empty flour sack with sand, tied off the top, and heaved it onto the other bags lining the outside of his tent in the Bir 19 area of the southern Gaza Strip. A displacement camp in a desolate sandy expanse west of Khan Younis, Bir 19 lies close to the yellow line where occupying Israeli troops are stationed. Al-Akhras stacked the sandbags three high, at about waist level, among drying laundry hung on a sagging clothesline, forming a makeshift barrier--a desperate attempt to protect himself and his family from Israeli gunfire. "Every day, around the clock, we are caught off guard by stray, deadly bullets fired indiscriminately," he told Drop Site News. "We have lost many loved ones who were martyred by stray bullets striking displacement tents for no reason whatsoever. We had no choice but to collect empty flour sacks, as you can see, and fill them with sand to build protective barriers to shield our children, our families, and our loved ones from the stray bullets." Al-Akhras is not alone. Many families in Bir 19 have taken to placing sandbags on the sides of their tents that face east toward the Israeli soldiers. Palestinians in Gaza, already struggling to survive genocidal conditions imposed by Israel--with multiple displacements, inadequate shelter, a lack of protection from the winter cold, storms and flooding, shortages of food and medicine, a lack of sanitation, and near daily aerial attacks--find themselves having to crouch behind sandbags to avoid flying Israeli bullets. Outside a nearby tent, a group of three children, no more than five or six years old, stood holding open a large flour sack as an older boy slowly filled it with shovelfuls of sand before struggling to stack it on some two dozen others lining two sides of their tent. Inside another tent, several sandbags were stacked at the head of each mattress. Two children lay on their backs watching a video with their heads propped up on a pillow against the bulging sacks. Families use sacks filled with sand to protect their tents and shelters from Israeli gunfire in Bir 19, Khan Younis on November 18, 2026. Video by Mohamed Ahmed. Many of the families in Bir 19 were displaced from Rafah, the southernmost city in the Gaza Strip, which was invaded by the Israeli military in May 2024 and subsequently completely depopulated and razed to the ground. "When the Israeli army entered Rafah, they ordered us to evacuate the city and move to safe areas. We came to these 'safe areas' and settled here, but after the Israeli army took control of Rafah, they began subjecting us to indiscriminate gunfire every single day," Tareq Abu Adhra told Drop Site. He worked with his daughter to fortify a line of sandbags outside his makeshift shelter, made of tape and corrugated metal sheets. "Every day, we hear bullets hitting the metal sheets and our tents. Our neighbors have been wounded. A child was martyred, a young man was killed two days ago, and a woman who was related to me was killed. Children are being killed in schools," he added. "This is what life is like for us in Bir 19 every day. So we decided to build protective barriers to shield ourselves. When we go to sleep at night, we sleep behind these barriers out of fear of the gunfire." Bir 19 camp residents pointed out multiple bullet holes in the sides of tents. A sheet of corrugated metal at one makeshift shelter was riddled with bullet holes. Another tent had a thick barrier built along one side using a patchwork of rebar covered with tarp that was filled with sand about one meter thick. "When we arrived here, we found that this was the worst place in the entire Gaza Strip when it comes to stray gunfire," Abdul Rahman Abu Adhra told Drop Site. "Just a week ago, a woman from our family was martyred when a bullet struck her as she was walking. That's why we built these barriers, to protect ourselves and our children." "People just want to live. These are peaceful people but the Israelis aren't--they won't leave anyone alone, not civilians, not women, not children, not the elderly," he continued. "There's barely a kilometer between us and the Israelis, and we're trapped between them and the sea. If they advance any further, God help us. There will be nowhere left for us to go." Israel has continued its near daily attacks despite a so-called ceasefire it signed over a year ago, in October 2025. Since then, nearly 1,700 Palestinians have been killed in airstrikes, shelling, and shootings by the Israeli military. Israel has also steadily encroached further west in violation of the agreement, moving from controlling 53% of the enclave to close to 70%, taking over more Palestinian land and corralling the entirety of Gaza's population onto less than a third of the territory. Many of the shootings occur close to Israel's line of control, where Israeli troops are stationed alongside newly built military bases. On November 17, six-year-old Eyas Al-Namnam was shot and killed inside a tent east of Deir al-Balah in central Gaza. According to his family, Eyas had just woken up, started eating, and was doing his homework when his mother asked him to go to his aunt's nearby tent to finish his work. He was accompanied by his older brother and younger sister when Israeli forces opened fire. "They hadn't even reached the entrance of the tent. His older brother went inside and then his little sister. His cousin told his older brother to sit down. His older brother sat down and Eyas was still standing. Then three shots were fired at him. Two bullets struck the ground and one hit him in the chest," another of Eyas's older brothers, Abdul Karim Al-Namnam, told Drop Site just hours after the incident. He spoke standing in the morgue as Eyas's small body wrapped in a white shroud and plastic body bag lay on a metal shelf beside him. "We were displaced from Gaza City. We fled from the north to the south, looking for safety. But there is no safety. There is no safety anywhere. Ceasefire? What ceasefire? There is shooting twenty-four hours a day. There is no peace at all. I wish there were some calm. At night, gunfire. During the day, gunfire. In the afternoon, gunfire." Family members mourn over the killing of six-year-old Eyas Al-Namnam, who was shot and killed inside a tent east of Deir al-Balah on November 17, 2026. Footage by Mohamed Ahmed. Abdul Karim had carried Eyas in his arms to Al-Aqsa Hospital. Doctors tried to stop the bleeding for an hour and a half but were unable to resuscitate him. "Eyas was a six-year-old boy, a beautiful boy with lovely curly black hair, and he came in via the emergency department, the operating theater. He was already very unstable," Dr. Mary O'Shea, an Irish anesthesiologist who was volunteering at Al-Aqsa Hospital in Deir al-Balah for two weeks and was on the scene, told Drop Site. "He had an obvious gunshot in the middle of his abdomen and an exit wound at the back." O'Shea said the hospital lacked the necessary equipment and medicines to provide the best possible emergency medical care to Eyas. "Usually, in a big trauma hospital, you get more information straight away--you would have scans, you would have ultrasounds, you would be able to identify where the bleeding was initially. RENEW YOUR LCV MEMBERSHIP >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/X6bzs~ From the frozen tundra of Alaska’s wilderness to the desert landscapes of Bears
Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante, Trump’s Department of the Interior has just
released an outrageous four-year plan to sell off and offload some of our most extraordinary and ecologically important landscapes. Here’s what’s at stake: Alaska’s wilderness: The Trump administration is advancing the destructive Ambler Road project, which would carve a 211-mile mining access road across Alaska’s fragile wilderness. At the same time, they’re working to clear the path for seismic testing for oil in the Arctic Refuge’s essential Coastal Plain, which disturbs wildlife and can collapse polar bear dens with cubs in them.
Our national forests: Efforts to repeal the Roadless Rule could open millions of acres of previously protected forests to logging and development, sacrificing ancient trees for increased timber profits.
Our national monuments: Iconic landscapes like Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante face ongoing threats to their boundaries and even national monument status as the Trump administration attempts to chip away at these natural and cultural treasures.
Our national parks and public lands: Deep cuts to the National Park Service and Forest Service, alongside efforts to repeal the Bureau of Land Management’s Public Lands Rule, threaten the very future of how public lands are stewarded in our country, while specific parks like Gates of the Arctic could see roads carved right through them. These are places that generations of environmentalists, often led by Indigenous
communities, have worked to protect. They’re places of deep natural and cultural
significance, essential ecosystems, and landscapes that belong to ALL OF US. Ahead of Giving Tuesday, we’re looking for 1,000 people to step up and send the
Trump administration a powerful message: OUR PUBLIC LANDS ARE NOT FOR SALE! Renew your LCV membership for just $15 and your gift will TRIPLE in impact to fund our campaigns to protect public lands >> https://links.messages.lcv. That’s not all! influence, even in states with a long history of loyalty to him. His approval
rating is at a career low of 32%. Trump’s obsession with selling off our public lands is deeply unpopular, even
within his own party. People of all political persuasions value our national
parks, forests, monuments, and wild places. People in America wantto see these special places protected for future generations, not sacrificed for
another corporate giveaway. We have public support on our side. Our campaigns to keep public lands in public
hands have worked before — but winning takes people power. And right now, we
need your help, Peter. Your renewed membership helps LCV: https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/w_ ✅ Hold anti-environment politicians accountable for attacks on the lands we all
share

How the Federal Withholding of funds Actually Works
Rather than immediately clawing back money already in ACPS's bank account, a federal directive to VDOE typically operates as a reimbursement freeze and high-risk designation:

* School districts usually spend money first and submit invoices to VDOE to be reimbursed from federal grant pools. Under a hold, VDOE pauses those reimbursements to ACPS until the federal conditions are met.

* VDOE has 30 days to submit a statewide corrective action plan showing how it will audit Virginia school districts to ensure hiring and safety laws are followed.

clean_body: | | | == == Happy Thanksgiving! | Team, I am thankful for your trust in me for another term in Congress, and I am thankful for President Donald J. Trump and his team, Governor Glenn Youngkin, 5th District Chair Ramona Christian, and all of our incredible volunteers for helping us pull off a hard-fought victory against a radical and heavily funded, Soros-backed opponent. We are especially thankful for the brave men and women of our military. Thank you for keeping us safe. Fox News The Big Weekend Show | == I joined Tomi Lahren, Johnny Joey Jones, Anita Vogel, and Kevin Corke on Fox News's The Big Weekend Show to break down how the grace of God and the strength of rural Virginia helped us defeat a Soros-backed opponent and overcome the blue wave. We also discussed what needs to happen next regarding Russia and Ukraine, Iran, the Democrats' lawfare plans, and getting real work done in Congress before January 3. == It's Miller Time | == Historically, the party in power faces headwinds in the midterms. The conflict in Iran, combined with Democrats shutting down U.S. refineries for a reckless electric vehicle mandate, left Americans vulnerable to high gas prices. Come January 2027, voters are going to have a massive case of buyer's remorse. We will keep working hard to earn the trust of the middle class and bounce back even stronger in 2028. In the meantime, here is a summary of White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller's remarks on President Trump's accomplishments: ✅ Unprecedented Two-Year Record: Miller states that President Trump has accomplished more in the past two years than any other president in American history, noting that listing every achievement would take hours. ✅ Net Deregulation: He describes Trump as the first president to achieve net deregulation, removing ten regulations for every new one introduced, a milestone he notes was not reached even during the Reagan administration. ✅ Social & Border Policies: Miller highlights the elimination of DEI initiatives and transgender policies, the securing of the border, record deportations, and historically low crime and low murder rates. ✅ Energy & Trade: He points to record domestic production of fossil fuels and coal, the activation of the first new nuclear reactors since the 1970s, and the rebalancing of global trade relationships. ✅ National Security & Foreign Policy: Miller cites the rebuilding of the U.S. military and federal law enforcement, the use of lethal force against drug cartels, a rapid takeover of Venezuela that doubled U.S. oil reserves, and reshaped diplomatic relationships with both Russia and China. ✅ Economic Performance: He credits the administration with building the strongest economy and fastest wage growth in U.S. history while overcoming the high inflation and perceived international standing issues inherited from the Biden administration. ✅ Looking Ahead: Concluding his remarks, Miller predicts that the upcoming two years will be the greatest in American history and expresses pride in serving as White House Chief of Staff to continue delivering results. == Weekly Recap - Protecting Virginia's Children | == here is a troubling pattern of child endangerment in the Albemarle County school system, and we are seeing similar failures in Alexandria and across the Commonwealth. Watch my recent interview with 29 News in Charlottesville to hear what we are doing to hold leadership accountable: == Socialism Sucks | Spotted this bumper sticker, and it says a lot. 🇺🇸 Socialism often sounds appealing in theory. In practice, when governments take control of production and eliminate private ownership of the means of production, the results have been consistent: ❌ Destroys incentives: When people cannot keep the rewards of their effort and risk-taking, productivity and innovation decline. ❌ Central planning fails: No group of planners can match the information and coordination that free prices and private decisions provide. The result is chronic shortages and waste. ❌ Shrinks liberty: Concentrating economic power in the state almost always expands political control and reduces individual freedom. ❌ Abolishes private property rights: It removes the fundamental right to own, use, and benefit from what you produce. ❌ Produces stagnation and scarcity: Instead of broad prosperity, it has repeatedly delivered shortages, declining living standards, and higher poverty relative to market systems. ❌ Has a grim track record: 20th-century socialist/ communist regimes that implemented these ideas caused tens of millions of deaths through famine, execution, forced labor, and repression (estimates commonly range from the mid-tens of millions to around 100 million). Authoritarianism was the rule, not the exception. A free-market economy built on secure private property rights and individual liberty, like the United States, has lifted far more people out of poverty than any other system in history. Let's protect the system of freedom that actually works. Newsmax Interview | == Under Speaker Mike Johnson's leadership, House Republicans passed over 1,000 bills, and roughly 700 of those measures are still awaiting Senate action. Republicans focus on how we're going to make life better for hardworking Americans, while Democrats focus on who they're going to target next. Come January, expect Washington to be bogged down in endless partisan investigations. == The Schilling Show: John McGuire | == We will never stop fighting to protect children. Today I had the honor of joining the Rob Schilling Show in Charlottesville to talk about the ongoing failures to protect children in Albemarle County Schools. == Albemarle County School Funding? | == How the Federal Withholding of funds Actually Works Rather than immediately clawing back money already in ACPS's bank account, a federal directive to VDOE typically operates as a reimbursement freeze and high-risk designation: School districts usually spend money first and submit invoices to VDOE to be reimbursed from federal grant pools. Under a hold, VDOE pauses those reimbursements to ACPS until the federal conditions are met. VDOE has 30 days to submit a statewide corrective action plan showing how it will audit Virginia school districts to ensure hiring and safety laws are followed. == Why Did Spanberger Opt Out of School Tax Credits? | == Why did Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger opt out of the new Federal Scholarship Tax Credit (FSTC) program for 2027, reversing former Governor Glenn Youngkin's initial move to enroll the state? Last weeks recap email: == == | == "The mistake has been corrected" - Elon Musk == You're Invited! A Christmas Thank You Party - December 19th | == Tracy and I would like to invite you to a special Christmas Thank You Party on Saturday, December 19th, in Appomattox. Let's come together, celebrate the birth of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, and enjoy some fellowship as we recognize the people who made this victory possible! Event Details: Saturday, December 19, 2026 12:30 PM - 2:00 PM Appomattox Community Center Appomattox, Virginia == Scan the QR code on the flyer above or click the link to reserve your free tickets today! Friend, I grew up in public housing on the west side of Savannah, Georgia. I had 11 brothers and sisters – and while my family was short on money, we were long on love and faith.

We have to deliver progress on the issues that will really make a difference for everyday people, and we have to hold this administration accountable for the harm they’ve caused.
**I need you with me every step of the way. I’m honored to have your support. Thank you.
– Rev. Raphael Warnock

| Patriot,
---
Ever since Biden’s FBI raided my home in 2021, I’ve been dragged through hell for 5 years straight – with no end in sight.
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
__
---
_Arresting me alongside President Trump as innocent men.
Freezing my bank accounts.
Shredding my law licenses.
Seizing my assets._
---
**And now, I have to be brutally honest about where things stand...**
---
**... _I’m being pushed to the brink of bankruptcy._**
---
**That’s the Left’s goal: to use every form of lawfare in their quiver to bleed me dry and bankrupt.**
---
_This is nothing but the most savage form of retaliation for successfully defending President Trump as his former attorney._
---
**But you know what, Patriot?**
---
_I’d do it all over again!_
---
**I’d rather lose everything than betray what I know to be true. I could never lie and say what I'm going through is a fair and honest process just to hang on to “earthly possessions.”**
---
_"_For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul_?" (Mark 8:36)_
---
**And while I stare down the threat of bankruptcy and the possibility of spending my last remaining living years in a prison cell in Arizona – where the President _legally_ cannot pardon me – I REFUSE to surrender the fight for my freedom.**
---
5 years ago, I was called a “DEAD MAN WALKING.” The media said I was cooked. They said there was _ZERO_ CHANCE I could survive this magnitude of legal warfare.
---
**Yet here I am, standing tall and ready to fight in the final battle for my freedom.**
---
But now, as I fight with all I’ve got, I have only one place left to turn to help me reach the finish line and secure my freedom: _good and honest Americans like _YOU.__
---
_Kind souls like you are the reason I’ve made it this far – and you will be the reason I declare victory in the final showdown for my freedom._
---
Patriot, I understand this was probably the last thing on your mind today. I get it. And that’s why I always say that if you can’t afford to help me in this fight, please delete this message and carry on with your day. Don’t even think twice about it.
---
**_But if you can help, I’m going to need the best defense I can get to win this final battle._**
---
[**Please make a contribution to the Rudy Defense Trust to ensure I have the resources needed to retain a top-notch defense team in what is now the FINAL BATTLE for my freedom and justice.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---

Thank you and God bless you,
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Rudy Giuliani
Rudy Defense Trust
---

## **Stepping Away From the Noise: What We Have to Be Thankful For This Week**
If you spend your days watching cable news, scrolling social media, or tracking the latest legislative battles on Capitol Hill, it is easy to feel like the country is locked in a permanent state of crises.
Between post-election analyses, lame-duck deadlines, and the non-stop churn of Washington headlines, the noise never really stops.
**That is exactly why Thanksgiving week is so important.**
As we head into Thursday, millions of Americans are packing up the car, boarding flights, and heading home to sit around a table with family and friends. For one week, the partisan talking points, corporate media narratives, and daily outrage cycles take a back seat to the things that acually matter (fingers crossed anyway).

Before the holiday rush kicks into high gear, I wanted to take a moment today to step back from the political fight and reflect on why - even in a divided era - we still have an extraordinary amount to be grateful for:
* **The Resilience of the American People:** No matter what happens in Washington, everyday Americans get up every morning, work hard, raise their families, serve our nation, and strengthen their communities. Here is a stat that blew my mind. A top Dem strategist at a post election panel shared that people who identify as independent voters -- have an average of 2.8 jobs, spend 4 minutes on political news a week and carry and average of $60,000 in credit card debt. Bottom line, they are spending their days working to get by and not hyper focused on the partisan fights.
* **The Freedom to Speak and Build:** We live in a nation where independent voices can challenge the status quo without asking permission from corporate gatekeepers.
* **The People Behind the Scenes:** From the men and women wearing the uniform overseas to first responders working holiday shifts here at home, our safety and freedom depends on people who rarely make the evening news.

And on a personal note, I am deeply grateful to every single one of you who reads this newsletter, tunes into the show, and supports independent journalism.
Today's issue is a look at what truly matters this Thanksgiving week - and a personal thank-you to this community.

Peter, Before we all disappear into our kitchens, eat entirely too much stuffing, and inevitably debate how much pie is socially acceptable to consume in one sitting, I wanted to take a little time to write to you. **Because this year, I've got a whole lot to be thankful for. And you're a pretty big part of that.** It's been quite a year, hasn't it? We've laughed. We've cried. We've yelled at our televisions. And we've probably all aged a few extra years. (I know I have. 😂) But through all of it, you've given me so many reasons to feel hopeful. I'm thankful for the people who kept showing up even when they were exhausted. The people who refused to give in to cynicism. The people who reminded their neighbors that we still have the power to change things. And I'm so incredibly thankful that I get to do this work alongside people like you. In just a few short weeks, I'll walk back into the Capitol as a member of the Democratic House majority for the very first time. **And OH, am I ready.** I'm ready to fight for families who are tired of worrying about how they're going to pay their bills. For people who deserve healthcare they can afford. For our kids, our communities, and a democracy that belongs to all of us. **I've been waiting four years for this opportunity, and I intend to make every single day of it count.** **[LET'S GET TO WORK!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143987239/662049298/-791998112?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MjZkMmQ5MC0yZGU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gTSL4PF4pTvz33Jz1BsuuYMP7uz3FvI5NvTxkYAcZs0=)** I've got ideas. I've got energy. I've got a growing to-do list. _And I've got a pretty healthy supply of Vermont perseverance to get me through whatever Washington throws my way. 😉_ But for the next few days, I hope we all give ourselves permission to enjoy the little things. Eat the extra slice of pie. Hug your people a little tighter. Call someone you've been meaning to call. Get outside if you can. Find a little joy wherever you can get it. And please know that somewhere up here in Vermont, there's a very grateful congresswoman thinking about how lucky she is to have you in her corner. It’s an extraordinary setback for American health and a marker of the deep distrust of vaccines across the country. This was entirely avoidable. Donald Trump and his Secretary of Health & Human Services, Robert Kennedy, Jr., are directly to blame for losing this coveted status, that took nearly half a century to attain. As a microbiologist and scientist who has spent my career studying infectious diseases, watching a safe, proven vaccine get undermined by conspiracy theories at the highest levels of government is both frustrating and incredibly dangerous. It leaves newborns, immunocompromised neighbors, and families across America vulnerable to a completely preventable disease. This is exactly why we need real scientists in Congress—to counter guys like RFK Jr., who refuse to take public health seriously.
