This week the president will pardon a turkey. It's a sweet tradition. The bird gets a name and a few camera flashes, and then it goes to live out its days on a farm.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8344630c-383b-4c38-9ce6-1ffa2fc51181?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Last year the president pardoned a different kind of turkey. This one is a Utah guy who bought of the most expensive ranches in the state, just up the road from me in Oakley. His name is Trevor Milton.
You probably never heard much about his pardon. That isn't because the story is small. There are so many stories like it that it's hard to keep track. When corruption comes at you like a firehose, every single drop gets lost. So let's make sure this story isn't forgotten. Buckle up, because this one is a wild ride.
Caroline Gleich ⛰️ is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..fXMBjd_LBGriolSxCTs9-9S6gGyWkeKoUxT0G4sIVfY?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=226381516)
In 2014, Milton started a company in Utah called Nikola. He promised hydrogen and electric semi trucks that would clean up our highways. I love that dream, and I want clean trucks too. The problem is that he lied about it over and over. The U.S. Attorney who prosecuted him said it plainly: "Trevor Milton lied to investors again and again."
Nikola put out a video of its semi-truck cruising down a highway, and it looked like the future. The truck couldn't actually drive itself anywhere. The team towed it to the top of a hill with just the right slope and let gravity do the rest. Milton also said the company was making hydrogen when it wasn't making any.
The hype worked like a charm. When Nikola went public in 2020, it was briefly worth about $30 billion, which was more than Ford. Then the truth came out, and the stock fell off a cliff. Nikola filed for bankruptcy in February 2025.
Prosecutors said Milton aimed his pitch at everyday people. Many of them started trading during the pandemic after they lost income, and some lost their retirement savings. One Salt Lake City businessman lost more than $100,000. He told the Washington Post, "I wrote that money off a long time ago."
In July 2021, a federal grand jury charged Milton with fraud, and a judge let him wait for trial at home in Utah. Days after he pleaded not guilty, he sold about $77 million of Nikola stock. That December, an LLC tied to Milton bought a $15 million estate in Summit County, UT. I run past it all the time.
In September 2022, the same month his fraud trial began, that same LLC paid $16 million for a penthouse in Manhattan. Seven months later, it was back on the market for $19.8 million. His victims were counting their losses while he was out house shopping.
A jury convicted Milton of fraud in 2022, and a judge sentenced him to four years in prison. He stayed free on bond during his appeal and never served a day.
In October 2024, less than a month before the election, Milton and his wife gave more than $1.8 million to a Trump reelection fund. Before that, the Financial Times reported, Milton had given less than $20,000 to congressional and presidential candidates. In March 2025, prosecutors asked the judge to make Milton pay his victims back nearly $700 million. Two weeks later, Trump called Milton personally to tell him he was pardoned. Trump told reporters Milton was "exonerated." He wasn't. A jury of twelve people convicted him. Because of the pardon, the judge can no longer order restitution of any kind. The pardon even wiped out the order to give up a second Utah ranch he bought with money from his fraud.
Then he came back for more. With Nikola in bankruptcy, Milton filed a claim asking the company to pay him nearly $70 million for his legal bills and other costs. His argument was that the pardon meant Trump had found him "factually innocent." The bankruptcy judge didn't buy it. Nikola's creditors say Milton still owes the company nearly $100 million from an arbitration award, and they had to subpoena him just to find out what he has.
Milton's case isn't a one-off. CBS News found that Trump's clemency has wiped out or blocked about $1.08 billion in fines and restitution since January 2025, and Milton's is the biggest single piece. Most Americans think this is wrong. In YouGov polling, 71 percent said it's inappropriate for a president to pardon his own campaign donors.
Instead of going to prison, Milton went back to business. In 2024, Milton and a group of investors bought SyberJet, a struggling small-jet maker based in Utah. He is now its CEO. The Wall Street Journal reviewed investor documents showing that SyberJet is trying to raise $1 billion at a $4 billion valuation. Milton pitches the planes as AI-powered, and he told the Journal that planes will be "10 times harder than Nikola ever was."
The comeback tour has been busy. Last December, at the Kennedy Center Honors, Milton mingled with celebrities inside the SyberJet Lounge. His company paid millions to sponsor it, and the president called it "gorgeous." Last month in Las Vegas, with the song "Survivor" blasting over the speakers, Milton unveiled a full-size mockup of the SJ36. It's a planned $14 million private jet, and he opened reservations for early buyers. According to the Journal, the first deliveries are aimed for 2032.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b0c4321f-cece-4451-9914-f6a28e5d4847?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So here we are at Thanksgiving. The turkey at the White House gets a farm. The people Milton hurt got nothing back. Milton got a clean slate, a jet company and a fresh pitch to new investors.
Happy Thanksgiving. I'm grateful for every one of you who keeps paying attention when it would be easier to look away. I'm a Park City local and a former U.S. Senate candidate. I ran because I believe our government should work for regular people and not for its biggest donors. Tell me in the comments whether a pardon should ever be able to erase what someone owes his victims. Share this with the person at your Thanksgiving table who still thinks Trump is draining the swamp. And subscribe so you don't miss the next Systems Check. If you want to listen to a podcast about this story from 2022, check out the [WSJ's Bad Bets.](https://substack.com/redirect/a56475ca-456d-4fa0-a9be-6bb6dc3ee24f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
P.S. One more thing before you head to the table. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, or BAAJA, already passed the Senate, and now it's up to the House. It would fast-track gas pipelines, polluting power plants and data centers across the country, including right here in Utah. It's the same story you just read: rules that work for the powerful while the rest of us foot the bill. The team towed it to the top of a hill with just the right slope and let gravity do the rest. Milton also said the company was making hydrogen when it wasn't making any. The hype worked like a charm. When Nikola went public in 2020, it was briefly worth about $30 billion, which was more than Ford. Then the truth came out, and the stock fell off a cliff. Nikola filed for bankruptcy in February 2025. Prosecutors said Milton aimed his pitch at everyday people. Many of them started trading during the pandemic after they lost income, and some lost their retirement savings. One Salt Lake City businessman lost more than $100,000. He told the Washington Post, "I wrote that money off a long time ago." In July 2021, a federal grand jury charged Milton with fraud, and a judge let him wait for trial at home in Utah. Days after he pleaded not guilty, he sold about $77 million of Nikola stock. That December, an LLC tied to Milton bought a $15 million estate in Summit County, UT. I run past it all the time. In September 2022, the same month his fraud trial began, that same LLC paid $16 million for a penthouse in Manhattan. Seven months later, it was back on the market for $19.8 million. His victims were counting their losses while he was out house shopping. A jury convicted Milton of fraud in 2022, and a judge sentenced him to four years in prison. He stayed free on bond during his appeal and never served a day. In October 2024, less than a month before the election, Milton and his wife gave more than $1.8 million to a Trump reelection fund. Before that, the Financial Times reported, Milton had given less than $20,000 to congressional and presidential candidates. In March 2025, prosecutors asked the judge to make Milton pay his victims back nearly $700 million. Two weeks later, Trump called Milton personally to tell him he was pardoned. Trump told reporters Milton was "exonerated." He wasn't. A jury of twelve people convicted him. Because of the pardon, the judge can no longer order restitution of any kind. The pardon even wiped out the order to give up a second Utah ranch he bought with money from his fraud. Then he came back for more. With Nikola in bankruptcy, Milton filed a claim asking the company to pay him nearly $70 million for his legal bills and other costs. His argument was that the pardon meant Trump had found him "factually innocent." The bankruptcy judge didn't buy it. Nikola's creditors say Milton still owes the company nearly $100 million from an arbitration award, and they had to subpoena him just to find out what he has. Milton's case isn't a one-off. CBS News found that Trump's clemency has wiped out or blocked about $1.08 billion in fines and restitution since January 2025, and Milton's is the biggest single piece. Most Americans think this is wrong. In YouGov polling, 71 percent said it's inappropriate for a president to pardon his own campaign donors. Instead of going to prison, Milton went back to business. In 2024, Milton and a group of investors bought SyberJet, a struggling small-jet maker based in Utah. He is now its CEO. The Wall Street Journal reviewed investor documents showing that SyberJet is trying to raise $1 billion at a $4 billion valuation. Milton pitches the planes as AI-powered, and he told the Journal that planes will be "10 times harder than Nikola ever was." The comeback tour has been busy. Last December, at the Kennedy Center Honors, Milton mingled with celebrities inside the SyberJet Lounge. His company paid millions to sponsor it, and the president called it "gorgeous." Last month in Las Vegas, with the song "Survivor" blasting over the speakers, Milton unveiled a full-size mockup of the SJ36. It's a planned $14 million private jet, and he opened reservations for early buyers. According to the Journal, the first deliveries are aimed for 2032. | | ---|---|--- So here we are at Thanksgiving. The turkey at the White House gets a farm. The people Milton hurt got nothing back. Milton got a clean slate, a jet company and a fresh pitch to new investors. Happy Thanksgiving. I'm grateful for every one of you who keeps paying attention when it would be easier to look away. I'm a Park City local and a former U.S. Senate candidate. I ran because I believe our government should work for regular people and not for its biggest donors. Tell me in the comments whether a pardon should ever be able to erase what someone owes his victims. Share this with the person at your Thanksgiving table who still thinks Trump is draining the swamp. And subscribe so you don't miss the next Systems Check. If you want to listen to a podcast about this story from 2022, check out the P.S. One more thing before you head to the table. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, or BAAJA, already passed the Senate, and now it's up to the House. It would fast-track gas pipelines, polluting power plants and data centers across the country, including right here in Utah. It's the same story you just read: rules that work for the powerful while the rest of us foot the bill. Take two minutes to tell your representative to reject BAAJA as written and deliver a better deal. Take action here: You're currently a free subscriber to . | | Derek,

I am incredibly humbled to have been re-hired by Virginians this year. Alongside new Democratic majorities in the House and Senate, I’m ready to continue fighting for working families in Washington.

That’s lots of talk right now about what Democrats should be focused on – _and for good reason_. Voters spoke loud and clear that they want leaders who will deliver results and bring folks together to solve problems.

**So as we look towards new Democratic congressional majorities, I wanted to let you know what fights I’m committed to in the coming months:**
* **We need to move towards universal health care in this country.** It’s clear we can no longer continue to patch a broken system. We need to ensure that every American has access to a basic standard of care – and that rural hospitals and clinics can remain open for communities that rely on them.

* **We need to put some serious guardrails on Artificial Intelligence.** I’ve been raising the alarm bells for years about the major disruptions and risks AI presents, and I have a comprehensive legislative package that Congress should act on immediately.

* **And we’ve got to put some checks and balances on the Trump administration.** I’ve been calling out this president’s downright stupid vanity projects, blatant corruption, and self-dealing since the start, and I’ll continue to stand up, push back, and speak out.

These are the fights that I spoke about with so many of you on the campaign trail over the last year – and I’m ready to deliver on them.

[_**None of this is possible without the support from this grassroots team. So, I’m asking: will you chip in $5 to my PAC, Forward Together, and help lead these fights in Virginia and across the country by electing more forward-looking and consensus-building leaders?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143990587/662060035/574570639?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_FTLaunch_261124_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZjg5ZjMwMi0zM2U4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Tn-DezyblDfIck-pbYyXWQ-CdahrzptakgaGx28je5M=)

Peter, I just got back to the Hudson Valley after two weeks in DC for new member orientation. And I have to tell you: I have met some incredible patriots and public servants who come from all across the country. Very different places, very different districts, but absolutely united by the same mission: **To lower costs. To root out corruption. And to really make America work for working people again.** There’s a lot to do. And I want to make sure that my team is able to hit the ground running on January 3rd, so that this incoming class can make a difference on day one. Very different places, very different districts, but absolutely united by the same mission: To lower costs. To root out corruption. And to really make America work for working people again. There’s a lot to do. And I want to make sure that my team is able to hit the ground running on January 3rd, so that this incoming class can make a difference on day one. | | With Thanksgiving just around the corner, it's easy to let the noise of daily life steal our joy. But gratitude has a remarkable way of changing our perspective, even in difficult circumstances. This week, we're sharing six inspiring stories that remind us of the power of a thankful heart. From Jimmy Stewart's handwritten thank-you notes to Corrie and Betsie ten Boom finding gratitude in a Nazi concentration camp, these remarkable stories show that thankfulness isn't dependent on perfect circumstances. Discover how one determined mother helped establish Thanksgiving as a national tradition, why George Washington called Americans to give thanks, and how faith can transform even life's greatest hardships. This Thanksgiving, rediscover the blessings that matter most and the joy of a grateful heart. [Read All 6 Inspiring Stories here](https://momsforamerica.us/so/5eQ8EpWyL/c?w=zzj2gy0m_FCe0lzB3h38pRPRDH-IdZ9Q8Qv-H9BOovw.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubW9tc2ZvcmFtZXJpY2EudXMvcG9zdC82LXRydWUtc3Rvcmllcy1vZi1ncmF0aXR1ZGUtdG8taW5zcGlyZS15b3VyLXRoYW5rc2dpdmluZyIsInIiOiI5NzRkODFlYy0zZWExLTQzZTgtYWM4OS0wYzQ0NDljNzZhMDkiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiJiMzgzOGJmOC1mYWIwLTQxYjktOTY3My1lOGM2YmVmYjY1NzcifQ) and discover why these ideas matter, and what we can do as moms to help preserve America's future.
---
| | | |
---
| | Thankful for Family: One Mom's Mission to Change Foster Care
---
| [](https://momsforamerica.us/so/5eQ8EpWyL/c?w=H98Piob0yVEMdjKOlh4yHrtqXamW7_ipqXtws1fHfeg.)
---
| | What happens when opening your heart and home to children in need becomes a mission to change thousands of lives? For homeschooling mom Melissa Khamkhlounnavong, adopting her children through foster care was just the beginning! Her family's journey opened her eyes to the challenges facing children in the system and inspired her to do something about it. Friends, With Thanksgiving coming up this week, I want to take the opportunity to express my gratitude not only for your support, but also for what we’ve built together. Many of you embarked on this journey with me two years ago motivated by a simple belief: the Hudson Valley deserves a representative who puts service above self, country above party, and working families above special interests. You devoted your time, energy, and resources to achieving that goal. And we did it. Now, it’s time to get to work. We have a lot to do to root out the corruption that has taken hold in Washington, lower costs for working families, and make our government serve the people once again. Just like I said throughout the campaign: it’s not going to be easy, but it’s sure as hell going to be worth it. Thank you for entrusting me with this privilege of a lifetime. I will never take it for granted. Wishing everyone a very happy and healthy Thanksgiving! With gratitude and fire,
Cait Conley

# [Tuesday fade follows Nvidia's violent Monday rocket](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Huang-driven squeeze faded on Tuesday as futures turned lower and Nvidia gave back gains, with strategists warning the bounce still resembles bear-market price action.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Futures turn red:** Nasdaq futures fell 1.6-1.9% and S&P futures slipped 0.9-1%, while Nvidia dropped 4-8% in premarket trading after Monday's 31.5% surge.
* **Historical pattern:** BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky noted that in all 12 cases since 1985 when the Nasdaq-100 fell 5% or more one day and rose 5% or more the next, the index later declined at least 4.6% within 30 days.
* **Still below averages:** Goldman's Vitali Meschoulam called the prior session a flush rather than a clearing, and major indexes remained below their 200-day moving averages.
* **Too violent to hold:** Goldman's Privorotsky described the Monday move as "too violent for anyone to hold," arguing it completes rather than ends the 2018 analogue.

# [Nvidia adds nearly $1 trillion as Trump pushes Huang return](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia's board reversed course and reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO after weekend pressure from President Trump, sending the stock up 31.5% and lifting the Nasdaq 6.5% in its best day since April 2025.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Record one-day gain:** Nvidia closed at $165.05 after adding roughly $952 billion in market value, the largest single-day increase ever for any U.S. company, while the S&P 500 rose 4.7% to 7,237 and the Dow gained about 1,450 points.
* **Trump claims credit:** Trump told CNBC he "made the deal" and "convinced them," saying administration officials gave the board assurances that Huang posed no national-security risk.
* **Employee welcome:** Staff chanted and hugged Huang on his return; he told them he would be "a better CEO the second time around."
* **Same-day action:** Commerce added Megaspeed and six other companies to the Entity List the day Huang was reinstated.

# [Congress schedules December interviews on Huang's return](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Lawmakers moved quickly after Huang's reinstatement, setting transcribed interviews and a Senate Banking hearing while residual national-security questions remain open.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **House dates locked:** Three House Republican chairmen said a brief internal review does not resolve smuggling and diversion concerns; transcribed interviews are scheduled for December 1-2.
* **Senate Banking set:** A Senate Banking Committee hearing is scheduled for December 3, with Democrats indicating further probes once they hold the majority.
* **Entity List move:** Commerce blacklisted Megaspeed and six other firms the same day, a step that had been requested earlier.
* **State probe continues:** California's attorney general said the state's examination of Nvidia's China activities will proceed despite the CEO's return.

# [Huang's return tests Nvidia governance and founder mode](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia's decision to reinstate a CEO who resigned over undisclosed affairs has drawn scrutiny of board independence and the company's reliance on its founder.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Staff reception:** Employees chanted, hollered and hugged Huang; he pledged to be a better CEO the second time around.
* **Too big to fire:** Analysts described Huang as effectively "too big to fire," highlighting the company's deep dependence on its co-founder.
* **Interim left out:** Reports indicated longtime CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress was not informed in advance of the reinstatement decision.
* **Norms under test:** The reversal is already being read as a test of corporate norms after a CEO resigned and was brought back under external pressure.

# [Nvidia short sellers lose $12 billion as options hit record](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Huang's return wiped out nearly all of short sellers' recent gains and set a single-day options-trading record on Nvidia stock.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Short losses:** S3 Partners said short sellers lost roughly $11.3-12 billion in one session, erasing nearly 90% of gains from the prior seven sessions.
* **Options volume:** More than 11 million options contracts traded on Nvidia Monday, the most active single day in the stock's history.
* **3x ETP wiped:** A London-listed triple-short Nvidia ETP was suspended after one line fell more than 91% in seconds when the stock gapped as much as 34%.
* **Mechanical bid:** Nomura's Charlie McElligott sized roughly $41 billion of levered-ETF buying that chased the upside once hedges died and shorts were stopped.

# [McElligott says AI is now too big to fail after Huang return](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nomura's Charlie McElligott argued that Huang's return and the resulting forced buying showed AI has become too big to fail, turning options plumbing into mechanical demand.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **$41 billion bid:** McElligott sized about $41 billion of levered-ETF buying that chased the upside once hedges expired and shorts were stopped out.
* **Market message:** Barron's said Trump's backing of the reinstatement sent a clear signal that Nvidia and AI are too big to fail, leaving open how far Washington will go to support the boom.
* **Still open questions:** Goldman's TMT desk separated the tactical bounce from a fundamental recovery, noting leadership relief does not resolve larger issues around returns on spending.
* **No follow-through:** Coverage noted the initial surge lacked sustained follow-through once the first wave of forced buying ended.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/4cfe71d3-8a3e-4301-8e03-345f9533c169?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# [Sanofi agrees to $41 billion cash deal for Insmed](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Sanofi agreed to buy respiratory specialist Insmed for $41 billion in cash, the year's largest pharmaceutical deal and the biggest biotech acquisition since 2023.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **$175 per share:** The offer is $175 a share, a roughly 17% premium to the prior close, and is expected to close in the first half of 2027.
* **Pipeline bulk-up:** The transaction adds two commercialized respiratory medicines and is positioned to help offset revenue pressure as top-selling drugs lose exclusivity later in the decade.
* **Accretive timeline:** Management expects the deal to become accretive by the end of 2028.
* **Market reaction:** Both Insmed and Sanofi shares rose on the announcement, which outlets described as a rare win-win structure.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/4cfe71d3-8a3e-4301-8e03-345f9533c169?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# [Oil slips toward three-month lows as Libya output drops](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Crude prices fell toward three-month lows on surplus expectations even as Libya reported a sharp production decline from pipeline shutdowns.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5a69b68d-4c4a-40c3-992a-c54227ea2d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Price levels:** Brent's January contract dropped about 1% to $88.52 a barrel and WTI futures fell 0.9% to $79.52.
* **Libya disruption:** Libya's NOC said output fell by about 365,000 barrels per day after an armed group shut a valve on the Sharara pipeline, on top of an existing Hamada shutdown.
* **Surplus backdrop:** Coverage linked the slide to fading conflict premium and expectations of a prospective supply surplus ahead of an OPEC+ meeting.
* **Fragile balance:** Other reports noted prices swinging higher at times on persistent shipping threats in the Gulf even as the overall trend pointed lower.

body:
[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1007&refcode=20261124_MJ_T2&akid=346%2E344797%2EgFp1z6 ]COURIER Newsroom

Hi Peter — Mark Jacob here, contributor at COURIER.

The midterms were a victory for the truth. Most voters are no longer
buying the MAGA con game, and more of the media have stopped sanewashing
it.

Finally, there are signs that we might be emerging from a dark period for
both democracy and journalism.

But we’re not out of the woods yet.

I wrote this week about how the American people are no longer buying
MAGA's lies, and how important pro-democracy media is in this moment.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1003&refcode=20261124_MJ_T2&akid=346%2E344797%2EgFp1z6 ]Before you read on, I hope you'll consider making a donation to COURIER
Newsroom before next week's fundraising deadline on Giving Tuesday. This
post-midterms period is a crucial time for the media to defend democracy —
and the scale of reporting COURIER is able to do in the weeks and months
ahead depends on how much readers like you are able to give today.

Thanks for reading,
Mark Jacob
COURIER Contributor

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1004&refcode=20261124_MJ_T2&akid=346%2E344797%2EgFp1z6 ]MAGA hat with tag: All Sales Final, No Refunds or Exchanges

MAGA won’t destroy us with their lies. They’ll destroy themselves.
The scams are shopworn, and the American people are no longer buying them
By Mark Jacob

Right-wing lies are becoming ever more outrageous because right wingers
are becoming ever more desperate.

Two examples came last week:

* Michael LoSapio, nominated by Donald Trump to head the Cybersecurity
and Infrastructure Security Agency, was asked at a Senate hearing
whether the Jan. 6 assault on the Capitol was an attack and he
answered, “No, I don’t believe it was an attack.”
* Elon Musk, embarrassed after spending nearly half a billion dollars on
the Republicans’ midterms humiliation, declared that he was “not
MAGA.” That’s quite a reversal for someone who said two years ago,
“I’m not just MAGA. I am dark, gothic MAGA” and even more recently led
the MAGA vandalism of government agencies.

Clearly, people connected to the Trump regime will lie as long as we
tolerate it. But the good news is that, increasingly, we’re not.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1005&refcode=20261124_MJ_T2&akid=346%2E344797%2EgFp1z6 ]DONATE

There’s reason to think Trump’s anti-trans hokum helped him win in 2024.
“The transgender thing is incredible,” he said then. “Think of it: Your
kid goes to school and comes home a few days later with an operation. The
school decides what’s going to happen with your child.”

But when Trump tried the same line of attack this year – claiming that
“Timmy” went to school and came home as “Tammy” after surgery – it fell
flat.

The midterms were a victory for the truth. Most voters are no longer
buying the MAGA con game, and more of the media have stopped sanewashing
it. Finally, there are signs that we might be emerging from a dark period
for both democracy and journalism.

When I went to work every day as a Chicago Tribune editor, I walked past
an inscription quoting Abraham Lincoln: “Let the people know the facts and
the country will be safe.” But the rise of MAGA fascism challenged my
faith in journalism’s ability to arm Americans with the facts they need to
do the right thing.

It wasn’t all the media’s fault, though. They gave the public plenty of
reasons to reject an obvious con artist in 2016 and to reject him again in
2024 after he attempted a coup and was convicted of 34 felonies.

Much of the media failed in those elections, and only a portion of them
seem to have learned anything. To its credit, CNN called the Timmy-Tammy
thing “an outlandish lie.” But other major news outlets are still too
soft. The New York Times described Musk’s claim that he wasn’t MAGA as a
“pivot” when it was obviously just a brazen attempt to deny the past.
Yesterday, the Times published a fact-check article on Stephen Miller’s
“egregious falsehoods,” but still wouldn’t use the word “lie.”

When I brought up the Times’ aversion to that word with assistant managing
editor Patrick Healy in a recent video discussion, he said “we aren’t
leaning into language” like that.

He explained: “If the New York Times was using the word ‘lie’ 20 times in
an article or multiple times on the front page, don’t you think that would
change, not just people’s sense of our own fairness and what we were
focusing on, but also lose the potency of the word itself?”

I responded: “So you’re saying you want to retain the potency of the word
‘lie’ by not using it?”

This post-midterms period is a crucial time for the media to defend
democracy. MAGA is on the run, having earned every bit of the humiliation
it is suffering, but we’re not out of the woods yet. The regime will cause
even more damage as long as it’s in power. The Trump-backed reinstatement
of Nvidia CEO and national security threat Jensen Huang is an example of
that.

Still, truth and accountability are making a comeback. When the new
Democrat-led Congress takes over in January, there will be a torrent of
subpoenas seeking to expose the facts behind the Nvidia scandal and other
aspects of the regime’s corruption.

Democrats at congressional hearings have already started asking Trump
nominees who won the 2020 election, exposing their unwillingness to admit
a basic truth. When Michael LoSapio told senators he didn’t think Jan. 6
was an “attack,” his dishonesty cost him. Thom Tillis, a North Carolina
Republican who will leave the Senate in January, put a hold on confirming
LoSapio, apparently dooming the nomination.

Some of the media are getting with the program too. Yesterday, ABC’s
Jonathan Karl played the LoSapio video for Jay Clayton, director of
national intelligence, and asked him the same question.

Karl: “Was there an attack on the Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021?”

Clayton: “I’m not going to relitigate that issue here.”

Karl: “I’m not asking you to relitigate it. I’m just asking if it
happened.”

Clayton: “The American people saw what happened that day. It was a very
unfortunate day for America ... but I’m not going to get into the political
characterizations.”

Karl pressed him repeatedly to call it an attack. The person in charge of
“national intelligence” played dumb. The regime is telling us it can’t be
believed, and that message is reaching more Americans.

The odious Stephen Miller said Friday that “the next two years are going
to be the greatest two years in American history.” If the country commits
to the truth, he may be right. If we punish the people who have tried to
defraud us with propaganda about Timmy and Tammy, the regime will lose the
power to destroy our country with its lies. Instead, it will destroy
itself.

body:
# [](https://act.janepac.com/go/30?t=1&akid=49%2E6803%2EQ4xcOa)
Jane Fonda here. It is with great pride that I’m announcing my support of Chris Van Hollen as the next Senate Majority Leader.
[](https://act.janepac.com/survey/ms_jfcp_em_20261124?source=em20261124-49&t=3&akid=49%2E6803%2EQ4xcOa)
**[Now, I’d like to hear from you. Do you believe it’s time for new leadership? Click here to join me in endorsing Chris Van Hollen for Senate Majority Leader.](https://act.janepac.com/survey/ms_jfcp_em_20261124?source=em20261124-49&t=4&akid=49%2E6803%2EQ4xcOa)**
This was an easy choice for me. The American people delivered a clear mandate on Election Day – one that I heard every time I sat down with voters this year.
_Enough of the status quo. Enough of corporate handouts. Enough of a politics that hasn’t served people for far too long._
I made a promise when I started this work that I’d fight like hell for what’s right, that I’d listen to the will of the people. So that’s exactly what I’m doing.
In a post-election poll of JanePAC supporters, over 87 percent said they wanted someone else as Senate Majority Leader, and I agree.
Corporate Democrats have sold out our communities for far too long. When I look at Chris Van Hollen’s record in Congress, I have no doubt in my mind that he’s the right guy for the job.
In Congress, he:
* **Proposed the Polluters Pay Climate Fund Act** , a bill that would hold corporate polluters accountable by requiring fossil fuel companies and oil refiners to pay into a fund to address the impacts of climate change.
* **Introduced the Power to the People Act** , a bill that would require AI data centers to supply their own power so residential ratepayers don’t absorb those costs in their utility bills.

That’s my kind of leader — unafraid of going toe-to-toe with powerful interests. It’s that very fearlessness voters demanded from our elected officials this November.
**I’ve been a proud Democrat all my life. But loyalty to our party should never come at the expense of the people we’re elected to serve. Being a Democrat means turning toward people, not turning our backs on them.**
**[So, as one of our top supporters, I want to hear from YOU. Do you support Chris Van Hollen as the next Senate Majority Leader? Please add your signature today on behalf of your community in Cresco. I'm counting on lots of us to make our voices heard.](https://act.janepac.com/survey/ms_jfcp_em_20261124?source=em20261124-49&t=5&akid=49%2E6803%2EQ4xcOa)**
**[Add my name ››](https://act.janepac.com/survey/ms_jfcp_em_20261124?source=em20261124-49&t=6&akid=49%2E6803%2EQ4xcOa)**
Thank you for signing,
Jane Fonda
[](https://act.janepac.com/survey/ms_jfcp_em_20261124?source=em20261124-49&t=7&akid=49%2E6803%2EQ4xcOa)
**Before you go...** We couldn’t be prouder of this movement. 226 climate champions elected. Over 55 seats flipped. But the fossil fuel industry isn't taking a day off, and neither can we. name: Chad Bianco
subject: Don't Believe the Headlines
body:
Sacramento's crime numbers don't match what my deputies see every day.

| | | | | |
---
| |

My fellow Californians,
Last week Sacramento put out a press release bragging about "record low crime" in California. I'd love for that to be true. But that's not what my deputies are seeing.
They're seeing the same repeat offenders arrested again and again. **Retail theft crews are hitting store after store. One ring was just tied to 24 burglaries across the state. And fentanyl is still taking our kids.** Crime numbers look a lot better when people stop reporting crimes because nothing happens to the criminals.
**Here in Riverside County, we don't spin numbers. We make arrests.** Just last week, my deputies ran a single operation in Perris and arrested eight shoplifters.
That's how you keep a community safe. You enforce the law, and you stand behind the men and women who do it. If you believe California needs sheriffs who still enforce the law, I'd be grateful to have you with me. **I am running for re-election as Sheriff of Riverside County, and I would be grateful for your support.**
God bless you, and God bless Riverside County.
**Sheriff Chad Bianco
Riverside County**

_**[How to Plan for Healthcare Costs in Retirement](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskL2u4yAUhJ8GukT8GUxBsVKULttuaR3MIWGFwcJHifbtV77VfYBbz8yn0ffnsTyg1NKev2HDQLkvCVNZgTAtDT9HRSIcy16htf7JfQykMnDDRi-ESosSyl6kvCjzbSl5ChlRoeYYpPPTZKwXgr8CCIc-pxjjLF2OXnhjBc5-nicdYRK8hJMopTLSC6ndVc7eGQVWWlhNjIoZgalQH9e_vZwvcv3X3ziua994DS-i_WD6F1N3pu47brEi9ZZLg7YWqGftzPQdmL5JM09M2ZXpm9LaO6bsIZm-NaDSG1Q-Qto_pdZyWMeMeG5QvhCcflDWO6j_AQAA__-NKYGa)**_ from todays sponsor Fisher Investments to explore Medicare, long-term care and ways to fund future medical needs for the new year. -- Cole, _CEO_

Health care is one of the biggest costs many retirees face. subject: Redistricting update: Dummymanders, the 2030 Census, and what it all means
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
This cycle proved that maps matter, but they don’t ultimately wholly decide elections.
#
Hi there,
After the 2024 election, Republicans used their power in states like Texas, North Carolina, Tennessee, and others to redraw congressional maps in their own favor. Their goal was to make it easier to win more House seats for years to come, in order to build a stronghold of Republican governing power.
**But then Election Day 2026 happened, and Republicans’ efforts didn’t go quite as planned.**
**Let’s talk about what we saw happen on November 3rd—and what that means for Republicans and Democrats going forward.**
To draw more Republican-leaning congressional districts, Republicans often had to shift Democratic votes into safely red seats. Republicans’ hubris made them believe that weakening safer districts would not make them competitive, but in a wave election like this one, Democratic candidates were able to pull off wins in these unfairly drawn congressional districts, sometimes referred to as a “dummymander.”
Here’s a deeper look at how redistricting played out across states:
* **North Carolina:** Republicans drew a map meant to give them 11 out of 14 seats. **Democrats are on track to win 11** instead.

* **Texas:** Republicans redrew districts in an attempt to flip five more seats red, but **Democrats ended up gaining one** on Election Day.

* **Florida:** Democrats held all four seats Republicans targeted in their redraw, and came close to **unseating three Republicans** , too.

* **Alabama:** Republicans used the Supreme Court’s decision in _Louisiana v. Callais_ to reinstitute their previously illegal congressional map. The old map limited Democrats to one congressional seat, down from the two they hold now, but the **incumbent Democrat in Alabama’s 2nd Congressional District, Representative Shomari Figures, held on.**

* **Tennessee:** Republicans redrew their map to try to eliminate the lone Democrat-held seat in the state. They picked up one seat but are on track to lose another, so there was **no net gain for either party.**

* **Utah:** A court-ordered map created a new district, and **Democrats won it.**

* **California:** Proposition 50 worked exactly as intended, and **Democrats gained five seats.**

* **Louisiana:** Louisiana Republicans redrew maps to try to eliminate one of their two Democrat-held congressional seats. **This is the only state still undecided** , with runoffs in the weeks ahead after close midterm races.

Republicans didn’t get the gains they had planned for through gerrymandering this year, but that doesn’t mean the underlying problem has gone away. Democrats are still competing on a congressional map that gives Republicans a significant structural advantage, and we have every reason to expect them to keep trying to expand that advantage with more mid-decade redistricting.
In Mississippi, GOP Governor Tate Reeves has already declared he intends to call a special session of the legislature to draw new maps in the state. And in _every_ state, the 2030 elections will decide which party draws the maps for the _next decade_ after the 2030 U.S. Census.
The expanded coalition of voters who helped overcome these Republican-drawn gerrymanders in 2026 might not be enough to withstand the challenges ahead—which include Trump not being on the ballot in 2028 and governing in divided government for the next two years. We need to expand it and make it stronger by reaching voters Democrats have traditionally overlooked or written off, and by persuading people who don’t yet agree with us, especially on issues where voters trust Democrats least.
To do that, Democrats need to harness our strategic advantage—people power—to pursue five interconnected priorities:
1. Show that Democratic governance can materially improve people's lives.
2. Hold Republican elected leaders accountable.
3. Invest in the slow, patient work of changing public opinion where Democrats are electorally weakest.
4. Lean into one of Democrats’ greatest strategic advantages: grassroots volunteers who are clamoring to do more.
5. Start building now for the 2028 general election.

[**If you’re ready to support that work, consider making a donation of $25 to Swing Left so we can keep helping Democrats win in competitive elections, no matter how the lines are drawn.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=groundtruth-2025-sl.QSDeHu&amount=25&%3Butm_source=ak&%3Butm_medium=em&%3Butm_campaign=redistricting-2026&%3Butm_content=20261124-1&%3Brefcode=ak_em_redistricting-2026_20261124-1&t=2&akid=3479%2E1562180%2EFZx7Ho)

Thank you, as always, for everything you do,
The Swing Left Political Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20261124-1&t=23&refcode2=3479_1562180_FZx7Ho&akid=3479%2E1562180%2EFZx7Ho)

| | | Friend, it's Chuck Schumer.

_We did it._ We defeated Trump's cronies, elected strong Democrats across the country, and took back the Senate. **But if we don’t deliver, all this will go away.**

Now that Democrats have a majority, we'll need a sharp, intelligent strategy to turn our Senate victory into action. **As a top grassroots Democrat, you have a part to play here.**

**[Throughout my years in leadership, I've seen firsthand how valuable up‐to‐the‐minute input from supporters like you can be. So please, will you take my Democratic Strategy Survey today and help keep the Senate blue to make a real difference for America?](http://go.dscc.org/go/24602?ask=7&t=5&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-ND-20261124-ChuckSchumer-SchumerNewMajorityStrategySurvey-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-ND-20261124-ChuckSchumer-SchumerNewMajorityStrategySurvey-Pros-sl1&akid=27601%2E9716520%2EBQxMDv)**

Let's face it: Trump's second administration has been _even more disastrous_ than his first. His policies are hurting Americans all over ‐‐ and that's why voters chose change.

But with so many Americans counting on Senate Democrats to get our country back on track, **we can't afford any missteps. The riskiest thing we could do is fail to deliver what the people expect of us.**

**To keep America moving forward, and to keep the Senate blue, I'm relying on your advice. So now's the time to have your say:**

**[Will you spend a few minutes taking my Democratic strategy survey before it closes at midnight?](http://go.dscc.org/go/24602?ask=7&t=7&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-ND-20261124-ChuckSchumer-SchumerNewMajorityStrategySurvey-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-ND-20261124-ChuckSchumer-SchumerNewMajorityStrategySurvey-Pros-sl1&akid=27601%2E9716520%2EBQxMDv)**

name: Lacy Lunsford
subject: The man I love is facing the fight of his life.
body:
I never imagined I would be writing a letter like this.

I'm a wife and a mother, not an activist. But today I'm asking for your help because the man I love is facing the fight of his life.
| | |
---
| | | Dear Fellow Patriot,I never imagined I would be writing a letter like this. I'm a wife and a mother, not an activist. But today I'm asking for your help because the man I love is facing the fight of his life.My husband, Officer Brad Lunsford, will soon be back in court defending himself against charges that never should have been brought in the first place.And the legal bills continue to pile up. [**That's why I'm asking you to make a generous contribution to the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF) today.**](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckcuOmzAUhp_G7IjwlbBgkQ6hikSqahbp0nLsY-KRLwgb-voV084LdHf06zuXT-fXXd6V8y7OP1SAXu9OrlmWFwQVnU87uGyVdnEuL7BulqQhosa4JkwqXdwOkqnK9NoISirocdtxzjqOefXq8dOYjuiOcjDPtjWCGQrWWta0wgDrKtcf4zAmDHeMY3Y6nxnHllvVaEGZoog122JUgXzSKWZYd3XsdDGmo0rxpFOofP8qZcmIXhAZERkz6G2Fk4pgUjkIREYP3lhExkUZ8gRdW8pFzT7CB20MouNWgsxpWzUgOrxfH4iIIwpg3BYQHa73y236F2oVFuXmiOjw93x8lt-G73K6TsMo368P-UnLaSKi_nmp3x63r84UC8SC6PD2uNVf7tXam-W3895l0SLWzEE5_ylW_vMfe0_-BAAA____RJfM) Brad has spent his entire adult life serving others. He's a proud Army combat veteran. A devoted husband and father. And for more than ten years, he served as a police officer with the Las Cruces Police Department.Then one afternoon everything changed. A robbery suspect attacked Brad's partner and knocked him to the pavement. During the struggle, the suspect gained control of the officer's taser and pointed it directly at him.In a matter of seconds, Brad was forced to make the decision no officer ever wants to make.He fired a single shot. His partner survived and went home to his wife and newborn baby. But our family's nightmare was only beginning.Because more than a year later, Attorney General Raul Torrez charged Brad with manslaughter. **To put New Mexico politics into context for you – Torrez is notoriously anti-cop and his campaign was bankrolled by leftist billionaire George Soros.**_The same George Soros who, for the past decade, has spent tens of millions of dollars installing his hand-picked, police-hating puppets into prosecutors’ offices across America._ What followed was a trial filled with troubling questions and irregularities that ultimately resulted in Brad's conviction – **including a juror who failed to disclose their ties to Black Lives Matter.** Since the trial was overturned, Torrez and his junior Attorney General, R. John Duran II, have doubled down his desire to see my husband behind bars – and will use the full resources of the state government to finish the job.Now we're preparing for the next chapter of this fight.And we can't do it alone.**[That’s why I’m asking you to donate $25, $50, $100, or more to LELDF today.](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckcuOmzAUhp_G7IjwlbBgkQ6hikSqahbp0nLsY-KRLwgb-voV084LdHf06zuXT-fXXd6V8y7OP1SAXu9OrlmWFwQVnU87uGyVdnEuL7BulqQhosa4JkwqXdwOkqnK9NoISirocdtxzjqOefXq8dOYjuiOcjDPtjWCGQrWWta0wgDrKtcf4zAmDHeMY3Y6nxnHllvVaEGZoog122JUgXzSKWZYd3XsdDGmo0rxpFOofP8qZcmIXhAZERkz6G2Fk4pgUjkIREYP3lhExkUZ8gRdW8pFzT7CB20MouNWgsxpWzUgOrxfH4iIIwpg3BYQHa73y236F2oVFuXmiOjw93x8lt-G73K6TsMo368P-UnLaSKi_nmp3x63r84UC8SC6PD2uNVf7tXam-W3895l0SLWzEE5_ylW_vMfe0_-BAAA____RJfM)** For over 30 years, LELDF has helped wrongly accused and convicted officers, like Brad, clear their names and win back their freedoms. From trials to appeals, and even presidential pardons, LELDF has a long track record of success.But they don’t receive taxpayer funding or grants, and large gifts are few and far between. Instead, LELDF relies on people like you who are sick and tired of progressive prosecutors trying to ruin the lives of good officers with bogus charges and witch-hunts.Brad’s first trial cost hundreds of thousands of dollars. With the games Torrez’s office is playing, we anticipate a second trial will cost even more. But your gift today ensures Brad receives the legal defense he deserves – not only at trial, but during this critical waiting period when Brad’s attorneys work to get the case dismissed.And believe me, they are working hard filing motions and investigating the corruption! [**So, can I count on you to make a generous, tax-deductible donation to LELDF today?**](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckcuOmzAUhp_G7IjwlbBgkQ6hikSqahbp0nLsY-KRLwgb-voV084LdHf06zuXT-fXXd6V8y7OP1SAXu9OrlmWFwQVnU87uGyVdnEuL7BulqQhosa4JkwqXdwOkqnK9NoISirocdtxzjqOefXq8dOYjuiOcjDPtjWCGQrWWta0wgDrKtcf4zAmDHeMY3Y6nxnHllvVaEGZoog122JUgXzSKWZYd3XsdDGmo0rxpFOofP8qZcmIXhAZERkz6G2Fk4pgUjkIREYP3lhExkUZ8gRdW8pFzT7CB20MouNWgsxpWzUgOrxfH4iIIwpg3BYQHa73y236F2oVFuXmiOjw93x8lt-G73K6TsMo368P-UnLaSKi_nmp3x63r84UC8SC6PD2uNVf7tXam-W3895l0SLWzEE5_ylW_vMfe0_-BAAA____RJfM) Remember, the prosecution has unlimited taxpayer resources. Brad does not. Your gift today could be the difference between a strong defense and the next 11 years in prison.Thank you in advance for standing with my husband and backing the blue.Gratefully,
---
**_Lacy Lunsford_**
---

Derek, Voters across Virginia and America sent a clear message in the midterms: they want leaders who will tackle the high cost of living _and_ hold this administration accountable. People keep asking if Democrats should focus on investigating corruption or delivering for working families. **My answer is that we can, and should, do both.** We can't let Donald Trump and his allies get away with self-dealing, reckless tariffs, and unconstitutional wars without real congressional oversight. And we have to stay laser-focused on lowering costs for everyday people, from groceries and housing to energy bills and health care. _There is no justice without accountability, and no progress without oversight._ As we prepare to take the majority and set our agenda for the year ahead, I want to hear directly from you. **[Will you take a few minutes to fill out my priorities survey and tell me what matters most to you?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143997818/662074353/-835206058?refcode=261124em_tk_surv&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDQvMS84ODkyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1NTA1MjY5My0zZmU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=s3UZxNIPKBcV08bvRclkYWSgm_jfqaKEefD3_wCWIAE=&emci=780fa879-2de8-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=55052693-3fe8-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=1801409)**

subject: Never in a MILLION years
body:
| | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143997948/662074817/115703642?refcode=261124_moore_thanksgiving&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZTA1MGU3OS00MGU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=jdhBeznN9jTATuAWcbRRFyhIOKJf-mb78OrIckhZMBU=)

This Thanksgiving, I'm so beyond thankful for this movement.
This is Rep. Patricia "Pat" Moore (D-LA), and I want to tell you something I don't say often enough.
I grew up in public housing. When I was a girl, nobody looked at me and saw a future member of Congress. Honestly, I didn't either – I’m only in this place because of the help of my family, my community, and my faith.
And yet here I am, 18 days away from becoming the first Black woman Louisiana has EVER sent to Congress.
I never expected to be standing on this doorstep. And I know exactly who carried me here: you.
More than 156,000 contributions to this historic campaign. All fueled by teachers. Nurses. Retirees. Doctors. Janitors. Folks from every corner of this country, giving what they can, when they can.
_**Our average donation? Just $17.**_
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143997949/662074818/115703642?refcode=261124_moore_thanksgiving&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZTA1MGU3OS00MGU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=jdhBeznN9jTATuAWcbRRFyhIOKJf-mb78OrIckhZMBU=)

This campaign doesn't belong to anybody powerful. It belongs to the people.
And that's exactly what scares the other side.
Right now, Super PACs, corporate special interests, and data center companies are lining up to buy this race. They think a seat in Congress is just another thing that's for sale.
We're going to prove them wrong. Dead wrong.
[**So this Thanksgiving week, I'm asking: Will you chip in $17, our average donation, to my campaign and Equal Opportunity Now to show this seat isn't for sale? And if $17 is too much right now, even $1 sends the same message. Every single gift is a vote of confidence that this race will be decided by folks like you, not by the highest bidder.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143997951/662074820/115703642?refcode=261124_moore_thanksgiving&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZTA1MGU3OS00MGU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=jdhBeznN9jTATuAWcbRRFyhIOKJf-mb78OrIckhZMBU=)

clean_body: | | | | = This Thanksgiving, I'm so beyond thankful for this movement. This is Rep. Patricia "Pat" Moore (D-LA), and I want to tell you something I don't say often enough. I grew up in public housing. When I was a girl, nobody looked at me and saw a future member of Congress. Honestly, I didn't either – I’m only in this place because of the help of my family, my community, and my faith. And yet here I am, 18 days away from becoming the first Black woman Louisiana has EVER sent to Congress. I never expected to be standing on this doorstep. And I know exactly who carried me here: you. More than 156,000 contributions to this historic campaign. All fueled by teachers. Nurses. Retirees. Doctors. Janitors. Folks from every corner of this country, giving what they can, when they can. Our average donation? Just $17. = = This campaign doesn't belong to anybody powerful. It belongs to the people. And that's exactly what scares the other side. Right now, Super PACs, corporate special interests, and data center companies are lining up to buy this race. They think a seat in Congress is just another thing that's for sale. We're going to prove them wrong. Dead wrong. = = | | | With gratitude, Rep. body:
The SAFE AI Act and the Remote Access Security Act.

| | The ARI Briefing | [](https://us.list-manage.com/3kUOReExAzo?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---|---
# Congress Gets to Work on AI
The SAFE AI Act, the remote access loophole, chip smuggling, and energy security
Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia has added another twist to a scandal that has put the company's China business and connections to chip smuggling under intense scrutiny. At stake are America's national security and the need for effective oversight of its most powerful technology companies.
As Congress builds support in the NDAA for export controls that crack down on smuggling, another accountability effort is underway in the House focused on the frontier labs. **Up first in this week 's briefing: the SAFE AI Act, a bipartisan proposal endorsed by ARI that would make frontier AI safety standards legally binding, require independent evaluations, and put government oversight behind company commitments.** It's a serious framework for lawmakers to tackle AI safety concerns as we head toward the 120th Congress.
[](https://us.list-manage.com/665srpr44FS?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
In this week's briefing, we'll also cover the push to close the remote access loophole, calls for a Justice Department investigation into Nvidia, and the recent relaunch of the Center for Responsible Innovation (CRI). Here's the latest.
| | Frontier AI | 01
---|---
## A Bipartisan Plan to Make AI Safety Rules Binding
ARI endorses the SAFE AI Act from Reps. Jacobs, Maloy, and Beyer
[](https://us.list-manage.com/dRwy8r_hsGC?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
Late last week, Reps. Sara Jacobs (D-CA), Celeste Maloy (R-UT), and Don Beyer (D-VA) released details of the Safe and Accountable Federal Evaluations of Artificial Intelligence (SAFE AI) Act, a bipartisan framework to address the risks of rapidly advancing AI. [ARI endorsed the proposal](https://us.list-manage.com/14M0Ne9NHH2?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), which reflects the principles in ARI's [Blueprint for AI Governance](https://us.list-manage.com/16_sQVbA5Cs?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf).
Unlike the current regime of voluntary company commitments, the standards proposed under the SAFE AI Act would be legally binding and couldn't be loosened by the companies on their own. Under the proposal:
| Government-set standardsThe Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) would set minimum requirements for AI developers' safety frameworks.
---
Testing before releaseFederal evaluation teams or accredited independent verifiers would check models for compliance before commercial release or broad internal access.
Incident reportingDevelopers would have to report safety incidents, including those involving an imminent risk of severe harm.
Whistleblower protectionsWhistleblowers would be protected and could report incidents to CAISI.
A federal floorStates could still adopt stronger protections and regulate AI models and developers the bill doesn't reach.
As the 120th Congress takes shape, lawmakers are preparing to legislate on AI. A year of AI incidents and voter demands for tech accountability in the midterm elections have given them a mandate to act. The SAFE AI Act gives them a foundation to build on: a detailed, bipartisan framework with binding safety standards, pre-release testing, and enforcement for the most advanced AI systems.
[Read ARI's statement ->](https://us.list-manage.com/aqdIZcldTOu?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
| | National Security | 02
---|---
## Closing the Remote Access Loophole
Congress can strengthen export controls by cracking down on remote access
[](https://us.list-manage.com/KpPq91a4HZw?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
U.S. export controls block China from buying America's most advanced AI chips, but they don't cover remote access. That gap has reportedly let Chinese tech giants like Alibaba and ByteDance rent advanced U.S. chips through data centers in other countries ([Politico](https://us.list-manage.com/VrslyaGmKKb?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)).
It's an issue that threatens to undermine America's lead in developing AI. While China can compete with or even outcompete the United States in access to data, energy, and talent, the United States has a multi-year lead in designing the advanced chips necessary to develop the next generation of AI technology. And while the U.S. is cracking down on chip sales and smuggling to countries of concern, China has found a backdoor: renting compute access from data centers abroad built on American chips.
Here's the good news: Last week the Commerce Department [issued a rule](https://us.list-manage.com/8w3DN8ECy0V?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) requiring licenses for advanced AI chips sold to overseas data centers that rent significant computing power to Chinese companies. ARI [called the rule an important step](https://us.list-manage.com/huXyVjQSKHA?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) and urged Congress to build on it.
"The Trump administration's new rule limiting China's access to America's computing power is an important step toward securing America's AI lead. Congress must now build on that progress by passing the Remote Access Security Act to close the cloud loophole."ARI, on the Commerce Department's new rule
---
As Congress considers this year's National Defense Authorization Act, lawmakers have a chance to close the loophole for good. Under consideration in the NDAA is a provision that would write remote access into export control law itself, giving the Commerce Department clear authority to regulate access to controlled chips through the cloud. The House [passed a similar bill, the Remote Access Security Act, 369-22](https://us.list-manage.com/13hoSmYjxIN?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) in January, led by Rep. Mike Lawler (R-NY). While a bipartisan Senate companion has yet to get a vote, congressional negotiators are now [considering attaching its language](https://us.list-manage.com/pQt_6nkeTbw?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) to the NDAA.
ARI has pressed the case all month, from our [explainer on how the loophole works](https://us.list-manage.com/Sw7DSA09Ce9?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) to ARI President Brad Carson's [interview on Bloomberg TV](https://us.list-manage.com/j3msRCzvOPo?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf). Congress should act to close the loophole.
[See how the loophole works ->](https://us.list-manage.com/M8OFCe6g3Rw?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
| | Chip Security | 03
---|---
## National Security Leaders Urge DOJ to Investigate Nvidia
15 national security and AI policy leaders ask the Justice Department to examine what Nvidia knew about chip smuggling to China
[](https://us.list-manage.com/TMZkh3ozgmK?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
On November 18, 15 national security and AI policy leaders, including a former CIA inspector general, a retired Army major general, and former Rep. Chris Stewart (R-UT), [sent a letter](https://us.list-manage.com/1p03zz714cN?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) urging Attorney General Todd Blanche to investigate Nvidia's knowledge of, and response to, illegal smuggling operations diverting controlled chips to China. ARI President Brad Carson and Vice President of Policy Morgan Plummer signed the letter.
Over the past year, the Justice Department has uncovered multiple smuggling operations, including a scheme in which prosecutors allege [at least $510 million](https://us.list-manage.com/umr1Aj1GiOz?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) worth of servers with advanced chips were illegally sent to China. As the letter notes, those cases alone don't establish that Nvidia broke the law. But companies that sell export-controlled technology are responsible for investigating red flags that customers may be diverting it.
"We urge the Department to follow the evidence wherever it leads and pursue appropriate enforcement action where violations are established. Protecting America's technological advantage requires confidence that our export controls are enforced throughout the supply chain."From the November 18 letter to the Attorney General
---
[Read the letter ->](https://us.list-manage.com/euI4T4gCRf7?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
| | Data Centers | 04
---|---
## Helping Communities Negotiate Better Data Center Deals
ARI applauds the bipartisan, bicameral Data Center Community Empowerment Act
[](https://us.list-manage.com/XqYzbC8A_EP?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
On November 18, Reps. Sam Liccardo (D-CA), Nick Begich (R-AK), Erin Houchin (R-IN), and Scott Peters (D-CA) [introduced](https://us.list-manage.com/BYHAWXr46t7?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) the Data Center Community Empowerment Act. The bill would create a Department of Energy program to give local governments the technical expertise to negotiate favorable data center deals. It's the House companion to a [bipartisan Senate bill](https://us.list-manage.com/HCMra8ZrQS8?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) from Sens. John Curtis (R-UT) and Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE).
"Hyperscale data center developers with enormous resources are coming into communities where local leaders do not have the experience or staff to rival them. Every day, officials are leaving community benefits on the table because they are outmatched, and Congress can empower them to do more."Brad Carson, ARI President, in [ARI's statement](https://us.list-manage.com/IrpAnpbOENF?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
The bill puts into practice an idea from ARI's call for a [Data Center Fair Deal](https://us.list-manage.com/mlt06PPYOX2?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf): a federal assistance program that puts power back in the hands of communities in the data center buildout.
[Read ARI's statement ->](https://us.list-manage.com/5Of_frdE6xu?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
| | Inside ARI | 05
---|---
## A New Research Agenda and Open Roles
CRI relaunches, and ARI is hiring
[](https://us.list-manage.com/13dqooUIL4_?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)
---
This month, the Center for Responsible Innovation (CRI), ARI's sister research organization, [relaunched](https://us.list-manage.com/rtVLbx8Z_7A?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf) with a new research agenda in development and plans to bring on new staff. Justin Bullock is leading development of the agenda as CRI's Head of Research. CRI's mission is to develop concrete AI policy proposals that can serve as ready-made solutions as emerging AI capabilities change the landscape.
ARI is hiring too, including a director to lead our national security policy work. If someone in your network belongs on our team, please pass these along.
| Now hiring[NSSC Policy Director/Senior Policy Director](https://us.list-manage.com/5nNF_hk07XJ?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), ARI office
---
Now hiring[Regional Director of State Government Affairs](https://us.list-manage.com/DXj9dY4ZNU7?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), ARI office or remote
Now hiring[Associate, Development & External Relations](https://us.list-manage.com/9nWpD1bQU2P?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf), San Francisco Bay Area
[See open roles ->](https://us.list-manage.com/pQrmuAF4zXw?e=a07d75591f&c2id=4fb88adb36cbae4881a2e5f253eb58cf)

Under the proposal: | Government-set standardsThe Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) would set minimum requirements for AI developers' safety frameworks. Testing before releaseFederal evaluation teams or accredited independent verifiers would check models for compliance before commercial release or broad internal access. Incident reportingDevelopers would have to report safety incidents, including those involving an imminent risk of severe harm. Whistleblower protectionsWhistleblowers would be protected and could report incidents to CAISI. A federal floorStates could still adopt stronger protections and regulate AI models and developers the bill doesn't reach. As the 120th Congress takes shape, lawmakers are preparing to legislate on AI. A year of AI incidents and voter demands for tech accountability in the midterm elections have given them a mandate to act. The SAFE AI Act gives them a foundation to build on: a detailed, bipartisan framework with binding safety standards, pre-release testing, and enforcement for the most advanced AI systems. | | National Security | 02 ---|--- Closing the Remote Access Loophole Congress can strengthen export controls by cracking down on remote access U.S. export controls block China from buying America's most advanced AI chips, but they don't cover remote access. That gap has reportedly let Chinese tech giants like Alibaba and ByteDance rent advanced U.S. chips through data centers in other countries (). It's an issue that threatens to undermine America's lead in developing AI. While China can compete with or even outcompete the United States in access to data, energy, and talent, the United States has a multi-year lead in designing the advanced chips necessary to develop the next generation of AI technology. And while the U.S. is cracking down on chip sales and smuggling to countries of concern, China has found a backdoor: renting compute access from data centers abroad built on American chips. Here's the good news: Last week the Commerce Department requiring licenses for advanced AI chips sold to overseas data centers that rent significant computing power to Chinese companies. ARI and urged Congress to build on it. "The Trump administration's new rule limiting China's access to America's computing power is an important step toward securing America's AI lead. Congress must now build on that progress by passing the Remote Access Security Act to close the cloud loophole."ARI, on the Commerce Department's new rule As Congress considers this year's National Defense Authorization Act, lawmakers have a chance to close the loophole for good. Under consideration in the NDAA is a provision that would write remote access into export control law itself, giving the Commerce Department clear authority to regulate access to controlled chips through the cloud. The House in January, led by Rep. Mike Lawler (R-NY). While a bipartisan Senate companion has yet to get a vote, congressional negotiators are now to the NDAA. ARI has pressed the case all month, from our to ARI President Brad Carson's . Congress should act to close the loophole. | | Chip Security | 03 ---|--- National Security Leaders Urge DOJ to Investigate Nvidia 15 national security and AI policy leaders ask the Justice Department to examine what Nvidia knew about chip smuggling to China On November 18, 15 national security and AI policy leaders, including a former CIA inspector general, a retired Army major general, and former Rep. Chris Stewart (R-UT), urging Attorney General Todd Blanche to investigate Nvidia's knowledge of, and response to, illegal smuggling operations diverting controlled chips to China. ARI President Brad Carson and Vice President of Policy Morgan Plummer signed the letter. Over the past year, the Justice Department has uncovered multiple smuggling operations, including a scheme in which prosecutors allege worth of servers with advanced chips were illegally sent to China. As the letter notes, those cases alone don't establish that Nvidia broke the law. But companies that sell export-controlled technology are responsible for investigating red flags that customers may be diverting it. "We urge the Department to follow the evidence wherever it leads and pursue appropriate enforcement action where violations are established. Protecting America's technological advantage requires confidence that our export controls are enforced throughout the supply chain."From the November 18 letter to the Attorney General | | Data Centers | 04 ---|--- Helping Communities Negotiate Better Data Center Deals ARI applauds the bipartisan, bicameral Data Center Community Empowerment Act On November 18, Reps. Sam Liccardo (D-CA), Nick Begich (R-AK), Erin Houchin (R-IN), and Scott Peters (D-CA) the Data Center Community Empowerment Act. The bill would create a Department of Energy program to give local governments the technical expertise to negotiate favorable data center deals. It's the House companion to a from Sens. John Curtis (R-UT) and Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE). "Hyperscale data center developers with enormous resources are coming into communities where local leaders do not have the experience or staff to rival them. Every day, officials are leaving community benefits on the table because they are outmatched, and Congress can empower them to do more."Brad Carson, ARI President, in The bill puts into practice an idea from ARI's call for a : a federal assistance program that puts power back in the hands of communities in the data center buildout. | | Inside ARI | 05 ---|--- A New Research Agenda and Open Roles CRI relaunches, and ARI is hiring This month, the Center for Responsible Innovation (CRI), ARI's sister research organization, with a new research agenda in development and plans to bring on new staff. Justin Bullock is leading development of the agenda as CRI's Head of Research. CRI's mission is to develop concrete AI policy proposals that can serve as ready-made solutions as emerging AI capabilities change the landscape. ARI is hiring too, including a director to lead our national security policy work. If someone in your network belongs on our team, please pass these along. | Now hiring, ARI office Now hiring, ARI office or remote Now hiring, San Francisco Bay Area | Voters asked for AI rules in November, and Congress is starting to write them. As the new Congress takes shape, ARI will keep pushing for binding safety standards, effective export controls, and a fair deal for communities. Thank you for being part of ARI's work.Onward,The ARI Team | Americans for Responsible InnovationAdvancing AI policy that serves the public interest. | ---|--- Americans for Responsible Innovation 750 17th St NW, Suite 1200 Washington, DC 20006 *

name: OnePA Team
subject: Tell school boards to stand up to Moms for Liberty
body:
Moms for Liberty is using artificial intelligence to track school board agendas and send its chapters after inclusive curriculum and student protections. | |
---
Peter, **When Moms for Liberty brought its national convention to Philadelphia, OnePA members were outside protesting.** Donald Trump and Ron DeSantis came to speak to the group, and our members made sure everyone knew our city stands with Black and brown students, LGBTQ+ students, and children from immigrant families. We told Moms for Liberty they could take their hate elsewhere because it was not welcome in Philadelphia. **Now we’re joining with national allies in our fight to defend public schools and our communities from Moms for Liberty’s attacks on local schools. The group, which the Southern Poverty Law Center has labeled an anti-government extremist group, is using artificial intelligence to monitor school board agendas** and mobilize its chapters against diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts, gender policies, and curriculum changes. This right-wing hate campaign puts Black and brown students, LGBTQ+ students, and children from immigrant families directly in the crosshairs. When a school board caves, students lose access to books that reflect their lives, lessons that tell the truth about our history, and protections that help them learn safely. Moms for Liberty applies the pressure, and our kids pay for every concession. Because of the right wing movement against representation in literature and Moms For Liberty’s underhanded tactics, publishers who might otherwise want to produce quality books are being forced not to, or to do so at a loss. Peter, it’s Chauna Banks, the Democrat running for Congress in Louisiana’s 6th Congressional District.

Earlier this month, I finished first in a 10-candidate open primary, 665 votes ahead of a MAGA candidate who raised more than $7.7 million to beat me.

And now, we’re heading into a runoff election on December 12th. If we win, I’ll become the first Black woman elected to the U.S. House from Louisiana.

**But we spent every last dollar we had in our primary election, and if we don’t fill our campaign’s bank account fast, we'll risk having to shut down our operations.**

I’ll be honest, there is too much on the line here for us to fall short. That’s why I’m coming to you for your urgent support.
