Protect Kids Colorado plans Jan. 16 Capitol rally to defend Props 133,
134 and 135

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s4q91a3ab17

PRESENTED BY ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s3r381cc7ad

Hi friends!

Want the full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast
here
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s7m9a6c0f32
or watch on YouTube
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sfm75927591
or Rumble
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sdu4d40b222

🏔️ HERE IN COLORADO... Protect Kids Colorado will hold a “We
the People Rally”
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/setd68b402a
at the Capitol on Jan. 16 urging lawmakers to “respect the vote”
on Props 133, 134 and 135, with speakers including Chris Elston, Chloe
Cole and Jennifer Sey; a state hearing officer dismissed what is
believed to be the first complaint under Colorado’s deepfake law,
ruling an AI video lampooning Democratic Sen. Cathy Kipp is protected
satire
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s4l4cdfcf81
the Colorado Court of Appeals ordered 2023 Parks and Wildlife
regulations overturned after the agency disregarded 95% of public
comments
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s7m8055e15b
and Denver City Council member Shontel Lewis, backed by Denver DSA,
wants to unseat Mayor Mike Johnston
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sdn34091fb3
though Denver hasn’t ousted an incumbent mayor since 1983.

🇺🇸 ON THE NATIONAL STAGE... Nvidia’s board unanimously
reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sdi301e6a5f
after he resigned earlier this month following reports of extramarital
relationships, including one with a woman suspected to be a Chinese
spy, and shares surged 30%.

🗣️ COMMENTARY SPOTLIGHT... Mark W. Salley urges Gov.-elect Phil
Weiser and Democratic lawmakers to stand firm on Props 133, 134 and
135
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s8s8e1bd8b5
which each passed with more than 1.3 million votes; and Ray Scott
argues Colorado Republicans must fix candidate vetting
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sche592d218
before primaries after losing every statewide race.

This is your Mountain Minute for Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

– Team RMV

TODAY'S TOP STORIES

PROTECT KIDS COLORADO PLANS JAN. 16 CAPITOL RALLY TO DEFEND PROPS 133,
134 AND 135
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sfga2900507

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s4jf9681f03

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sbsfe01be12

Voters approved all three of Protect Kids Colorado’s ballot measures
in November. Now the group plans to take its case to the Capitol
steps.

PKC will hold a “We the People Rally” at the state Capitol on
Saturday, Jan. 16, according to a flyer from the group. A
family-friendly pre-rally runs from 11 a.m. to noon. The rally follows
from noon to 2 p.m.

The flyer’s message is short. “Respect the vote. Protect 133, 134,
135.”

The rally falls five days after lawmakers convene the 2027 session
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s0s377a8532
on Jan. 11. It also falls four days after Gov.-elect Phil Weiser takes
office
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s5pef986dd1
on Jan. 12.

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sfu82d84444

COLORADO REPUBLICANS MUST FIX CANDIDATE VETTING BEFORE THEY CAN
REBUILD
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s7j8d940096

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/sbu202a58e2

BY RAY SCOTT, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s2sa1ee9104

_After losing every statewide race and handing Democrats legislative
supermajorities, a GOP columnist argues the party’s rebuild must
start with how it picks and prepares candidates.
_

*
VETTING MUST HAPPEN BEFORE THE PRIMARY: The author argues Republicans
should research candidates’ professional history, finances,
litigation and public statements before investing in them, warning
that discovering problems in October is far more damaging than
catching them early, and notes Sen. Barbara Kirkmeyer herself warned a
2026 gubernatorial nominee’s background could become attack-ad
material.

*
ELECTABILITY REQUIRES MORE THAN BASE APPEAL: With more than half of
Colorado’s registered voters unaffiliated, the piece argues winning
a primary proves little, pointing to Rep. Jeff Hurd’s narrow 3rd
District win after he broke from the party on public lands sales and
touted bipartisan work with Sen. Michael Bennet as a model worth
studying.

*
A CALL FOR A REAL CANDIDATE PIPELINE: The author urges identifying and
training candidates years in advance, including opposition research on
themselves, and says the party must be willing to tell some loyal
Republicans they aren’t the right fit for a given race.

AND 135
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s3kab645a5e

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s9i5d82e9b5

BY MARK SALLEY | COMMENTARY | NOVEMBER 23

_Will you stand firm? Will you stand with the more than 1,373,000
voters who voted to protect women and children in Colorado? Are you
with the 1,373,942 who voted to protect minors from gender-mutilating
surgeries to alter their biological sex? _

THE TOLERANCE WEAPON: RED ROVER, RED ROVER — LET THE LITTLE ONES
OVER!
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/s9v69532035

BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | NOVEMBER 22

_Red Rover, Red Rover, send somebody over! Remember that childhood
game? Two teams of kids lined up facing each other, clasping hands and
cheering for someone from the other team to run over and break
through. It was a fun mix of friendly competition and teamwork —
with the occasional bruised ego or body part!_
__

NET MIGRATION PLUNGED 94% AND COMPANY EXITS DOUBLED ARRIVALS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._A/scl667660c6

BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | NOVEMBER 20

_From 2015 through 2019, Colorado had an average net gain of 37,019
people a year from other states, according to a new analysis by the
Common Sense Institute, or CSI. From 2021 through 2025, it had an
average net loss of 1,882 a year._
__

FEEL LIKE YOU HAVE A UNIQUE STORY, COMMENTARY OR TIP TO SHARE? Email
submit@rockymountainvoice.com.

🦃 DID YOU KNOW?

_FDR ACCIDENTALLY SPLIT THE COUNTRY INTO TWO THANKSGIVINGS. _In 1939,
President Franklin D. Roosevelt moved Thanksgiving a week earlier to
lengthen the Great Depression Christmas shopping season. Critics
dubbed it "Franksgiving," and 23 states rejected the change, leaving
Americans celebrating on two different Thursdays until Congress locked
in the fourth Thursday in 1941.

name: Michael Bennet
subject: Americans put their trust in us. We won’t disappoint you.
body:
The fight has only just begun:
| | |
---
Friend, I want to express my sincere gratitude for you.
The American people didn’t just give Democrats a 56-seat majority in the Senate this November – they entrusted us with a resounding mandate to steer our country on a course correction.
**Now, our job for the next two years is to prove ourselves worthy of it.**
_By lowering costs.
By ending the war.
By regulating Big Tech.
By protecting our public lands.
By expanding access to healthcare.
By reasserting our constitutional power to check the most corrupt administration in U.S. history._
So when the 120th Congress convenes with a Democratic supermajority in January, I vow to use every tool at my disposal to follow through. Until then, my top priority is to hash out a deal to keep the government open through the holidays WITHOUT providing a single cent of extra funding for President Trump's disastrous war of choice.
**But as long as Republicans are still in control, delivering the change we need will take all of us working together. **
So as we enter next month’s government funding negotiations, the best way to make it clear that _We the People_ demand an end to their lawlessness and chaos is with a surge of grassroots support. So Friend, I’m personally asking:
**[Can you please chip in $5, or anything you can spare now to my victory fund, The Colorado Way, to fuel my fight? I’m ready to get to work delivering the changes that working people in Colorado and across the country want to see, but I can’t do it without you alongside me.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143999772/662081223/-1978052288?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1651-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjgvMS83NDc5MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNmQ4ZThkZS00NWU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rLi5V81RXbgJ-EeEOdqt4CTcIh8CQ0KpyIJ6alb4mcw=)**

Dear Readers,
Can you believe the holiday season is already upon us? I feel like every year it arrives a little faster, but I'm always happy when it does. There is so much to be thankful for.
One thing that shocks me more than anything - today is Maggie's 20th birthday! She was born three weeks after our first congressional campaign, here a year later with President-elect Barack Obama (and Tinkerbell) and now a sophomore at Clemson University competing to become an officer through Air Force ROTC. Happy birthday, Mags - you and your brother Jack make me so proud!
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0a92599c-4646-4417-960e-e3241323a4e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a9a9eb3c-4c65-4df8-ab33-ac5d843a8123?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Thanksgiving has always been one of my favorite holidays. And this year, I find myself feeling especially grateful. For our family, for the friendships I've made over the years, and for the extraordinary privilege of serving a country I love so dearly. I've been fortunate to experience America in ways I never could have imagined as a kid growing up in a rowhouse in Philly and starting in community college. I've seen firsthand what makes this country so special.
One of the things I love most about America is the generosity of our people. At a time when way too many bash young Americans, I've been moved by how many young (and old) Americans dedicate their time and energy to helping others, often without expecting anything in return. To me, that's what service and citizenship are all about. And it's something we should celebrate more often.
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, over 75 million Americans volunteer each year, contributing nearly five billion hours of service. Even more encouraging, 54.2% of Americans help neighbors informally, whether running errands, caring for a home, or lending a hand when it was needed. I'll be really proud as my kids deliver turkey meals this Saturday to families in need once again through our local church community.
These days we hear so much about what divides us. We don't stop to reflect that we should be grateful in a democracy that honors the votes of the people, without violence or use of force. It's truly heartening to see that in reality more than half of Americans go out of their way to help a neighbor. We see that same spirit of generosity in parents coaching their kids' Little League teams, volunteers stocking the shelves at local food banks, and neighbors checking in on elderly friends. These people may never make the headlines, but they're making life a little better for the people around them. I can't think of a better expression of love for one's country than that.
Of course, we won't always agree on politics. That's part of living in a free country. But I've always believed that we have far more that unites us than divides us.
I learned that lesson in Iraq. The soldiers in my unit represented different regions, backgrounds, and political beliefs. Nobody asked or discussed how you voted before deciding whether you could be trusted. What mattered was your preparation, your judgment, and whether you would show up when someone needed you.
I've carried that understanding into every chapter of my public life. We should expect vigorous disagreement in a free society. But we should also remember that our shared obligations as Americans extend well beyond the issues that divide us.

# **The Stock Market is Likely Going Up - Helping Many Retirement Plans**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7d31373f-7ccc-4c40-93b4-0ab30da52ad5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

One of the benefits of a divided government is that the stock market usually does very, very well. I'm not a day trader and never will be, but when 156 million Americans own shares through retirement accounts like 401(k)s and IRAs, that's probably a good thing.
# A Debt to the Vietnam Generation
This year, I want to recognize a generation of Americans to whom I owe a particular debt: our Vietnam veterans.
More than 58,000 Americans lost their lives in Vietnam. Those who returned came home to a country deeply divided over the war, and many encountered indifference, misunderstanding, or hostility. After all they had sacrificed, they deserved to come home to a grateful nation. Too many didn't get the welcome they deserved. And yet, what so many of them chose to do next is one of the greatest examples of generosity I've witnessed in American life.
Beginning in the late 1970s, Vietnam veterans organized to demand recognition of the physical and psychological consequences of war. Their advocacy contributed to the establishment of community-based Vet Centers, advances in understanding post-traumatic stress, and decades of work to secure care for veterans exposed to Agent Orange.
And my generation was among those who benefited from their work.
When I returned from Iraq, I benefited from a country that had learned to separate the war from the warrior. That change didn't happen by accident. Vietnam veterans helped make it possible.
These were Americans who had every reason to feel let down by their country. They knew what it felt like to return home and find that the people you'd served didn't always understand what you'd been through. But rather than let that disappointment define them, so many devoted themselves to making sure the next generation wouldn't have to endure the same experience.
They could have turned away. Instead, they helped build something better for the rest of us. I don't know that I could ever thank them enough.
I think of the military spouses who kept their families going through long deployments, the caregivers who sat beside a loved one through the hardest days of recovery, and the teachers who believed in a young person before that young person believed in themselves. So much of the good in this world comes from people who may never know just how much they've meant to someone else.
Approximately 390 Vietnam veterans pass away every day. Last week, we lost one of them, and one of my personal heroes, Richie Gresko. A U.S. Marine, Richie literally jumped on a grenade in Vietnam to save the lives of his brothers. He barely survived, and his decades-long road to recovery began at a veterans hospital in Philadelphia. He was put in by his commander for the Medal of Honor, but the paperwork was lost and it took six years for him to be awarded the Navy Cross - the second-highest military decoration recognizing extraordinary heroism in combat. Richie and I used to work out together at our local Crunch gym, where I'd bust his chops about how paratroopers could lift more than Marines. Never mind that I was about 20 years younger than him! He'd get a big belly laugh out of that. I've worked my ass off to upgrade Richie's Medal of Honor packet when in Congress, the Pentagon, and even still today. He's now up in heaven with his wife, but we'll be honoring him this Sunday night and laying him to rest this Monday. But the fight for Richie's upgrade will not end with his death. If you know a Vietnam Vet, please proactively reach out and say "Welcome home brother" or "Welcome home sister!" You can read Richie's obituary [here.](https://substack.com/redirect/0d3a163a-1e69-4303-8376-13d8ad4a5308?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
# What We Carry Forward
As a father, I think a lot about the kind of country we leave to our children. Like every parent, I want my kids to grow up in an America where they feel safe, loved, and free to follow their dreams. But I also want them to understand how much they have to be thankful for, how important it is to share our blessings with others, and also to live life with an attitude of gratitude. Each of our children will inherit the example we set in how we treat one another - so now that political season is over, please do what you can to unify our deeply divided nation through example, not just words.
I hope our kids grow up loving this country as much as I do, understanding that America has never been perfect and we never will be, but our duty laid out in our US Constitution is to make it a 'More Perfect Union.' We've made mistakes, and we have work to do. But what makes me proud to be an American is how many people care enough to keep trying to make life better for the next generation. That's the kind of patriotism I want my children to know and live their life by no matter what their profession may be.
And this Thanksgiving, I hope we take a moment to appreciate the Americans who are spending the holiday caring for others. The volunteers preparing meals for families in need. The nurses and first responders working through dinner away from their family. And especially our 174K service members who are spending another Thanksgiving overseas far from the people they love. I know what it's like to be away from home during the holidays, it's not easy, and I hope they know how grateful we are for them.
If there's one thing I hope my children carry with them, it's that the best way to show your love for this country is to love the people who call it home. Be kind to your neighbors. Help someone who needs it. And never take for granted the people who help make your life a little better.
That's the America I love. And it's the America I hope we leave to our children.
## **Thanksgiving at Home**
This Thanksgiving, I'm especially looking forward to spending time with my family. Genine and I spend much of the year traveling, working, and pursuing causes we care deeply about, and as much as we love the work we do, nothing makes us happier than having our kids home, sitting around the table together, catching up, sharing stories, and laughing about things that probably aren't nearly as funny to anyone outside our family. Those are the moments I treasure most, and I wish we could have more of them.
I also know that Thanksgiving isn't an easy holiday for everyone. Some families are celebrating new chapters, while others are experiencing loss, or may have an empty place at the table because someone they love is serving overseas or working to keep their community safe.
One thing I've learned over the years is that a little bit of kindness goes a long way, especially during the holidays. So if you have the chance this Thanksgiving, call an old friend even if it's been a minute. Check in on someone who might be spending the day alone. Tell someone how much they've meant to you. You never know how much they might need to hear it.
From our family to yours, Genine and I wish you a Happy Thanksgiving! May your holiday be filled with love, laughter, and the company of those who matter most.

He barely survived, and his decades-long road to recovery began at a veterans hospital in Philadelphia. He was put in by his commander for the Medal of Honor, but the paperwork was lost and it took six years for him to be awarded the Navy Cross - the second-highest military decoration recognizing extraordinary heroism in combat. Richie and I used to work out together at our local Crunch gym, where I'd bust his chops about how paratroopers could lift more than Marines. Never mind that I was about 20 years younger than him! He'd get a big belly laugh out of that. I've worked my ass off to upgrade Richie's Medal of Honor packet when in Congress, the Pentagon, and even still today. He's now up in heaven with his wife, but we'll be honoring him this Sunday night and laying him to rest this Monday. But the fight for Richie's upgrade will not end with his death. If you know a Vietnam Vet, please proactively reach out and say "Welcome home brother" or "Welcome home sister!" You can read Richie's obituary What We Carry Forward As a father, I think a lot about the kind of country we leave to our children. Like every parent, I want my kids to grow up in an America where they feel safe, loved, and free to follow their dreams. But I also want them to understand how much they have to be thankful for, how important it is to share our blessings with others, and also to live life with an attitude of gratitude. Each of our children will inherit the example we set in how we treat one another - so now that political season is over, please do what you can to unify our deeply divided nation through example, not just words. I hope our kids grow up loving this country as much as I do, understanding that America has never been perfect and we never will be, but our duty laid out in our US Constitution is to make it a 'More Perfect Union.' We've made mistakes, and we have work to do. But what makes me proud to be an American is how many people care enough to keep trying to make life better for the next generation. That's the kind of patriotism I want my children to know and live their life by no matter what their profession may be. And this Thanksgiving, I hope we take a moment to appreciate the Americans who are spending the holiday caring for others. The volunteers preparing meals for families in need. The nurses and first responders working through dinner away from their family. And especially our 174K service members who are spending another Thanksgiving overseas far from the people they love. I know what it's like to be away from home during the holidays, it's not easy, and I hope they know how grateful we are for them. If there's one thing I hope my children carry with them, it's that the best way to show your love for this country is to love the people who call it home. Be kind to your neighbors. Help someone who needs it. And never take for granted the people who help make your life a little better. That's the America I love. And it's the America I hope we leave to our children. Thanksgiving at Home** This Thanksgiving, I'm especially looking forward to spending time with my family. Genine and I spend much of the year traveling, working, and pursuing causes we care deeply about, and as much as we love the work we do, nothing makes us happier than having our kids home, sitting around the table together, catching up, sharing stories, and laughing about things that probably aren't nearly as funny to anyone outside our family. Those are the moments I treasure most, and I wish we could have more of them. I also know that Thanksgiving isn't an easy holiday for everyone. Some families are celebrating new chapters, while others are experiencing loss, or may have an empty place at the table because someone they love is serving overseas or working to keep their community safe. One thing I've learned over the years is that a little bit of kindness goes a long way, especially during the holidays. So if you have the chance this Thanksgiving, call an old friend even if it's been a minute. Check in on someone who might be spending the day alone. Tell someone how much they've meant to you. You never know how much they might need to hear it. From our family to yours, Genine and I wish you a Happy Thanksgiving! May your holiday be filled with love, laughter, and the company of those who matter most. | | ---|---|--- If you enjoy my writing and believe in the work I do advocating for our veterans and military families, I'd be grateful if you'd consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. Friend --
From the day he took office, Mark Kelly has done three things that set him apart from every other member of the United States Senate.
First, Mark publishes a public schedule of his meetings in the Senate.
Second, he refuses to take money from corporate PACs.
And third, he has all of his financial assets in blind trusts so Arizonans know he can’t trade stocks using the privileged information he gets as a senator.
We call this the Mark Kelly Standard of Government. And we believe the country would be in significantly better shape if every Senator and Member of Congress committed to these same standards.

| | | Dear Friend, The election results are in. A new majority has taken the House and Senate, and with it comes an emboldened coalition that has made no secret of its aims: the socialist-Islamist alliance now preparing to set the agenda in Washington.

Its implications are plain. Higher taxes. Expanded regulation. Hostility to the free market and to free speech. A foreign policy that treats allies with suspicion and adversaries with indulgence. And an open determination to reshape American institutions along lines that would have been unrecognizable to the founders--or to any Congress of living memory.

The question is no longer theoretical. Who will report the facts without fear? Who will examine the voting records, the alliances, the funding streams, and the policy consequences? Who will hold the new radicals and their un-American ideas to account when the rest of the press prefers accommodation or silence?

**That work is the daily business of The New York Sun.

** For a penny a day, you can join the readers who insist on clear-eyed reporting and independent judgment at the moment it is most needed. The Sun has never been a party organ. It is a newspaper that measures proposals by their results, that treats radicalism as a subject for scrutiny rather than celebration, and that remains committed to the principles of free enterprise, limited government, and the defense of American values.

The new Congress will move quickly. The alliance that helped put it there will not pause. The time for accountability -- and to join the paper that will demand it -- is now.**
**

We overcame incredible odds earlier this month and defeated 7-term Congressman Scott Perry. Now, I am ready to take your voice to the halls of Congress. I have a goal to hear from 300 of my future constituents (like you!) before I head back to DC to be sworn in. Can you take my official 2027 Priorities Survey? Your response is confidential and will help shape my strategy to best serve you! 2027 Priorities Survey Question #1: What is the first thing you would like to see me address in Congress? | | The more of you I hear from, the better, so please share this with your neighbors! I look forward to reading your responses and figuring out how to best work on them as quickly as possible. Thank you so much for trusting me to be your advocate. Peter, This week, millions of Americans will gather with their loved ones in celebration. But for 23 families, there will be an empty chair this year that didn't need to be there. One of them is Master Sgt. Nicole Amor, one of the six soldiers killed in the drone attack on the Port of Shuaiba in Kuwait, in the earliest hours of a war that Congress never authorized.
---
|
---
New details about the attack that claimed Nicole’s life, along with 5 of her fellow soldiers, just emerged through a whistleblower complaint from Army Maj. Stephen Ramsbottom.
That report just made its way to the House and Senate Armed Services committees this week.
Ramsbottom’s complaint has some startling allegations that, as a combat aviator, make my blood run cold.
He supplies evidence alleging that CENTCOM had advance warning not only that the command center at Shuaiba Port was known to our adversaries, but that the precise building location and surrounding elements had been surveilled in advance by Iranian quadcopter drones, allegedly seen in this clip provided to CBS 60 Minutes, filmed the night before the deadly attack.
---
|
---
Worse?
He details reports that were provided to his commanders a week prior to the attack requesting counter-drone systems, citing intelligence showing that the specific building that was struck had already been identified by the Iranians as a target. A system that could not be procured or installed in time before this administration recklessly rushed us into war.
They also cited the lack of a mass casualty plan, and inadequate emergency medical supplies on site.
All of this was known well before the attack that claimed the lives of six servicemembers and injured dozens more.
---
|
---
All killed in a predictable retaliatory attack, on a building allegedly known to be a target, in response to a war that WE started.
A war, it bears repeating, that Congress still has never authorized.
Nicole’s husband Joey has been left to pick up the pieces with their 18 year old son and 10 year old daughter, now facing the holidays without their mom. When he spoke to 60 Minutes last week, he did not mince words.
“The command of the 103rd has handled this so poorly,” he said in his interview. “They killed my wife. They killed these soldiers.”
The report from 60 Minutes also featured new images and video not previously seen from the attack, and the scenes are chilling.
---
|
---
This week, as my family gathers, we will say a prayer for MSG Amor, MAJ Khork, SGT Coady, MAJ O’Brien, MSG Tietjens, and CW3 Marzan – along with rest of the 23 servicemembers killed and the 865 wounded in this senseless, stupid war of choice.
But prayers are not enough. We need accountability.
This is not on our military. This administration – along with all who excuse and enable it – bears the ultimate responsibility for an unauthorized conflict that puts our own troops in harm’s way.
Every Soldier, Sailor, Airman, Marine, and Coast Guardsman accepts that we may be called to make the ultimate sacrifice in service to our country. We swear that oath and we do it with pride, honor, and a commitment to service.
We owe a debt to our servicemembers not to take that oath lightly; to do everything in our power to limit risks to their lives and bring them home safely to their families.
To not put them needlessly in harm’s way or to disregard threats to their safety.
By all accounts, that is not what happened here.
These families deserve answers, but Keith Self – who has himself commanded troops in combat – is not pursuing those answers.
That is a shocking abdication of duty and it must be rectified. I have faith that the incoming Democratic majority will pursue the truth of what happened at Port of Shuaiba on March 1st, 2026, and hold Hegseth accountable.
And when we flip this seat in 2028, I will continue that work to stop needless wars of choice and ensure we are honoring our promises to all who serve.
[The 2028 race has already begun. He details reports that were provided to his commanders a week prior to the attack requesting counter-drone systems, citing intelligence showing that the specific building that was struck had already been identified by the Iranians as a target. A system that could not be procured or installed in time before this administration recklessly rushed us into war. They also cited the lack of a mass casualty plan, and inadequate emergency medical supplies on site. All of this was known well before the attack that claimed the lives of six servicemembers and injured dozens more. | All killed in a predictable retaliatory attack, on a building allegedly known to be a target, in response to a war that WE started. A war, it bears repeating, that Congress still has never authorized. Nicole’s husband Joey has been left to pick up the pieces with their 18 year old son and 10 year old daughter, now facing the holidays without their mom. When he spoke to 60 Minutes last week, he did not mince words. “The command of the 103rd has handled this so poorly,” he said in his interview. “They killed my wife. They killed these soldiers.” The report from 60 Minutes also featured new images and video not previously seen from the attack, and the scenes are chilling. | This week, as my family gathers, we will say a prayer for MSG Amor, MAJ Khork, SGT Coady, MAJ O’Brien, MSG Tietjens, and CW3 Marzan – along with rest of the 23 servicemembers killed and the 865 wounded in this senseless, stupid war of choice. But prayers are not enough. We need accountability. This is not on our military. This administration – along with all who excuse and enable it – bears the ultimate responsibility for an unauthorized conflict that puts our own troops in harm’s way. Every Soldier, Sailor, Airman, Marine, and Coast Guardsman accepts that we may be called to make the ultimate sacrifice in service to our country. We swear that oath and we do it with pride, honor, and a commitment to service. We owe a debt to our servicemembers not to take that oath lightly; to do everything in our power to limit risks to their lives and bring them home safely to their families. To not put them needlessly in harm’s way or to disregard threats to their safety. By all accounts, that is not what happened here. These families deserve answers, but Keith Self – who has himself commanded troops in combat – is not pursuing those answers. That is a shocking abdication of duty and it must be rectified. I have faith that the incoming Democratic majority will pursue the truth of what happened at Port of Shuaiba on March 1st, 2026, and hold Hegseth accountable. And when we flip this seat in 2028, I will continue that work to stop needless wars of choice and ensure we are honoring our promises to all who serve. Peter, November is a month for good news! Here’s some more: **Last week, the House unanimously passed my bipartisan legislation to help small businesses grow and succeed.** Small businesses are the backbone of our local economies and our communities — my district, MN-03, has over 17,000 small businesses! Unfortunately right now, too many are struggling with rising costs, market uncertainties, and challenges accessing funding. My bill would help make sure a federal program that connects small businesses with private financing is working as effectively as possible. It would require more frequent and detailed reporting so we can better track where funding is going, identify any problems, and make sure the program is delivering results. When we think about getting things done in Congress, we often think big — and we should! There is so much big, important work to be done. But not every meaningful accomplishment makes headlines. Sometimes, it's the smaller, behind-the-scenes work of making government function better for the people we serve that makes a difference in people’s lives. I’m proud to have worked across the aisle to get this legislation through the House with unanimous support, and I’ll keep working to find common ground wherever possible and, above all, deliver results for Minnesotans. I’ll keep you updated along the way!With gratitude and resolve,
Kelly

| | | As ballots were still being counted in races across the country, new member orientation got underway in Washington! It was incredibly inspiring to meet my future colleagues for the first time and begin working together.
---
The 120th Congress is full of motivation and is hungry to get to work! Orientation included training sessions, along with traditions such as a class photo on the Capitol steps and the office lottery. We cannot wait to host Granite Staters in our new office!
Another highlight for me was the chance to meet Peaches, a beloved operator of the U.S. Capitol Subway System. Her energy and enthusiasm are contagious!

| | This experience and that chance to learn all that we need to know to hit the ground running on January 3rd is one that I will never forget.

As New Hampshire families prepare to gather for Thanksgiving and the holiday season arrives, I feel the weight of responsibility that lies ahead and the trust placed in the 120th Congress to deliver. Our team will be ready to get to work.
Thank you for EVERYTHING!

---
Derek, **2027 DNC Member Cards are almost here! But before we start printing and mailing them (you can reserve yours[**here**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-membercard.1omOxh&refcode=em_20261124_10368_fr&amount=7&t=5&akid=10368%2E22930333%2EYiFag6)), we want to make sure we have _your_ input on which design you like the best.** Whether you’ve chipped in this year, volunteered your time and energy to help elect Democrats, or just been keeping up to date with the DNC’s work to elect Democrats up and down the ballot, _we’re grateful to have you on our team_. Our 2027 DNC Member Cards will be an important reminder of your integral role on our grassroots team, and of the work we have ahead of us in the upcoming two years. With the 2026 midterms in the rearview, we’re beginning to look ahead. **First order of business: Choosing a design for our 2027 Member Cards.** [**This is what we have on file for you right now, can you confirm that it’s accurate?**](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/2027-member-card-design-voter-em/?refcode=em_20261124_10368_fr&t=6&akid=10368%2E22930333%2EYiFag6) **_2027 DNC Member Card Voting Record**_ **NAME:** Derek Willis
**2027 MEMBER CARD VOTER:** NO, NOT YET ❌
**SUGGESTED ACTION:** VOTE ON YOUR FAVORITE DESIGN **[VOTE NOW](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/2027-member-card-design-voter-em/?refcode=em_20261124_10368_fr&t=9&akid=10368%2E22930333%2EYiFag6)** None of the major victories that Democrats won this year — from Democrats flipping the House and Senate to winning down-ballot races across the country — would’ve been possible without the help of our generous grassroots supporters. We’re so excited to share these Member Cards with you as a reminder that we can win _big_ when we all stand together. [**Please take a few seconds to share your thoughts on which design you’d like to see on your Member Card today >>](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/2027-member-card-design-voter-em/?refcode=em_20261124_10368_fr&t=11&akid=10368%2E22930333%2EYiFag6)** **[VOTE NOW](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/2027-member-card-design-voter-em/?refcode=em_20261124_10368_fr&t=14&akid=10368%2E22930333%2EYiFag6)** Thank you, The Democrats

# [The truth comes out: Behind Microsoft's Code Red after worst email outage ever](https://substack.com/redirect/3363f3f3-a352-45bd-a9c8-319df0bd08ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Microsoft **[issued a code red](https://substack.com/redirect/0d961242-7164-4677-a55b-f73dc8f7f123?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after a Nov. 12-13 outage knocked out Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, targeting worldwide fixes within an hour amid a record flood of software flaws.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3363f3f3-a352-45bd-a9c8-319df0bd08ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Outage root cause:** A flaw introduced in July went unnoticed for about four months; Microsoft ruled out hackers and AI agents.
* **Response scale:** Teams exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 chats while needed data sat scattered; one executive said the component had roughly ten years of acceptable failures.
* **Uptime calculation:** The 99.9% Microsoft 365 promise allows about 44 minutes of monthly downtime; one 24-hour outage used nearly three years' worth by Yahoo calculations.
* **Patch flood context:** Nearly 17,500 new flaws were reported in October; Ben Emons warned every patch is a chance for something to break.

# [Huang tells staff: No succession plan needed. Ever.](https://substack.com/redirect/3363f3f3-a352-45bd-a9c8-319df0bd08ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to employees Tuesday at **[his first all-hands since returning,](https://substack.com/redirect/15f08dad-6195-407a-b7b7-df82b7d4bd48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** saying he hurt them and promising a better second chance while rejecting any need for succession planning.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3363f3f3-a352-45bd-a9c8-319df0bd08ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Meeting apology tone:** Huang called the gathering the second-hardest of his life after speaking with his wife and disclosed he is in therapy.
* **Succession view:** He argued Nvidia's unique model with multiple capable leaders across units makes a formal plan unnecessary and hierarchy-creating.
* **Resignation context:** Huang stepped down Nov. 12 after affairs that included one with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a Beijing spy.
* **Return details:** The board reinstated him Monday after federal input; President Trump backed the deal.

* **Saved post habit:** About 20% of daily Instagram users save at least one post a day, many of them shoppable items or ads.

Family and friends have contributed **[more than $1 billion to Trump Accounts](https://substack.com/redirect/22af28a5-87f1-4a8c-a3d5-4752cb084118?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from over 3 million individuals since the July 4 launch, bringing total deposits above $9 billion.

* **Philanthropy note:** Temporary rules now allow stock donations, letting some donors avoid capital-gains taxes on appreciated shares.

An Amazon Prime Air drone landed on a Huntington Woods, Michigan, garage Friday **[after striking a fiber cable](https://substack.com/redirect/80a2e607-2c84-4dea-b6fe-f55c0b5df0f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and becoming entangled in power lines during takeoff.

---|---|---

* **NTSB status:** The board is collecting preliminary details before deciding whether to open its own inquiry.
* **Amazon statement:** Spokesperson Jack Stelzner said there were no injuries, the drone has been removed, and the company is in contact with the resident.
* **Operations continue:** Detroit-area Prime Air flights continued after the incident; Amazon said safety remains the top priority and such events are rare.

Nearly 17,500 new flaws were reported in October | | | Nov 24| | | ∙| | Guest post ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | Microsoft after a Nov. 12-13 outage knocked out Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, targeting worldwide fixes within an hour amid a record flood of software flaws. | | ---|---|--- Outage root cause: A flaw introduced in July went unnoticed for about four months; Microsoft ruled out hackers and AI agents. Response scale: Teams exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 chats while needed data sat scattered; one executive said the component had roughly ten years of acceptable failures. Uptime calculation: The 99.9% Microsoft 365 promise allows about 44 minutes of monthly downtime; one 24-hour outage used nearly three years' worth by Yahoo calculations. Patch flood context: Nearly 17,500 new flaws were reported in October; Ben Emons warned every patch is a chance for something to break. | | ---|---|--- Use Clear Street's built-in AI, Omni, to understand a stock, a sector, the market, or your portfolio. Get all the context you need without spending time searching through everything yourself. Disclosure: The Capitalist is a paid partner of Clear Street LLC. Omni is a research tool, not investment advice. Any orders require your confirmation. | | | | ---|---|--- | 5:51 PM | Reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to employees Tuesday at saying he hurt them and promising a better second chance while rejecting any need for succession planning. | | ---|---|--- Meeting apology tone: Huang called the gathering the second-hardest of his life after speaking with his wife and disclosed he is in therapy. Succession view: He argued Nvidia's unique model with multiple capable leaders across units makes a formal plan unnecessary and hierarchy-creating. Resignation context: Huang stepped down Nov. 12 after affairs that included one with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a Beijing spy. Return details: The board reinstated him Monday after federal input; President Trump backed the deal. Meta's ad-free Muse agent is by helping users organize saved posts, with 25% of Muse users shopping and average purchases above $200. | | ---|---|--- Saved post habit: About 20% of daily Instagram users save at least one post a day, many of them shoppable items or ads. Conversion lift: A senior executive said Muse raises advertiser conversions by cutting shopping friction even without its own ads. Shopping share: In the week ending Nov. 22, Muse handled 51% of all agentic orders measured by Forter Intelligence. Revenue plan: Zuckerberg said the company plans a small fee on transactions made through the agent. CoreWeave bonds Tuesday amid renewed AI-trade concerns, wiping out Monday gains that followed Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang. | | ---|---|--- 2031 note drop: The 9% bond due 2031 fell as much as 3.6 points to 76.6 cents, lowest since its July 2025 issuance. 2032 note drop: The 9.625% note due 2032 declined 4.6 points to 74.9 cents, lowest since June 2026. Additional lows: The 9.75% 2031 note hit 76.3 cents and the 9.25% 2030 note reached 80.9 cents, both records since issuance. Trade context: The moves ranked among the day's biggest corporate-bond losses and erased the prior session's Nvidia-driven rally. Kalshi's on Thursday and Friday for the first consecutive days, highlighting expansion beyond event contracts. | | ---|---|--- Thursday volumes: Perps notional volume reached $3.4 billion versus about $3 billion for prediction markets, coinciding with Anthropic's stock debut. Product growth: Kalshi first launched U.S. perps after May regulatory approval for crypto and has since added metals, oil, indexes, and stocks. Offshore scale: Offshore perps generated more than $90 trillion in notional volume in 2025; Kalshi's chief risk officer called the business early innings. Structure difference: Perps volume includes leverage while event contracts remain fully collateralized. Family and friends have contributed from over 3 million individuals since the July 4 launch, bringing total deposits above $9 billion. | | ---|---|--- Treasury statement: Scott Bessent said the contributions reflect the finest instincts of the national character; Frank Bisignano called the program the largest government start-up in history. Account rules: Any U.S. child under 18 with a Social Security number can hold an account; annual after-tax contributions are capped at $5,000 until the year before age 18. Seed and gifts: Children born 2025-2028 receive a $1,000 Treasury deposit; additional philanthropic pledges include stock gifts and targeted grants. Philanthropy note: Temporary rules now allow stock donations, letting some donors avoid capital-gains taxes on appreciated shares. The Pentagon is in preliminary talks with General Motors, Ford, and other manufacturers for mass-produced military drones. | | ---|---|--- Deal status: No agreements are finalized; executives have raised questions about profit margins and the business case for weapons-supply work. Project Agincourt: A Sept. 30 memorandum by War Secretary Pete Hegseth established the effort to build a four-star Autonomous Warfare Command. Leadership named: Owen West is CEO and U.S. Navy SEAL Senior Chief Max Strasiser is COO of the initiative. Prior cooperation: Lockheed and GM Defense previously delivered Patriot missile housing components in 22 days after an August agreement. An Amazon Prime Air drone landed on a Huntington Woods, Michigan, garage Friday and becoming entangled in power lines during takeoff. | | ---|---|--- FAA probe: The agency confirmed it is investigating the incident and reviews such reports for possible corrective or enforcement action. NTSB status: The board is collecting preliminary details before deciding whether to open its own inquiry. Amazon statement: Spokesperson Jack Stelzner said there were no injuries, the drone has been removed, and the company is in contact with the resident. Operations continue: Detroit-area Prime Air flights continued after the incident; Amazon said safety remains the top priority and such events are rare. The last few weeks have been a whirlwind. First, I want to say that I'm incredibly grateful for the way Californians showed up in this year's midterms. You turned out in historic numbers and delivered a decisive rebuke of Donald Trump’s attacks on our democracy. And since Election Day, my team has been right back at work — so before you sign off for the Thanksgiving holiday, I want to share an inside look at what my office has been up to. We've been taking action:
* We sued OpenAI for failing to keep its models secure and putting public safety at risk.
* We sued to block this administration’s efforts to strip housing support from mixed-status immigrant households.
* We filed an amicus brief urging the Ninth Circuit to uphold an order requiring humane conditions at the Adelanto ICE detention center.
* We sued to block a $3.5 billion veterinary supply merger between Covetrus and MWI Animal Health, which threatens to squeeze veterinary clinics and leave pet owners footing the bill.

And we've been winning:
* Just yesterday, we secured a major victory in our multistate lawsuit to protect federal funding for permanent supportive housing. The court struck down the Trump administration’s unlawful attempt to redirect funding that helps keep thousands of our most vulnerable neighbors off the streets.
* We secured a final court order permanently striking down Shasta County's Measure B, which would have undermined voting rights and upended the county's elections system.
* And after defeating the Trump administration at the Supreme Court, it finally abandoned its latest unlawful effort to interfere with California's elections and disenfranchise eligible voters.

This is what the work looks like, day in and day out: Fighting to stop the unlawful power grabs from the federal government. Defending our immigrant communities. Protecting reproductive freedom, safeguarding our environment, holding greedy corporations accountable. _And standing up to abuse of power wherever and whenever it appears. _ **[Fighting isn’t always easy, but the last two years have proven that we’re at our strongest when we stand together. If you support this work and want to keep fighting with me, will you let me know? Add your name to show you’re with me.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144001930/662088938/-248911487?refcode=261124em_rb_roundup&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyODRhY2MyZi01MWU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=fAA1P2xtDvuuVlwCG_Oho6rnUEthIKfOc9ewOCPcICo=&emci=154acc2f-51e8-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=284acc2f-51e8-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=33430436)**

Justice Samuel Alito
recently stood up at a black-tie dinner for a right-wing think tank and
defended the Supreme Court’s “independence.”

The message underneath wasn’t subtle: reforming the Court would put that
independence at risk. It’s absurd.

An independent Court is supposed to rule without fear or favor. When Alito
says “independence,” he means a Court free from accountability.

That’s why he’s sounding the alarm. Adding seats would break the
ultra-conservative supermajority he’s part of and end its grip on our
rights.

Reform isn’t a threat to the Court. Alito is. Here’s what he and his
supermajority have given us:

* Our rights rolled back. Roe v. Wade is gone. The Voting Rights Act has
been gutted.
* A Court that operates with zero transparency, and no binding ethics
code to keep the justices in check.
* Ruling after ruling for corporations and their billionaire
bankrollers.
* Trump abusing the shadow docket to rush through his authoritarian
agenda, with the Court’s blessing.

The Court’s independence isn’t in danger. Ours is.

As long as the conservative supermajority holds, these rulings won’t stop.
Expanding the Court is how we break it, break Trump’s stranglehold on the
bench, and give the Court back to the people.

Congress can expand the Court, but lawmakers won’t act without pressure.
Demand Justice PAC is building that pressure, making the case for
expansion and holding the Court accountable every time it rules against
the people.

name: Mark Teixeira
subject: Three weeks of gratitude 🇺🇸
body:
A quick look back, and a big thank you.

| | | | | |
---
| | Peter, It’s been three weeks since you elected me to serve Texas’ 21st District, and I’m still overwhelmed with gratitude. I’m humbled by your trust, and ready to roll up my sleeves and get to work. We had a very busy, productive orientation in Washington with my fellow incoming members of Congress, including several from Texas. I learned a lot about congressional procedure, found my way around the Capitol halls, and had some fun picking a new office. Check out all the updates below!| [](https://us.list-manage.com/FGCpnBr4QPu?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)| **Election night** This victory belongs to you, and nobody will work harder to keep earning your trust.[**See more »**](https://us.list-manage.com/mxksrzuRv8q?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)
---|---
[](https://us.list-manage.com/VxA2UMOxvrg?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)| **Veterans Day** I’m so proud of my dad’s service in the Navy, and grateful to every veteran and military family.[**See more »**](https://us.list-manage.com/olJwxQr9Z7W?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)
---|---
[](https://us.list-manage.com/18eoINaNa_g?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)| **New Member Orientation** Learning my way around the halls and tunnels of the Capitol, and running into a giant of Texas history.[**Watch »**](https://us.list-manage.com/Dw06tXwcgwJ?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)
---|---
[](https://us.list-manage.com/19cEJzb1sEV?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)| **Baseball can wait** Folks keep asking if I’ll play in the Congressional Baseball Game. You sent me to Washington to work for you, and that’s where my focus is.[**Watch »**](https://us.list-manage.com/evE8TzMN_kI?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)
---|---
[](https://us.list-manage.com/kpC8CUusjeY?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)
---
**LAST PICK****105 out of 105.** I drew the very last number in the House office lottery. I consider it an honor to let my fellow freshmen go ahead of me. As Matthew 19:30 reminds us, “But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”**The happy ending:** I lucked out and got a great office. My team and I are proud of it and can’t wait to welcome you there starting January 3rd.[**Watch the video ▶**](https://us.list-manage.com/4MXbK9GxpXS?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)****[**See more »**](https://us.list-manage.com/gGxgY_MyaCZ?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)
**Counting our blessings**
I’ve always been an optimist, so I see the glass half full, and this year I’m especially filled with gratitude. I’m grateful to God for so many blessings: my faith; Leigh and our three kids; the troops, law enforcement officers, and first responders serving today so the rest of us can be home with our families; and every volunteer and neighbor across TX-21 who knocked on doors, hosted events, and prayed for us.
[](https://us.list-manage.com/14RAR_Y0mHk?e=2814cf23ed&c2id=545d45db23489864f66a83d0befb5592)
_Thank you, Team Tex!_
Thanksgiving is a uniquely American holiday. In his first Thanksgiving Proclamation, George Washington asked the nation to acknowledge:
| _“With grateful hearts the many signal favors of Almighty God.”_**GEORGE WASHINGTON, 1789**
---|---
That’s still true today. We’re truly blessed to live in the greatest country on earth, and I’m hopeful that America’s best days remain ahead.
From our family to yours, I pray you have a wonderful Thanksgiving. Enjoy the time with family, good food, and football!
God bless Texas, and God bless America.
_Mark “Tex” Teixeira_
21st Congressional District of Texas

name: George Whitesides
subject: My CNN interview on AI
body:
|
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144002268/662090200/954579451?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMzUyN2I3MS01MmU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=V0pVtzG5UPL5zQw-YakgiaIqtDkyy-DrA484iTmsVsQ=)
Does it feel like there’s a new tech or AI crisis every day, Peter? I hear it constantly, and the headlines are raising real concerns about our digital safety and security. So I wanted you to hear this from me: a few days ago, I joined Congressman Don Beyer, Congressman Nathaniel Moran, and more than 20 of our colleagues to launch the **bipartisan AI Safety and Innovation Caucus.** Our goal is simple: bring Democrats and Republicans together to pass meaningful AI safety legislation, confront emerging threats, and strengthen national security while keeping America at the front of innovation. When I sat down with CNN recently to talk about AI, they asked me a question I keep coming back to: what can Congress _actually_ do to make this technology safer? Too often, the debate gets framed as a choice between doing nothing and banning AI outright. I don’t accept that. In aerospace, nobody launches until we know it’s safe, and that has never stopped America from leading. Here’s where I think we start:
* **Protecting our kids.** I have a bill to understand how AI is being used in classrooms, because kids’ digital health has to be a priority.
* **Protecting workers.** A lot of people are worried about what AI means for their jobs. Congress should be planning for that now, not after the damage is done.

Hey folks,
This one has me absolutely furious.
Reporting from ProPublica and MS NOW raises serious questions about what's happening inside Donald Trump's Justice Department under Attorney General Todd Blanche. We're talking about extraordinary taxpayer-funded settlements involving Trump associates, investigations into alleged pollution being shut down, and families in West Virginia who say they can't even drink or bathe in their own water.
And the more I dig into these stories, the more concerned I get about what we _haven 't_ uncovered yet.
Here's what we get into:
* [**00:00:34**] A reported $500,000 payout to a Trump-connected golf professional raises questions about how the Justice Department is handling taxpayer-funded settlements.
* [**00:03:17**] Legal experts question the unusual settlement process, and I explain why I'm concerned it could open the door to more payouts.
* [**00:07:19**] We revisit Trump's controversial proposed DOJ compensation fund for people claiming government mistreatment, including January 6 defendants and other allies.
* [**00:11:47**] Reporting alleges that Todd Blanche's office ordered prosecutors to shut down an investigation involving a coal company tied to Senator Jim Justice's family.
* [**00:15:28**] West Virginia residents describe contaminated water, bringing us back to the fundamental question: Who is our government actually protecting?

Here's what I keep coming back to: **Government is supposed to work for ordinary people.** It's supposed to protect your drinking water, keep your family safe, enforce the law fairly, and make sure your tax dollars aren't being abused.
Instead, these reports raise deeply troubling questions about whether political connections are influencing who gets paid, who gets investigated, and who gets left behind.
And that should concern every American, regardless of who they voted for.
We need transparency. We need serious congressional oversight. And we need meaningful ethics and campaign finance reform so the public can trust that nobody is above the law.
That's why I'm going to keep digging into these stories and demanding answers. If you value independent media that follows the money and holds powerful people accountable, help me keep this work going.

Democrats win when we center the people. That means fighting for bold
policies that go as broad and deep as the hurt our communities are facing,
and refusing to moderate our aspirations.

Our Squad is living proof, and the powerful know it.

Whenever Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida take on corporations, the
dark money shows up. Outside forces line up to take them down, and the
op-eds arrive right on schedule calling for someone more reasonable —
meaning someone quieter, someone who takes the lobbyist meeting.

from longtime supporters and first-time donors who refuse to sit by while
our rights are on the line. That’s why the Squad can’t be bought. It’s
also why they’re in Congress right now, fighting unapologetically for
working people.

Now Democrats have the majority, and we need to use it to deliver the
progressive change our communities have been demanding. Our Squad will be

Peter, There’s been a ton of attention on the unprecedented Democratic flips in Ohio, Texas, and Georgia. But I want to take a moment to talk about Wisconsin, because voters in the Badger State also voted for transformational change this election: “For the first time in 17 years, Wisconsin Democrats will have complete control over state government in 2027 and with it the ability to modify or undo many of the election laws that Republicans spent years passing.”— _Wisconsin Watch_ This is personal for me as someone born and raised in Wisconsin. In fact, I spent three weeks sleeping on the cold marble floor of the Wisconsin State Capitol building in 2011 — alongside 100,000 other concerned citizens protesting Governor Scott Walker’s administration’s power grab. Walker and his extreme allies in the state legislature changed the rules of the state supreme court to undermine the state’s longstanding chief justice, gutted the state’s nonpartisan elections board, and enacted a horrifying gerrymander, which guaranteed them an unearned lock on power for a decade. The NDRC was founded in the wake of that setback to fight back against anti-democracy power grabs exactly like that. Today, we’re celebrating electing Democracy Defender David Crowley to the governor’s office and flipping both chambers of the legislature — giving Democrats a trifecta in state government. Those landmark victories mean Wisconsin legislators can vote for fair maps, voting rights, and other pro-democracy priorities. You helped make that happen. Now, our movement can't let this incredible moment pass. Winning is wonderful — it’s what you do with those victories that matters more. clean_body: These victories are critical. Now it’s a question of what we do with them. | Peter, There’s been a ton of attention on the unprecedented Democratic flips in Ohio, Texas, and Georgia. But I want to take a moment to talk about Wisconsin, because voters in the Badger State also voted for transformational change this election: “For the first time in 17 years, Wisconsin Democrats will have complete control over state government in 2027 and with it the ability to modify or undo many of the election laws that Republicans spent years passing.”— Wisconsin Watch This is personal for me as someone born and raised in Wisconsin. In fact, I spent three weeks sleeping on the cold marble floor of the Wisconsin State Capitol building in 2011 — alongside 100,000 other concerned citizens protesting Governor Scott Walker’s administration’s power grab. Walker and his extreme allies in the state legislature changed the rules of the state supreme court to undermine the state’s longstanding chief justice, gutted the state’s nonpartisan elections board, and enacted a horrifying gerrymander, which guaranteed them an unearned lock on power for a decade. The NDRC was founded in the wake of that setback to fight back against anti-democracy power grabs exactly like that. Today, we’re celebrating electing Democracy Defender David Crowley to the governor’s office and flipping both chambers of the legislature — giving Democrats a trifecta in state government. Those landmark victories mean Wisconsin legislators can vote for fair maps, voting rights, and other pro-democracy priorities. You helped make that happen. Now, our movement can't let this incredible moment pass. name: Sarah McBride
subject: A simple but profound choice
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
It is very easy to destroy. It is a lot harder to build.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=4160%2E21716%2E9nts9r)
**In recent years, our politics have boiled down to a simple but profound choice between destroyers and builders.**
It is very easy to destroy. It is a lot harder to build. _But it is worth it._ And it is what our job is over the next few years in Washington.
We need to build a healthcare system where every patient can get the care they need. To build the housing of tomorrow that makes homeownership within reach.
We need to build a cradle through career support system with universal paid leave, affordable childcare, and strong public schools so that it’s actually affordable to start a family again.
And we need to build an economy of the future that guarantees that the new prosperity unleashed by new technologies is shared by the many, not just the wealthy few.
But to do any of that — to forge a new deal for this century and for our country — we also have to be builders of trust in ourselves and in one another.
**We have to be what scripture calls “repairers of the breach,”** so that we can restore the foundational faith that makes this American experiment, and democracy itself, even possible.
That faith that your neighbor can change so that your country can change. That faith that through peaceful conversation and basic compassion, through disagreement and debate, we can summon our better angels and build a brighter future.
That’s the work ahead of us. And I’m committed to doing my part every single day — but I’m counting on people like you to keep standing with me.
[**If you can, please consider pitching in $5 or any amount to fuel our grassroots movement and help me build the government we all deserve.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20261124-1.p-Gef8&refcode=em20261124-4160&amount=5&t=2&akid=4160%2E21716%2E9nts9r)

| | | I've been thinking a lot about road trips this week. When I was a kid, my family didn't take many vacations. When we did travel, we brought our own food, and my parents planned every stop. They made sure we had what we needed before we set out, because once you're on the highway, you can't turn back for what you forgot. **_That's how I've come to think about this fight._** For the last two years, the road has been long, and a lot of it has been downright hard. We watched the safety net that saved my family get gutted. We watched hate become a strategy. We watched a president turn the government against his critics and treat the White House like a family business. There were stretches where it was hard to see where we were going at all. Then came November... Kansas sent a Democrat to the Senate for the first time since 1932. Texas, Alaska, Arizona, and Florida delivered wins that almost nobody predicted. After a long stretch of hard road, it felt like pulling into an oasis. **This Thanksgiving, I'm grateful for that oasis, and I'm grateful for you. ** Every volunteer who knocked a door, every donor who chipped in, and everyone who read these emails and refused to give up made it possible.Election Day felt like a great oasis amidst the arduous journey of the Trump 2.0 era. That’s a phenomenal accomplishment, and I don’t want to understate it. However, we’d be lying to ourselves if we said the trip was finished.We can't stay at this oasis. We need to finish what we started. **This road trip ends in 2029, when we evict MAGA extremism out of the White House, elect a Democratic supermajority in Congress, and finally get to work passing laws that give working families a real shot. That means fair wages, lower costs, good schools in every zip code, and an economy where hard work still leads somewhere.** That's a long drive, and the most important part of a long drive happens before you leave: you restock, refuel, and make sure you have what you need for the road ahead. That's what this end-of-year push is about for Equal Opportunity Now. Every dollar we raise now is fuel in the tank for the races that will decide whether we finish this trip. **[Before you head into the holiday, help us fill the tank. Chip in $15 or $40 to Equal Opportunity Now, and let's hit the road running.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144003778/662094830/1090555623?refcode=261124_ngp_roadtrip&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNjExYzNiMS01OWU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=KKDhT8HW_wSrg7Ldv3t9aZd_mlpEm8_FBI7PUM3rBH4=)**

name: Alex Padilla
subject: Medicare for All
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Alex Padilla for Senate
body:
#

Friends,
**Healthcare is a human right and no American should go bankrupt just because they got sick.**
That’s why one of the first things I did when I got to Congress in 2021 was sign on as a co-sponsor of Senator Bernie Sanders’ _Medicare For All Act_. And I’ve been a proud supporter ever since.
It’s also why I’ve been supportive of steps along the path to universal healthcare, like Senator Andy Kim’s _MediKids_ bill to give ALL kids Medicare.
And it’s why I fought so hard against Trump and Republicans’ massive cuts to Medicaid funding.
But with new Democratic majorities in Congress, we have a chance to reverse the damage they’ve done and make real, positive changes to the healthcare system in this country. _We can’t waste it_.
**Congress can and _must_ act to make healthcare affordable and accessible for ALL Americans, regardless of zip code or tax bracket.**
In other developed nations around the world, ensuring healthcare is available to everyone is simply a given... because healthcare is a right, not a privilege. It's long past time for the United States to transition to a model of Medicare For All.
But there are plenty of powerful interests who are very invested in the status quo — and who are mobilizing right now to try to stop any push for universal healthcare. And it’s not just the Republicans in Congress. To do this, we are going to have to take on the health insurance companies and big pharma alongside the GOP.
So let’s do it.
Thank you, for joining the fight to pass Medicare for All and guarantee healthcare as a human right for ALL of us. More soon.
Sincerely,
Alex Padilla
U.S. Senator for California

* * *

_👋 Wait! While you’re here... 👋_
Right now, Alex is hard at work preparing for the next Congress and making sure that Democrats use their new majorities to improve the lives of Californians and working families across the country. _That includes guaranteeing healthcare for ALL Americans._
If you’d like to support that work, [**please make a contribution today to help him keep it up.**](https://act.alex-padilla.com/go/553?c0=padilla-em-nov26.IBznFA&refcode=em261124-1-270&t=1&akid=1951%2E159979%2EWV0IdS) Even $5 or $10 goes a long way when lots of people are chipping in.
_Thank you_. 🙏

Dear Friend,

I know that this time of year can be hard. With the price of groceries, utilities, and rent on the rise, budgets are getting stretched thin and many families are having to decide what they can do without this holiday season.

I’ve spent the better part of 30 years organizing to build a better world for my daughters and for everyone who calls our community home. But change doesn’t always come quickly enough to put food on the table.

**That’s why I’m inviting you to join me in contributing to one of our local food banks, so that everyone can enjoy this holiday season:**
* **_[Alameda County Community Food Bank](accfb.org/give?link_id=1&can_id=12471c8e444f80358077c9724aea85a0&source=email-test-email-2-31&email_referrer=email_3510888&email_subject=share-food-with-our-neighbors-this-holiday-season&&)_**
* **_[Berkeley Food Network](berkeleyfoodnetwork.org/get-involved/ways-to-give/donate/?link_id=2&can_id=12471c8e444f80358077c9724aea85a0&source=email-test-email-2-31&email_referrer=email_3510888&email_subject=share-food-with-our-neighbors-this-holiday-season&&)_**
* **_[Alameda Food Bank](alamedafoodbank.org/donate/?link_id=3&can_id=12471c8e444f80358077c9724aea85a0&source=email-test-email-2-31&email_referrer=email_3510888&email_subject=share-food-with-our-neighbors-this-holiday-season&&)_**
* **_[Davis Street Community Center](davisstreet.org/ways-to-support-davis-street/donate-to-davis-street/ ?link_id=4&can_id=12471c8e444f80358077c9724aea85a0&source=email-test-email-2-31&email_referrer=email_3510888&email_subject=share-food-with-our-neighbors-this-holiday-season&&)_**

Please consider donating to the local East Bay organizations above. **These organizations are lifelines in our communities – and their tireless efforts make sure no one in our community goes hungry this holiday season.**

I will continue to work towards rolling back this Administration’s cuts to SNAP and advance policies that help lower costs.

In the meantime, I hope you get to enjoy sharing time and food with your loved ones this holiday season.

And if you're able, I hope you will consider helping another family enjoy a nourishing and memorable holiday meal.

In solidarity,
Lateefah

body:
We must stop the epidemic of antisemitic violence and harassment.
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144004431/662096846/-1995338237?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&refcode=jtk5996-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiZDg2MmU4Mi01YmU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1eYVBFxxaeYaxsL4UIejwBtHvGaQqsFMuGu7YO32hb8=)

Friend,
I am the third Jewish woman and the first former synagogue President ever elected to the United States Senate. Think about that: In our nation’s 250-year history, there were only TWO Jewish women elected to the Senate before I joined.
Like any believer, my faith is deeply tied to who I am, what I fight for, and my role as a lawmaker. It’s part of why I care about the issues that I do, and it means that I bring with me the same struggles that all Jews face. Most prominently, the threat and impact of antisemitism.
**That's why I'm leading the charge in the Senate to combat the increasing levels of violence and harassment Jewish Americans are facing right now.**
[**_Will you please make a gift of $5 or more to support my work in Washington to fight the epidemic of antisemitism across our country?_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144004432/662096847/1388585385?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=jtk5996-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiZDg2MmU4Mi01YmU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1eYVBFxxaeYaxsL4UIejwBtHvGaQqsFMuGu7YO32hb8=)
| | [Donate $5](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144004433/662096848/-1995338237?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=jtk5996-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiZDg2MmU4Mi01YmU4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1eYVBFxxaeYaxsL4UIejwBtHvGaQqsFMuGu7YO32hb8=)
---
For me, this fight is personal. When I was just a few years old, I was playing in a hotel swimming pool with my mom while on vacation when a lifeguard on duty told her that we were “dirty” because we were Jewish – and that we had to leave the pool immediately because of it. My parents packed up our things and left that hotel. We never returned. My mom never forgot that interaction, retelling the story for years.

Nearly every Jewish American has a moment in their lives when they experience or witness antisemitism like that firsthand, and the problem is especially serious today.
Swastika graffiti. Physical assaults and threats. Firebombings. **Multiple** deadly mass shootings. These attacks on Jews are not isolated incidents. They represent a regression toward one of civilization’s darkest chapters.
All of it is wrong, and addressing this kind of violent antisemitism is an issue I’ve been working on since before I came to Congress and throughout my time in the House and Senate. **That is why:**
* I founded the Senate’s first-ever Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism, which now includes more than half the Senate as members.

* I introduced the _Jewish American Security Act –_ sweeping legislation to fight antisemitism on college campuses, at Jewish communal institutions, and online. The bill is supported by the American Jewish Committee, the ADL, and the Jewish Council for Public Affairs.

* I successfully pushed the Biden administration to create the first-ever National Strategy to Counter Antisemitism, which took a whole-of-government approach to tackling rising hate.

* I led the effort in Congress to increase the power of the State Department’s Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Antisemitism by raising the position to the rank of Ambassador.

* I introduced and successfully helped pass legislation reauthorizing the _Never Again Education Act_ to educate communities about the Holocaust.

* I successfully pressured the Trump administration to avoid weakening Coast Guard standards for hate symbols like swastikas.

When I think about this work, I think about being that little girl with her mom again. Every day, I'm trying to help make our country a place where nobody is targeted because of their faith or who they are – whether it’s at a swimming pool, on a college campus, or in the United States military.

It is the roads, the water, the public records, the school board meeting and the polling place down the street. **It is the part of government closest to home, and almost nobody argues with it, whatever their politics.** The general election just wrapped up, and across Alaska, local elections have been happening too. **Clerks helped make it all happen**. We just need more of them. Earlier this year, your support helped us sit down with a dozen local government clerks from across Alaska. Their stories became **[_Unsung Heroes_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144004505/662097096/1523912470?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzEwMjc1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZjdmMGY3NC01Y2U4LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=iTw0ZhmvBxvxEi60sch4Ht0dOc8nwFYMpc4cyverBCY=&emci=24be7718-23e8-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=cf7f0f74-5ce8-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=9512399)** , a short video about the people behind a job most Alaskans have never heard of. _**Thank you. God Bless. And Goodbye.**_ Patriot, I prayed that we would never reach this point. **But barring anything short of a miracle, we’re reaching the end of the line.** It’s Rep. Brandon Gill. First, I just want to tell you how grateful I am that you even opened this text. I know you get a lot of messages. So I appreciate you giving this one your time. **[But as I sit here running through our donor files over and over again, it breaks my heart to tell you this. His record speaks for itself:**
* **Family separation:** Miller defended the administration's "zero-tolerance" immigration policy, which resulted in thousands of children being separated from their parents.
* **The travel ban:** He helped engineer sweeping entry restrictions targeting predominantly Muslim countries.
* **Dismantling asylum:** Miller pushed policies to limit refugee admissions, restrict access to asylum, and make it harder for certain immigrants to obtain legal status.

# Another ground stop ordered at Chicago's O'Hare International Airport
A **[ground stop](https://substack.com/redirect/9faef0ea-890e-47d3-bf62-be889c3e74a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** was issued at Chicago's O'Hare International Airport Tuesday afternoon due to an equipment malfunction, lasting until 4:15 p.m. and affecting flights departing from Minneapolis, Milwaukee, Green Bay, and Des Moines.
